title: Stationary Handball Fundamentals
primarySkill: Basic stationary handball technique
objective: Develop a repeatable stationary handball action in which players correctly support the football, strike its lower rear section with a closed fist and direct it towards a controlled target.
groundSize: A flat 10-metre × 10-metre technical area, or one clearly marked station for every two to four players.
equipment: Flat markers or small target cones
Optional handball technique boards or rebound nets
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Simple organisation with minimal observation or intervention
setup:
Mark a safe technical area with adequate spacing between players.
Each player stands with a football and at least two metres of clear space around them.
Players face a cone, line marking, partner or stationary target positioned three to five metres away.
Begin without speed, competition or defensive pressure.
Right-handed players initially place their left foot slightly forward when handballing with the right fist; reverse the stance for the opposite hand.
The coach positions themselves where the support hand, striking fist and ball contact point can be clearly observed.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players begin in an athletic stance with knees slightly flexed, head up and the football supported in front of the body.
On the coach’s instruction, each player forms a compact striking fist with the thumb positioned outside the fingers.
Players place the football on the open supporting hand with the long axis directed towards the target.
The striking fist moves forward from behind the football and contacts its lower rear section.
The supporting hand remains open and stable while the striking arm follows through towards the target.
Players retrieve the football, reset their body position and repeat the action at a controlled tempo.
Complete sets of six to ten repetitions before changing the striking hand.
The coach pauses the group when necessary to demonstrate or correct a common technical fault.
coachingPoints: Hold the football on the open supporting hand rather than gripping it tightly between both hands.
Keep the football in front of the body where the player can see the ball and the intended target.
Form a firm, compact fist with the wrist straight and the thumb safely outside the fingers.
Strike through the lower rear section of the football rather than pushing or carrying it forward.
Keep the supporting hand stable and avoid throwing the football upwards before contact.
Transfer body weight slightly towards the target as the fist moves through the ball.
Finish with the striking fist pointing towards the target.
Prioritise clean contact and legal technique before speed or distance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players begin with a balanced stance and the football positioned in front of the body.
Whether the supporting hand stays open and underneath the football.
Whether the fist contacts the football rather than the supporting hand.
Whether the football leaves the hand from a clear striking action rather than a throw.
Whether the follow-through travels towards the intended target.
Whether players can repeat the technique without rushing or losing body control.

commonErrors.error: The football is tossed or thrown from the supporting hand.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the supporting hand still and require the fist to create the football’s movement.

commonErrors.error: The fist contacts the side or middle of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Mark or point to the lower rear contact area and slow the action until contact improves.

commonErrors.error: The striking wrist bends on impact.
commonErrors.correction: Form a firmer fist and keep the wrist aligned with the forearm.

commonErrors.error: The player grips the football tightly with both hands.
commonErrors.correction: Rest the football on the open supporting palm with only light finger control.

commonErrors.error: The player stands upright with locked knees.
commonErrors.correction: Adopt a balanced athletic stance with soft knees and a slight forward weight transfer.

commonErrors.error: The follow-through finishes across the body.
commonErrors.correction: Direct the fist straight through the football and towards the target.

progressions: Handball towards a partner or stationary target from four to six metres.
Complete consecutive repetitions without pausing between each handball.
Alternate the striking hand after every repetition.
Require players to nominate the target before beginning the action.
regressions: Practise the fist movement without a football.
Hold the football closer to the striking fist to reduce the length of the action.
Use a larger soft football or reduced distance for younger players.
Allow the coach or partner to hold the football lightly while the player practises clean contact.
successIndicators: Support the football on an open and stable hand.
Make clear fist-to-football contact without throwing the ball.
Direct the football towards the intended target.
Demonstrate the basic action with both hands at a controlled speed.
matchApplication: A legal and technically sound handball is the foundation of releasing a teammate, maintaining possession and moving the football through congestion. Players who establish correct supporting-hand position, contact and follow-through are better prepared to execute under movement and pressure later in the chapter.

title: Support-Hand Platform Control
primarySkill: Maintaining a stable supporting-hand platform
objective: Teach players to position and stabilise the football on the supporting hand so the striking fist can make clean, legal and accurately directed contact.
groundSize: A 10-metre × 10-metre area divided into individual technical stations approximately three metres apart.
equipment: Optional coloured tape or removable stickers to identify the ball’s support position and contact area
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Simple organisation with minimal observation or intervention
setup:
Players spread throughout the marked area with one football each.
Place a target cone three to four metres in front of each player.
Players begin by holding the football on the open palm of the supporting hand.
The long axis of the football should point generally towards the target.
The supporting elbow remains slightly flexed and positioned away from the torso.
Players work initially with their preferred supporting hand before changing sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players adopt a balanced stance and place the football on the open supporting hand.
On the first coach call, players freeze and display the football position without striking it.
The coach checks that the football is not being squeezed, tipped excessively or hidden beside the hip.
On the second call, players complete a slow handball towards the target cone.
Players retrieve the football and rebuild the platform before every repetition.
After five repetitions, players change the supporting hand and striking fist.
The coach introduces random “hold” calls so players must stop immediately and show their platform position.
Complete two to three sets on each side.
coachingPoints: Keep the supporting palm open and underneath the centre of the football.
Use the fingers only to steady the football rather than gripping it.
Position the football slightly forward of the hip and in front of the torso.
Point the long axis of the football towards the intended target.
Keep the supporting wrist firm enough to resist collapsing at contact.
Maintain space between the football and the body so the striking fist has a clear path.
Avoid lifting or flicking the supporting hand during the handball.
Rebuild the platform deliberately before every repetition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the football rests on the palm rather than being held tightly in the fingers.
Whether the ball is positioned in front of the body.
Whether the long axis of the football aligns with the target.
Whether the supporting wrist and elbow remain stable at contact.
Whether the supporting hand flicks the football upwards.
Whether platform quality remains consistent when players change hands.

commonErrors.error: The football is held beside or behind the hip.
commonErrors.correction: Move the supporting hand forward so the player can see both the football and target.

commonErrors.error: The fingers squeeze the football tightly.
commonErrors.correction: Open the palm and use only light finger pressure to steady the ball.

commonErrors.error: The football points across the body.
commonErrors.correction: Rotate the ball so its long axis points towards the intended target.

commonErrors.error: The supporting hand lifts during contact.
commonErrors.correction: Freeze the platform and make the striking fist responsible for propulsion.

commonErrors.error: The supporting wrist collapses.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the handball distance and reinforce a firm, stable wrist position.

commonErrors.error: The football sits too close to the torso.
commonErrors.correction: Move the platform away from the body to create a clear striking path.

progressions: Perform the drill while looking at the target rather than down at the football.
Add a partner who checks and provides feedback on platform position.
Handball through a narrow cone gate positioned four metres away.
Change hands on a random coach call.
regressions: Remove the striking action and practise holding the platform position.
Use a stationary coach inspection before every repetition.
Support the football with the preferred hand only.
Reduce the target distance to two metres.
successIndicators: Present an open and stable supporting hand.
Position the football in front of the body.
Align the football with the intended target.
Avoid lifting, tossing or flicking the supporting hand.
Reproduce the platform position on both sides of the body.
matchApplication: A stable supporting-hand platform allows a player to release the football quickly and legally when under pressure. Correct positioning also helps the player keep vision on teammates and reduces miskicks, throws and poorly directed handballs during congested play.

title: Contact Point and Follow-Through
primarySkill: Clean striking contact and directional follow-through
objective: Develop clean contact on the lower rear section of the football and a straight follow-through that produces controlled, accurate ball flight.
groundSize: Pairs positioned four metres apart within a 15-metre × 15-metre technical area.
equipment: Optional removable ball markers or tape
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players in pairs facing each other four metres apart.
Place one cone beside each player to maintain the correct distance.
One player begins with the football while the partner presents both hands as a target.
Players use a controlled stationary stance.
The coach identifies the lower rear striking area of the football before the drill begins.
Pairs complete separate blocks with the right and left fist.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player with the football establishes a stable support-hand platform.
The player forms a closed fist with a straight wrist and positions it behind the football.
The fist travels directly through the lower rear section of the football.
The player completes the action with the fist pointing towards the partner’s chest.
The receiver secures the football, briefly checks the previous handball’s flight and returns it using the same technique.
Partners complete eight handballs each with one fist.
Players then change the supporting and striking hands for a second set.
The pair counts clean handballs that travel directly to the partner without excessive loop, wobble or sideways rotation.
coachingPoints: Keep the striking fist compact, with the thumb outside the fingers.
Align the wrist with the forearm before and during contact.
Contact the lower rear section of the football to produce forward flight.
Drive through the football rather than stopping the fist at impact.
Follow through directly towards the partner’s chest.
Use a small forward weight transfer rather than leaning backwards.
Maintain a stable supporting hand until the football has left the platform.
Judge quality by clean flight and accuracy, not by how hard the football is struck.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the fist is correctly formed before the action begins.
Whether the wrist remains straight at the point of contact.
Whether contact occurs on the football rather than the support hand.
Whether the football travels with controlled forward rotation rather than excessive wobble.
Whether the follow-through finishes towards the partner.
Whether players maintain the same mechanics with both fists.

commonErrors.error: The fist strikes the middle or top of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the contact point and rehearse the fist path slowly.

commonErrors.error: The wrist bends or turns at impact.
commonErrors.correction: Reset the fist and align the wrist directly behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The action stops immediately after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Extend the fist towards the partner and complete the follow-through.

commonErrors.error: The football floats excessively upwards.
commonErrors.correction: Strike through the lower rear rather than underneath the ball.

commonErrors.error: The football travels across the partner’s body.
commonErrors.correction: Align the platform, fist path and follow-through with the centre of the target.

commonErrors.error: The player tries to create power only with the arm.
commonErrors.correction: Add a controlled weight transfer towards the target.

progressions: Increase the partner distance to five or six metres.
Handball through a one-metre-wide cone gate before reaching the receiver.
Complete five consecutive accurate handballs without resetting the count.
Alternate hands after every handball.
regressions: Reduce the distance to two or three metres.
Use a larger chest-level target such as a handball board.
Pause with the fist positioned behind the football before striking.
Practise the follow-through without a football.
successIndicators: Contact the lower rear section of the football.
Produce controlled and direct ball flight.
Perform the action effectively with both fists.
matchApplication: Clean contact and directional follow-through allow players to release teammates accurately at short and medium distances. This is essential when handballing through congestion, feeding a runner or maintaining possession after winning the football at ground level.

title: Dominant-Hand Partner Accuracy
primarySkill: Accurate dominant-hand handballing to a stationary partner
objective: Develop consistent dominant-hand accuracy by requiring players to deliver catchable handballs to a stationary partner’s preferred receiving area.
groundSize: Pairs positioned five metres apart in a 20-metre × 15-metre area.
equipment: Optional coloured bibs or chest target markers
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Players form pairs and stand five metres apart.
One cone marks each player’s starting position.
Each player identifies their dominant striking hand.
The receiver presents a target with hands positioned between waist and chest height.
The handballer must remain behind the cone until the football has been released.
Pairs maintain sufficient space to prevent footballs entering neighbouring lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver calls the handballer’s name and presents a clear two-hand target.
The handballer looks at the target, establishes the support-hand platform and delivers using the dominant fist.
The handball must arrive between the receiver’s waist and upper chest and within the width of the torso.
The receiver secures the football with two hands and resets behind their cone.
The receiver then becomes the handballer and returns the football using their dominant hand.
Pairs count one point for every handball received cleanly without the receiver moving either foot.
Complete rounds of ten handballs per player.
After each round, players record their score, discuss one technical adjustment and repeat.
coachingPoints: Identify the partner’s receiving target before beginning the handball action.
Keep the football in front of the body and aligned with the target.
Use the dominant fist without allowing speed to replace correct technique.
Aim between the receiver’s waist and chest.
Deliver a firm but catchable handball.
Complete a straight follow-through towards the partner.
Communicate before every disposal.
Reset body position after receiving rather than returning the football while off balance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether receivers communicate and present a visible target.
Whether handballers look at the target before releasing the football.
Whether the football reaches the partner at a catchable height and pace.
Whether players maintain correct technique when trying to increase their score.
Whether receivers secure the football cleanly with two hands.
Whether each repetition begins from a balanced position.

commonErrors.error: The handball consistently arrives above shoulder height.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the contact point and direct the follow-through towards the receiver’s chest.

commonErrors.error: The football drops below the receiver’s knees.
commonErrors.correction: Strike through the football and maintain a firm wrist.

commonErrors.error: The receiver must step sideways repeatedly.
commonErrors.correction: Square the platform and fist path to the centre of the partner’s torso.

commonErrors.error: Players rush to improve the score.
commonErrors.correction: Require a visible reset and target call before every repetition.

commonErrors.error: The handball is too hard for the distance.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce striking force and prioritise a catchable delivery.

commonErrors.error: The receiver does not present a target.
commonErrors.correction: Require both hands to be shown before the handballer may release.

progressions: Increase the distance to six or seven metres.
Reduce the permitted receiving target to a smaller chest-level zone.
Complete a timed round while maintaining the accuracy standard.
Require three consecutive accurate handballs before scoring begins.
regressions: Reduce the distance to three metres.
Allow the receiver to move one step to complete the catch.
Use a larger target area from knees to shoulders.
Remove scoring and return to controlled repetition.
successIndicators: Identify and look at the receiving target.
Deliver the football within the partner’s torso width.
Produce a catchable handball at waist-to-chest height.
Maintain dominant-hand technique across repeated efforts.
matchApplication: Accurate dominant-hand delivery allows a player to release a teammate without slowing their movement or exposing them to pressure. The ability to place the football in a safe receiving area improves possession chains around stoppages, contests and defensive exits.

title: Non-Dominant-Hand Technique
primarySkill: Non-dominant-hand handball technique
objective: Develop a functional non-dominant handball action that players can execute legally, accurately and with increasing confidence.
groundSize: Pairs positioned three to four metres apart in a 15-metre × 15-metre technical area.
equipment: Optional coloured wristbands to identify the non-dominant striking hand
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Players form pairs three to four metres apart.
Each player identifies their non-dominant striking hand.
The football is placed on the opposite supporting hand.
Players begin from a balanced stance with the foot on the supporting-hand side slightly forward.
The receiver presents a broad target from waist to chest height.
No scoring is used in the first set; quality and confidence are prioritised.
howTheDrillWorks:
The handballer slowly establishes the non-dominant-side stance and support platform.
The player positions the non-dominant fist directly behind the lower rear section of the football.
The handball is delivered towards the partner at a controlled pace.
The receiver secures the football and allows the handballer time to reset.
Players complete five consecutive repetitions before changing roles.
After both players complete two sets, partners begin alternating every handball.
In the final round, pairs count accurate non-dominant handballs that reach the partner’s torso.
The coach stops players who revert to a throwing action or switch back to their dominant hand.
coachingPoints: Accept a slower action while the non-dominant pattern is being established.
Place the football securely on the opposite supporting hand.
Keep the non-dominant wrist straight and the fist compact.
Position the fist behind the football rather than approaching from the side.
Use a short, direct striking path.
Transfer body weight gently towards the target.
Finish the fist at the partner’s torso.
Measure improvement through clean contact and accuracy rather than power.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players use the nominated non-dominant fist.
Whether the supporting hand and stance correctly reverse from the dominant side.
Whether the wrist remains firm at contact.
Whether players attempt to throw or push the football when coordination breaks down.
Whether confidence and accuracy improve across the sets.
Whether the action becomes more fluent without losing legality.

commonErrors.error: The player switches back to the dominant fist.
commonErrors.correction: Use a wristband or verbal cue and complete short dedicated sets on the non-dominant side.

commonErrors.error: The football is held on the wrong supporting hand.
commonErrors.correction: Place the ball on the hand opposite the striking fist before every repetition.

commonErrors.error: The fist approaches from across the body.
commonErrors.correction: Square the shoulders and position the fist directly behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The player throws the football to compensate for poor coordination.
commonErrors.correction: Freeze the supporting hand and reduce the speed and distance.

commonErrors.error: The wrist collapses at impact.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the striking action and reinforce fist and forearm alignment.

commonErrors.error: The player attempts excessive power.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the distance and reward clean, catchable delivery.

progressions: Increase the partner distance to five metres.
Require five consecutive accurate non-dominant handballs.
Alternate dominant and non-dominant hands without coach prompting.
Handball through a broad cone gate.
regressions: Reduce the distance to two metres.
Practise the striking motion without releasing the football.
Allow the coach or partner to hold the football lightly.
Complete repetitions into a large stationary target.
successIndicators: Use the correct non-dominant fist and opposite supporting hand.
Deliver the football to a catchable target area.
Show improved balance and confidence across repeated efforts.
matchApplication: Players are frequently forced to release the football from the non-preferred side because of pressure, body position or the location of a teammate. Developing both hands reduces predictable movement, prevents unnecessary turning and allows faster disposal in congestion.

title: Alternating-Hand Partner Handball
primarySkill: Switching accurately between dominant and non-dominant handballs
objective: Teach players to reorganise their stance, support hand and striking fist efficiently when changing between right- and left-handed handballs.
groundSize: Pairs positioned four metres apart within a 20-metre × 15-metre area.
equipment: Optional two-coloured markers representing right and left
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Players form pairs four metres apart.
Each pair has one football and two starting cones.
The coach establishes two calls: “right” means strike with the right fist; “left” means strike with the left fist.
Players must place the football on the opposite supporting hand after hearing the call.
The receiver presents a chest-level target.
Calls are initially predictable before becoming random.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player with the football waits in a balanced stance and looks towards the partner.
The coach calls “right” or “left”.
The handballer places the football on the correct supporting hand and adjusts the stance.
The player delivers an accurate handball using the nominated fist.
The receiver secures the football and waits for the next coach call.
Players continue exchanging the football, using the hand nominated before every disposal.
A pair scores one point when the correct hand is used and the receiver catches the football without moving their feet.
Complete two rounds of twelve handballs, changing the pattern and speed of the calls between rounds.
coachingPoints: Listen to the call before organising the football.
Change the support hand as well as the striking fist.
Reposition the feet and hips so the body remains balanced.
Keep the football in front of the body during the change.
Avoid crossing the striking arm excessively across the torso.
Maintain the same contact and follow-through standards on both sides.
Prioritise correct organisation over beating the call.
Look at the partner’s target before releasing the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players correctly interpret the right or left call.
Whether the football is moved to the appropriate supporting hand.
Whether the player reorganises their feet rather than twisting awkwardly.
Whether technique deteriorates on the non-dominant side.
Whether the player looks at the target after responding to the call.
Whether both hands produce catchable deliveries.

commonErrors.error: The player uses the correct fist but the wrong supporting hand.
commonErrors.correction: Require the football to be placed on the opposite palm before the action continues.

commonErrors.error: The player reacts before hearing the full call.
commonErrors.correction: Add a brief pause and require eye contact with the coach before each cue.

commonErrors.error: The feet remain fixed while the torso twists.
commonErrors.correction: Reset the stance and turn the hips and shoulders towards the target.

commonErrors.error: Accuracy falls sharply on the non-dominant side.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the calls and reduce the partner distance.

commonErrors.error: The player looks only at the football.
commonErrors.correction: Organise the ball, then lift the eyes to the partner’s target before release.

commonErrors.error: Players rush and use a throwing action.
commonErrors.correction: Remove scoring until legal technique is restored.

progressions: Increase the speed and unpredictability of the calls.
Use visual coloured cues instead of verbal calls.
Require the receiver to call the hand to be used.
Add a one-step lateral reposition before the handball.
regressions: Use an alternating right-left pattern rather than random calls.
Complete a full set with one hand before changing.
Reduce the distance to three metres.
Allow players to verbally name the support hand before releasing.
successIndicators: Position the football on the correct supporting hand.
Reorganise their stance without losing balance.
Respond to the cue without rushing the technique.
matchApplication: Players must often choose the hand that protects the football from an opponent or releases a teammate into space. Efficiently changing sides helps players avoid turning back into pressure and improves disposal speed around contests and stoppages.

title: Target-Gate Handball Accuracy
primarySkill: Directing the handball through a defined accuracy gate
objective: Improve handball accuracy by requiring players to align the support platform, striking path and follow-through through a clearly defined target gate.
groundSize: Straight handball lanes five to six metres long and approximately three metres wide.
equipment: Optional target hoops or handball boards
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Players form pairs five metres apart.
Place two cones midway between each pair to create a gate approximately 1.5 metres wide.
The gate should align with the receiver’s torso.
One player begins with the football while the partner stands behind the gate.
Players complete separate rounds with the dominant and non-dominant fist.
Adjust gate width for age and ability.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver presents a two-hand target behind the cone gate.
The handballer aligns the football, body and striking path with the centre of the gate.
The player handballs through the gate towards the receiver.
The receiver catches the football and returns it through the same gate.
A pair scores one point when the football passes cleanly through the gate and is caught without the receiver moving more than one step.
Complete ten handballs per player using the dominant fist.
Repeat the round using the non-dominant fist.
Record separate dominant- and non-dominant-side scores to identify technical differences.
coachingPoints: Align the feet, hips, support platform and follow-through with the centre of the gate.
Look through the gate towards the receiving target.
Keep the handball flat enough to travel through the gate at a catchable height.
Use controlled force appropriate to the distance.
Finish the fist through the centre of the gate.
Maintain the same accuracy process on both sides.
Reset fully after an inaccurate handball rather than immediately repeating the error.
Use the gate as a directional guide, not as the final target; the teammate remains the target.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players align their body and football before striking.
Whether the handball passes through the central portion of the gate.
Whether the football reaches the receiver at a practical height and pace.
Whether misses consistently occur to one side.
Whether players adjust after an inaccurate repetition.
Whether non-dominant-side accuracy remains technically legal.

commonErrors.error: The football repeatedly misses on the striking-hand side.
commonErrors.correction: Straighten the follow-through and prevent the fist from sweeping across the body.

commonErrors.error: The football misses on the supporting-hand side.
commonErrors.correction: Check the ball angle and ensure the platform points through the gate.

commonErrors.error: The handball travels over the top of the gate.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the contact point and direct the fist towards chest height.

commonErrors.error: The player focuses only on the cones.
commonErrors.correction: Look through the gate and target the receiver’s hands.

commonErrors.error: The football reaches the gate but not the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Increase the controlled weight transfer and complete the follow-through.

commonErrors.error: Accuracy drops when changing hands.
commonErrors.correction: Widen the gate temporarily and slow the non-dominant action.

progressions: Narrow the gate to one metre.
Increase the distance between partners.
Alternate hands after every handball.
Require three consecutive successful handballs before the pair may score.
Move the gate slightly to the player’s right or left to change the delivery angle.
regressions: Widen the gate to two metres.
Remove the receiver and handball into a large stationary target.
successIndicators: Align their body and handball action with the target.
Send the football cleanly through the gate.
Deliver at a catchable height and pace.
Correct their alignment after a miss.
Achieve improving accuracy with both hands.
matchApplication: Accurate handballs must travel through narrow spaces between opponents and reach a teammate without exposing them to interception or immediate pressure. The gate represents the available passing lane while the partner represents the intended receiver.

title: Receive, Set and Release
primarySkill: Organising the football after receiving and before handballing
objective: Teach players to receive the football cleanly, establish a balanced handball platform and release accurately without unnecessary fumbles or additional movements.
groundSize: Triangular stations with each cone four to five metres apart, arranged within a 20-metre × 20-metre area.
equipment: One football per group of three
Optional bibs to identify starting roles
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players into groups of three.
Place three cones in a triangle, four to five metres apart.
One player begins at each cone.
The football starts with Player A.
Players remain at their cone during the introductory version.
The handball direction stays the same for one set before reversing.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A handballs accurately to Player B.
Player B receives the football with two hands and brings it under control in front of the body.
Player B adjusts the football onto the correct supporting hand.
Player B looks towards Player C and delivers an accurate handball.
Player C repeats the receive, set and release process back to Player A.
Players continue around the triangle for a set period or a nominated number of complete circuits.
Reverse the direction so players organise the football on the opposite side.
If the football is fumbled or poorly directed, the group resets rather than rushing the next action.
coachingPoints: Present both hands early to receive the football.
Cushion the football into the hands rather than allowing it to strike the chest.
Secure possession before repositioning the football onto the support hand.
Keep the football in front of the body during the transfer.
Establish balance before striking.
Lift the eyes and identify the next receiver before release.
Use the hand that allows the football to move naturally in the direction of the drill.
Remove unnecessary taps, spins or changes of grip.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players present a clear target before receiving.
Whether the football is secured cleanly with two hands.
Whether players reposition the football efficiently onto the supporting hand.
Whether the body remains balanced during the transfer.
Whether players identify the next target before handballing.
Whether the drill flows without rushed or uncontrolled disposals.

commonErrors.error: The receiver traps the football against the chest.
commonErrors.correction: Present both hands and cushion the football before it reaches the body.

commonErrors.error: The football is spun or moved repeatedly before release.
commonErrors.correction: Use one controlled transfer directly onto the supporting hand.

commonErrors.error: The player looks down throughout the action.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the ball, then lift the eyes to the next receiver before striking.

commonErrors.error: The handball is released before balance is established.
commonErrors.correction: Require a stable stance and clear platform before disposal.

commonErrors.error: The player uses the same hand regardless of direction.
commonErrors.correction: Reverse the triangle and nominate the most efficient striking side.

commonErrors.error: Players rush after a fumble.
commonErrors.correction: Stop, regain clean possession and rebuild the technique.

progressions: Allow one step towards the next receiver before releasing.
Alternate the direction on a coach call.
Introduce a second football once the group demonstrates control.
Reduce the permitted time between receiving and releasing.
Require players to call the next receiver’s name before possession arrives.
regressions: Increase the distance between repetitions by using only one football and a slower tempo.
Allow players to pause for two seconds after receiving.
Use the preferred hand throughout the first set.
Reduce the triangle distance to three metres.
successIndicators: Receive the football cleanly with two hands.
Transfer it directly onto the supporting hand.
Identify the next target before release.
Deliver accurately in both directions around the triangle.
matchApplication: Players commonly receive a handball and must release a teammate immediately. Efficiently securing, setting and disposing of the football reduces possession time, limits fumbles and supports fast ball movement through congestion and overlap situations.

title: One-Step Partner Handball
primarySkill: Using a balanced step to support handball accuracy
objective: Develop the ability to use one controlled step towards the target while maintaining balance, legal technique and partner accuracy.
groundSize: Pairs positioned six metres apart in handball lanes approximately three metres wide.
equipment: Optional line markings to indicate the step zone
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Players form pairs six metres apart.
Mark a starting cone and a release cone one metre in front of each player.
The receiver begins behind the starting cone.
The handballer may take one controlled step from the starting cone towards the release cone.
Players initially use the dominant hand for one set and the non-dominant hand for the next.
The lane must remain clear of other footballs and players.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver presents a target and calls for the football.
The handballer steps towards the release cone with the foot that supports a balanced handball action.
As body weight transfers forward, the player delivers the football towards the partner’s torso.
The player completes the handball before moving beyond the release cone.
The receiver secures the football, resets behind their starting cone and repeats the action.
Players alternate handballs for ten repetitions each.
Repeat the drill using the opposite striking hand.
Pairs count accurate handballs that are delivered from a balanced step and caught without the receiver leaving the lane.
coachingPoints: Step towards the intended target rather than across the body.
Keep the football stable while the feet begin to move.
Time the striking action with the forward transfer of body weight.
Maintain the supporting-hand platform throughout the step.
Keep the head steady and eyes on the receiver.
Release the football from a balanced position rather than lunging.
Complete the follow-through towards the target.
Rebuild the feet and platform correctly when changing hands.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the step travels towards the target.
Whether the player remains balanced during and after release.
Whether the football moves excessively before the striking action.
Whether weight transfer improves the handball without creating excessive force.
Whether the receiver is given a catchable delivery.
Whether players adjust their footwork when changing striking hands.

commonErrors.error: The player steps across the body.
commonErrors.correction: Point the lead foot towards the receiver and keep the hips aligned with the target.

commonErrors.error: The player lunges and loses balance.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the step and keep the chest over the hips.

commonErrors.error: The football bounces on the support hand during the step.
commonErrors.correction: Stabilise the platform and move the body around the football.

commonErrors.error: The handball is released too early.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the forward weight transfer before the fist reaches contact.

commonErrors.error: The handball is released after the player has overstepped the cone.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the action and strike while balanced inside the release zone.

commonErrors.error: Non-dominant footwork is awkward.
commonErrors.correction: Rehearse the step and stance without the football before restarting.

progressions: Remove the release cone and require players to self-organise the step.
Alternate hands after every repetition.
Add a second step while preserving legal disposal technique.
Require the receiver to move one metre to the right or left before presenting the target.
Increase the distance to seven or eight metres.
regressions: Reduce the step length to half a metre.
Reduce the partner distance to four metres.
successIndicators: Maintain football stability during the movement.
Deliver a catchable handball to the partner.
Perform the one-step action with both hands.
matchApplication: A controlled step helps players generate distance, improve accuracy and move the football towards a teammate without overcommitting their balance. This action commonly occurs after a mark, ground-ball win or short receive when a player has limited but usable space.

title: Two-Sided Handball Fundamentals Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing fundamental handball competency with both hands
objective: Assess each player’s ability to execute legal, controlled and accurate stationary and one-step handballs using both the dominant and non-dominant fist.
groundSize: Four technical stations arranged within a 25-metre × 20-metre area, with handball distances ranging from three to six metres.
equipment: One football per pair or station
Four target gates or marked receiving zones
Optional handball targets or rebound boards
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Establish four stations:
Station 1: Stationary dominant-hand technique over four metres.
Station 2: Stationary non-dominant-hand technique over three to four metres.
Station 3: Alternating-hand accuracy through a 1.5-metre target gate.
Station 4: One-step handball to a partner over six metres.
Players work in pairs, with one player performing and one receiving.
A coach or nominated observer records technical and accuracy outcomes.
Each player completes a defined number of repetitions before rotating.
Stations must provide enough separation to prevent interference.
Assessment criteria are explained before the first rotation.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, the player completes five stationary dominant-hand handballs to a partner’s torso.
At Station 2, the player completes five stationary non-dominant-hand handballs to a partner’s torso.
At Station 3, the player completes six handballs through the gate, alternating the striking hand after each repetition.
At Station 4, the player completes three one-step handballs with each hand.
The observer records whether each repetition is legal, technically controlled and accurately received.
Players rotate to the next station after both partners have completed the required repetitions.
At the end of all four stations, each player receives one technical strength and one priority for improvement.
Players repeat the lowest-scoring station for a short correction block.
coachingPoints: Apply the same legal technique standard at every station.
Assess the support-hand platform, fist formation, contact point and follow-through separately.
Distinguish between an inaccurate handball and an illegal throwing action.
Require players to organise the correct support hand when alternating sides.
Observe balance before, during and after disposal.
Judge accuracy according to whether the partner can receive without being placed under unnecessary difficulty.
Record non-dominant-side performance separately from dominant-side performance.
Provide specific feedback based on observable actions rather than general encouragement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the football is supported on an open and stable hand.
Whether the player uses a clear closed-fist striking action.
Whether contact occurs on the lower rear section of the football.
Whether the follow-through is directed towards the target.
Whether the football reaches the receiving area at a catchable height and pace.
Whether the player can reorganise correctly when changing hands.
Whether balance is maintained during the one-step component.
Whether the player responds to feedback during the correction block.

commonErrors.error: The player achieves accuracy by throwing or flicking the football.
commonErrors.correction: Remove the score for that repetition and rebuild the legal striking action at reduced speed.

commonErrors.error: Dominant-hand results are strong but non-dominant results are poor.
commonErrors.correction: Prescribe additional non-dominant platform, contact and short-distance accuracy work.

commonErrors.error: The player contacts the supporting hand.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition the fist behind the football and increase the space between ball and body.

commonErrors.error: The player repeatedly misses to one side.
commonErrors.correction: Check platform alignment and whether the follow-through sweeps across the torso.

commonErrors.error: The one-step action causes loss of balance.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the step and align the lead foot with the target.

commonErrors.error: The player rushes after an unsuccessful repetition.
commonErrors.correction: Require a complete reset before the next assessed handball.

commonErrors.error: The receiver is forced to reach above the head or below the knees.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the strike angle and target the waist-to-chest receiving zone.

progressions: Narrow the accuracy gate from 1.5 metres to one metre.
Increase stationary handball distance by one to two metres.
Complete the assessment against a defined time limit without reducing the technical standard.
Add a visual cue that determines the striking hand.
Require two consecutive successful repetitions before a station is passed.
regressions: Remove the one-step component and assess stationary technique only.
Allow a technical rehearsal before each assessed repetition.
Assess the dominant and non-dominant sides in separate blocks rather than alternating.
successIndicators: Complete a legal handball action with both fists.
Position the football correctly on the supporting hand.
Produce clean contact and directional follow-through.
Deliver most handballs into the partner’s receiving zone.
Change hands without losing technical organisation.
Maintain balance during the one-step handball.
Identify and respond to a specific coaching correction.
matchApplication: The assessment identifies whether a player possesses the minimum technical foundation required to handball effectively in Australian football. Competency with both hands allows faster release, improved protection of the football and more effective use of teammates positioned on either side of a contest.

title: Rapid Chest-Level Exchange
primarySkill: Quick, accurate handball exchange between stationary partners
objective: Develop the ability to receive, organise and return a chest-level handball quickly while preserving legal technique and catchable accuracy.
groundSize: Pairs positioned three to four metres apart within a 15-metre × 15-metre technical area.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players into pairs facing each other three to four metres apart.
Place one cone at each player’s starting position.
One player begins with the football.
Both players remain behind their cone and present a chest-level receiving target.
The first round uses the dominant fist only.
The second round uses the non-dominant fist.
The final round alternates striking hands after every handball.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player with the football delivers a firm, catchable handball towards the partner’s chest.
The receiver secures the football with two hands.
The receiver immediately positions the football on the correct supporting hand.
The football is returned without unnecessary taps, spins or changes of grip.
Pairs continue exchanging the football for a 20-second work period.
Players rest briefly, then repeat using the opposite striking hand.
In the final round, players alternate hands after every disposal.
The pair records the number of clean consecutive exchanges completed without a dropped football, illegal disposal or inaccurate delivery.
If an error occurs, the count restarts from zero while the work period continues.
coachingPoints: Present both hands before the football arrives.
Cushion the football into the hands rather than trapping it against the chest.
Transfer the football directly onto the supporting hand.
Keep the ball in front of the body during the receive-and-release action.
Use a compact striking motion to support quick release.
Maintain a straight wrist and clear fist-to-football contact.
Deliver to the partner’s torso rather than simply handballing quickly.
Increase tempo only while the football remains controlled and legally disposed of.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players present their hands before the football arrives.
Whether the football is controlled cleanly without being trapped against the body.
Whether players reposition the football efficiently.
Whether handball technique becomes a throw as the tempo increases.
Whether the football continues to reach the partner’s torso.
Whether non-dominant-hand speed improves without a major reduction in accuracy.
Whether players remain balanced throughout repeated exchanges.

commonErrors.error: Players return the football before securing it.
commonErrors.correction: Require clear two-hand control before the ball is placed on the supporting hand.

commonErrors.error: The supporting hand flicks the football during quick exchanges.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the tempo and make the fist responsible for propulsion.

commonErrors.error: Accuracy falls as the pair attempts to increase the count.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and require the handball to reach the partner’s torso before increasing tempo.

commonErrors.error: The player uses unnecessary taps or ball rotations.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer the football directly from the catch onto the supporting palm.

commonErrors.error: The receiver’s hands appear late.
commonErrors.correction: Present the target before the partner begins the handball action.

commonErrors.error: Players remain on the dominant side during the alternating round.
commonErrors.correction: Call the striking hand aloud before each disposal.

progressions: Extend work periods from 20 to 30 seconds.
Reduce the partner distance slightly to increase exchange speed.
Require alternating hands throughout the entire round.
Add a target count that must be reached without an error.
Require players to call the partner’s name before every handball.
regressions: Allow players to pause after each catch.
Complete full sets with the dominant hand before changing sides.
Increase the target area from waist to shoulders.
Reduce the exchange count to five consecutive handballs.
successIndicators: Receive the football cleanly with two hands.
Transfer it directly onto the correct supporting hand.
Release quickly without using an illegal throwing action.
Deliver the football to the partner’s chest.
Maintain rhythm and accuracy with both hands.
Complete increasing numbers of uninterrupted exchanges.
matchApplication: Quick handball exchanges occur around stoppages, loose-ball contests and short possession chains. Players must secure the football, organise it efficiently and release a teammate before pressure closes without sacrificing legality or accuracy.

title: High-Low Target Handball
primarySkill: Controlling handball height to varied receiving targets
objective: Develop the ability to adjust handball trajectory and force so the football reaches high, central and low receiving targets accurately and safely.
groundSize: Pairs positioned four to five metres apart within a 20-metre × 15-metre area.
equipment: Optional coloured bibs or target cards
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Players form pairs four to five metres apart.
One player begins as the handballer and the other as the receiver.
The receiver may present one of three targets:
Hands above chest height.
Hands at chest height.
Hands between waist and hip height.
The receiver must display the target before the handball action begins.
Players complete one round with the dominant fist and one with the non-dominant fist.
Low targets must remain above knee height to encourage safe, realistic receiving.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver presents a high, central or low two-hand target.
The handballer identifies the target before organising the football.
The player adjusts the contact point, striking force and follow-through to reach the nominated height.
The receiver catches the football and resets the target.
After five repetitions, players exchange roles.
Once both players have completed each target height, the receiver varies the target randomly.
The handballer scores one point when the football reaches the presented target without forcing the receiver to move their feet.
Complete a dominant-hand round followed by a non-dominant-hand round.
coachingPoints: Look at the presented hands rather than handballing automatically to chest height.
Keep the platform aligned with the receiver.
Use a slightly higher finishing line for a high target without scooping the football.
Use a direct, controlled strike for the central target.
Reduce the finishing height and force for the low target.
Maintain legal fist contact regardless of trajectory.
Avoid excessive looping ball flight.
Make every delivery catchable and appropriate to the receiver’s position.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify the target before beginning the handball.
Whether trajectory changes are created through controlled technique rather than throwing.
Whether high handballs remain within a safe receiving range.
Whether low handballs arrive above the knees.
Whether the receiver can catch the football without moving their feet.
Whether players can make the same adjustments with both fists.
Whether ball flight remains direct rather than excessively looped.

commonErrors.error: High targets cause the player to throw the football upwards.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a stable platform and create height through the striking angle and follow-through.

commonErrors.error: Low handballs bounce before reaching the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Increase the firmness of contact and aim above knee height.

commonErrors.error: Every handball is delivered at the same height.
commonErrors.correction: Require the player to name the target height before release.

commonErrors.error: The football travels above the receiver’s head.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce force and finish towards the presented hands.

commonErrors.error: The player looks down at the football throughout the action.
commonErrors.correction: Organise the platform, then return the eyes to the target before striking.

commonErrors.error: Non-dominant handballs lose directional control.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the distance and use predictable targets before returning to random cues.

progressions: Use random target changes immediately before release.
Alternate striking hands after each repetition.
Add a fourth target slightly to the receiver’s right or left.
Increase the partner distance by one metre.
Require three successful deliveries to each target height.
regressions: Predetermine a sequence of high, central and low targets.
Reduce the partner distance to three metres.
Allow the handballer an extended pause before release.
successIndicators: Recognise the target height before release.
Adjust handball trajectory without throwing the football.
Deliver within the receiver’s safe catching range.
Maintain direct and controlled ball flight.
Reach varied targets with both hands.
Select appropriate force for the distance and height.
matchApplication: Teammates rarely present identical receiving positions. A player may need to handball over an opponent’s arm, down to a teammate gathering at ground level or directly into a runner’s hands. Controlling handball height supports possession and protects the receiver.

title: Lateral Release Body Alignment
primarySkill: Handballing accurately to a target positioned beside the body
objective: Teach players to realign their feet, hips and shoulders to deliver an accurate handball to a teammate positioned laterally rather than directly in front.
groundSize: Groups arranged in a shallow triangle with targets four metres to the left and right of the central player.
equipment: One football per group of three
Optional coloured markers for left and right
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players into groups of three.
Place one central cone and one target cone four metres to either side, forming a shallow triangle.
The central player begins with the football.
One receiver stands at each outside cone.
The player on the right should generally be reached with a right-fist handball, while the player on the left should generally be reached with a left-fist handball.
The coach may modify the nominated hand when teaching protection or specific body-position outcomes.
howTheDrillWorks:
The central player begins facing forward with the football secured in front of the body.
The coach or one outside player calls “left” or “right”.
The central player adjusts the feet, hips and shoulders towards the nominated receiver.
The football is placed on the correct supporting hand.
The player delivers an accurate handball to the receiver’s torso.
The receiver returns the football to the central player.
The next call is made only after the central player has regained balance and reset facing forward.
Complete eight to twelve repetitions before rotating the central player.
Every player completes one rotation in the central position.
coachingPoints: Move the feet before attempting to force the handball across the body.
Turn the hips and shoulders sufficiently towards the intended target.
Keep the football in front of the torso during the realignment.
Use the striking hand that allows a direct fist path towards the receiver.
Maintain balance through the turn and release.
Avoid dropping the football beside or behind the hip.
Lift the eyes to confirm the receiver’s target.
Reset to the original position after each disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player moves the feet or only twists through the torso.
Whether hips and shoulders align with the receiver.
Whether the football remains visible and in front of the body.
Whether the correct striking hand is selected.
Whether the handball travels directly to the receiver.
Whether balance is maintained after release.
Whether players can perform the action equally to both sides.

commonErrors.error: The player twists without moving the feet.
commonErrors.correction: Use a short adjustment step to turn the hips towards the receiver.

commonErrors.error: The football is carried behind the hip.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the support platform in front of the torso throughout the turn.

commonErrors.error: The player handballs across the body with the wrong fist.
commonErrors.correction: Reorganise the football onto the hand that creates a direct striking path.

commonErrors.error: The player over-rotates and loses sight of the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Use a smaller turn and keep the head directed towards the target.

commonErrors.error: The handball travels behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the body turn before striking and follow through at the receiver’s chest.

commonErrors.error: The player does not reset between repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Return to the central starting position before the next call.

progressions: Make the left or right call later.
Allow both outside players to move one metre before presenting a target.
Alternate the striking-hand rule to challenge body organisation.
Add a passive marker in front of the central player to encourage release away from pressure.
Require a one-step follow after the handball.
regressions: Complete all repetitions to one side before changing.
Reduce the target distance to three metres.
Allow the central player to begin already facing the receiver.
successIndicators: Adjust their feet before releasing laterally.
Align their hips and shoulders with the target.
Keep the football in front of the body.
Maintain balance during the turn and release.
matchApplication: Players regularly win the football while facing away from supporting teammates. Correct lateral alignment allows them to release to an outside runner or nearby teammate without throwing across the body, losing balance or exposing the football unnecessarily.

title: Half-Turn Receive and Handball
primarySkill: Receiving with the back partially turned and reorganising to handball
objective: Develop the ability to receive the football from behind or beside the body, complete a controlled half-turn and release accurately to a visible teammate.
groundSize: Straight stations approximately eight metres long and four metres wide.
equipment: One football per group of three
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Organise players into groups of three in a straight line.
Player A begins with the football.
Player B stands three metres ahead, facing away from Player A.
Player C stands a further four metres ahead and slightly to one side.
Player B looks over the shoulder before the football is delivered.
The side occupied by Player C determines the preferred direction of Player B’s turn and handball.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player B scans over the shoulder to locate Player A and then identifies Player C.
Player A handballs to Player B’s presented hands.
Player B receives the football cleanly and keeps it in front of the body.
Player B pivots through a controlled half-turn towards Player C.
Player B organises the football onto the appropriate supporting hand.
Player B delivers an accurate handball to Player C.
Players follow their disposal: Player A moves to Player B’s cone, Player B moves to Player C’s cone and Player C takes the football to the starting position.
After several repetitions, move Player C to the opposite side so players turn and release both ways.
Continue until every player has performed multiple turns in each direction.
coachingPoints: Scan before the football arrives.
Present both hands towards the initial handballer.
Secure the football before beginning the turn.
Pivot with short, controlled footwork rather than swinging the upper body.
Keep the football in front and away from the trailing side.
Lift the eyes to relocate the final receiver.
Use the hand that supports a direct release after the turn.
Maintain balance and complete the disposal before accelerating to the next cone.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player B scans before the initial handball arrives.
Whether the football is received cleanly with two hands.
Whether the turn begins only after possession is secured.
Whether the football remains in front of the body.
Whether the player selects the appropriate hand after turning.
Whether the final handball reaches Player C accurately.
Whether rotation movement begins after a balanced disposal.

commonErrors.error: The receiver turns before controlling the football.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the ball with two hands before initiating the pivot.

commonErrors.error: The player does not scan before possession.
commonErrors.correction: Require a visible shoulder check before Player A may handball.

commonErrors.error: The football is carried around behind the body.
commonErrors.correction: Keep it in front of the chest and turn the feet around the football.

commonErrors.error: The player uses large, unstable pivot steps.
commonErrors.correction: Use shorter adjustment steps and keep the chest over the hips.

commonErrors.error: The final receiver is not relocated after the turn.
commonErrors.correction: Lift the eyes before organising the handball platform.

commonErrors.error: The player releases with the wrong hand and handballs across the torso.
commonErrors.correction: Move the football to the support hand that creates a direct path to the receiver.

progressions: Move Player C to an unpredictable left or right position.
Require Player C to present a high or low target.
Increase the pace of Player A’s initial handball.
Allow Player B one step forward after completing the turn.
Add a second possible receiver and require Player B to choose after turning.
regressions: Allow Player B to begin side-on rather than facing away.
Reduce the distance between Player B and Player C.
Pause after the catch before beginning the turn.
successIndicators: Keep the ball in front of the body.
Release accurately after turning both directions.
matchApplication: Players often receive while facing a contest, boundary or defensive goal and must turn to connect with support. Scanning, controlled footwork and efficient release help maintain possession and prevent the player from turning blindly into pressure.

title: Distance-Control Handball
primarySkill: Adjusting handball force for short, medium and longer targets
objective: Develop the ability to vary handball force and body contribution so the football reaches teammates accurately across different short and medium distances.
groundSize: Handball lanes eight metres long and approximately four metres wide.
equipment: Flat markers placed at three, five and seven metres
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Establish a handballer’s starting cone.
Place target cones at three, five and seven metres.
One receiver begins at each target distance, or one receiver moves between the three distances.
The handballer begins with the football at the starting cone.
The coach nominates the target distance before each repetition.
Players complete blocks using both fists.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach calls “short”, “medium” or “long”.
The nominated receiver presents a two-hand target.
The handballer identifies the distance and adjusts stance, force and weight transfer.
The player delivers an accurate, catchable handball to the nominated receiver.
The receiver returns the football to the handballer.
Complete six repetitions before changing the handballer.
In the second round, the distance calls become random.
In the final round, players alternate striking hands after every repetition.
One point is awarded when the football reaches the nominated receiver without bouncing or forcing more than one corrective step.
coachingPoints: Judge the target distance before beginning the striking action.
Use a compact arm action for the short handball.
Add controlled weight transfer for the medium handball.
Use stronger leg and body contribution for the longer handball.
Maintain the same stable support platform at every distance.
Avoid creating extra distance by throwing or lifting the football.
Keep ball flight firm and direct.
Prioritise the receiver’s ability to catch and continue play.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the nominated distance before release.
Whether striking force changes appropriately.
Whether longer handballs include controlled body and weight transfer.
Whether short handballs are overhit.
Whether longer handballs become throws or high looping disposals.
Whether accuracy remains consistent across all distances.
Whether both hands can reach the required targets legally.

commonErrors.error: Short handballs are struck too hard.
commonErrors.correction: Use a shorter fist action and reduce forward weight transfer.

commonErrors.error: Longer handballs fall short.
commonErrors.correction: Increase body contribution and complete the follow-through.

commonErrors.error: The player throws the football to reach the longest target.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the distance temporarily and reinforce a stable platform and clear strike.

commonErrors.error: Ball flight loops excessively.
commonErrors.correction: Strike through the lower rear section and direct the follow-through at the receiver.

commonErrors.error: The same force is used for every target.
commonErrors.correction: Rehearse each distance separately before returning to random calls.

commonErrors.error: Non-dominant handballs cannot reach the longest target accurately.
commonErrors.correction: Move that target closer until legal, controlled technique is established.

progressions: Increase the longest target to eight or nine metres for capable players.
Give the distance call later.
Require alternating hands.
Add a small left or right adjustment to each target position.
Score consecutive successes across all three distances.
regressions: Use only short and medium targets.
Allow the handballer to use the dominant fist only.
Remove scoring and focus on controlled technique.
successIndicators: Adjust force appropriately for each distance.
Maintain legal fist contact at longer ranges.
Use body weight effectively without overbalancing.
Reach short, medium and longer targets with both hands.
matchApplication: Players must judge whether a teammate is close enough for a soft release or requires a stronger handball into space. Correct distance control prevents overhandballing, hospital handballs and disposals that fall short of a moving teammate.

title: Two-Ball Partner Coordination
primarySkill: Maintaining handball technique while managing two simultaneous footballs
objective: Develop receiving readiness, communication and technical consistency by requiring pairs to exchange two footballs in a controlled sequence.
groundSize: Pairs positioned four metres apart with a minimum four-metre-wide lane.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Players form pairs four metres apart.
Each player begins with one football.
Establish a clear sequence before using continuous exchanges.
Player A begins by handballing while Player B holds their football.
Player B receives Player A’s football, then returns the football they originally held.
The sequence continues so only one football is travelling at a time during the introductory version.
Pairs must remain separated from adjacent groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A calls the partner’s name and delivers the first football.
Player B receives Player A’s football while continuing to control the second football.
Player B immediately handballs the second football back to Player A.
Player A receives it and then returns the football they were originally given.
The exchange continues in a controlled alternating rhythm.
Complete a 20-second round using dominant-hand disposals.
Repeat using non-dominant-hand disposals.
In the final round, alternate the striking hand after each disposal.
If both footballs are released at once or either football is dropped, the pair resets before restarting.
coachingPoints: Communicate before every release.
Present the free hand clearly to receive.
Secure the arriving football before releasing the second football.
Keep both footballs separated and in front of the body.
Maintain a stable support platform even when attention is divided.
Use a controlled rhythm rather than attempting maximum speed.
Keep deliveries at chest height.
Stop and reset immediately if the sequence loses control.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players follow the correct release sequence.
Whether communication occurs before each handball.
Whether the receiving hand is presented early.
Whether either football is trapped against the body.
Whether technique deteriorates because attention is divided.
Whether both hands can be used without disrupting the rhythm.
Whether pairs reset safely after an error.

commonErrors.error: Both players release simultaneously.
commonErrors.correction: Return to a clear Player A then Player B sequence.

commonErrors.error: The arriving football is not secured before the second is released.
commonErrors.correction: Require two-hand control before the outgoing handball.

commonErrors.error: Players hold one football against the body.
commonErrors.correction: Keep both footballs visible and supported in front.

commonErrors.error: Communication disappears as speed increases.
commonErrors.correction: No disposal is permitted until the partner’s name is called.

commonErrors.error: Handballs drift outside the receiving lane.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the rhythm and target the centre of the partner’s torso.

commonErrors.error: Players become stationary and tense through the upper body.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain soft knees, relaxed shoulders and balanced posture.

progressions: Increase the work period to 30 seconds.
Allow the sequence to become continuous once control is demonstrated.
Alternate striking hands after each disposal.
Require one football to travel high and the other at chest height.
Add a target count for uninterrupted exchanges.
regressions: Allow a full pause between receiving and releasing.
Reduce the distance to three metres.
Have the coach call each release in sequence.
successIndicators: Receive cleanly while controlling the second football.
Use both hands without losing coordination.
matchApplication: Although two footballs are not used in match play, the drill develops divided attention, receiving readiness and the ability to organise the football while processing another action. These qualities support clean disposal in crowded, fast-moving possession chains.

title: Protective-Side Handball
primarySkill: Positioning the body between the football and passive pressure before handballing
objective: Teach players to use their body as a barrier, organise the football on the protected side and release accurately away from passive pressure.
groundSize: Stations approximately six metres long and four metres wide.
equipment: One football per group of three
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Organise players into groups of three: ball carrier, passive pressure player and receiver.
The ball carrier begins at the central cone.
The passive pressure player stands one arm’s length to the ball carrier’s left or right.
The receiver stands four metres away on the opposite side.
The pressure player may extend an arm or hold a bump pad but may not tackle, bump or strike at the football.
The ball carrier must use the body to protect the football before releasing to the receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins with the football secured in front of the body.
The pressure player takes a controlled position on one side.
The ball carrier turns slightly so the hips, shoulder and torso sit between the pressure and the football.
The football is positioned on the protected-side supporting hand.
The receiver presents a target away from the pressure.
The ball carrier handballs accurately to the receiver.
Players rotate from ball carrier to receiver, receiver to pressure and pressure to ball carrier.
Change the pressure side regularly so players protect and release with both hands.
The pressure player remains controlled and provides positioning information rather than attempting to win possession.
coachingPoints: Identify the side from which pressure is arriving.
Place the body between the pressure player and the football.
Keep the feet wide enough to maintain balance.
Hold the football on the side furthest from pressure.
Keep the supporting elbow and football away from the pressure player.
Look beyond the pressure to identify the receiver.
Use the striking hand that allows release away from the opponent.
Avoid leaning backwards or exposing the football during the handball action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier recognises the pressure side.
Whether the body is positioned between the opponent and football.
Whether the football remains on the protected side.
Whether the player maintains balance.
Whether the receiver presents away from the pressure.
Whether the handball travels into safe space.
Whether both sides of the body are used competently.

commonErrors.error: The football is held on the side closest to pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer it to the protected-side supporting hand before release.

commonErrors.error: The player turns their back completely and loses sight of the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Use a side-on protection position while keeping vision downfield.

commonErrors.error: The stance is narrow and unstable.
commonErrors.correction: Widen the feet and lower the centre of gravity.

commonErrors.error: The player extends the football away from the body.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the platform compact and within the protected space.

commonErrors.error: The handball is released across the pressure player.
commonErrors.correction: Select the outside hand and direct the disposal away from pressure.

commonErrors.error: The pressure player becomes too active.
commonErrors.correction: Return to passive arm or bump-pad positioning with no tackling.

progressions: Allow the pressure player to apply light body pressure with a bump pad.
Move the receiver one metre after the ball carrier assumes the protection position.
Require the ball carrier to identify the pressure side from a late cue.
Add a second receiver on the protected side.
Reduce the time allowed before release.
regressions: Remove the pressure player and use a cone to represent pressure.
Allow the ball carrier to begin already side-on.
successIndicators: Position the body between pressure and the football.
Keep the football on the protected side.
Use both sides of the body as required.
matchApplication: Players frequently win possession with an opponent positioned nearby. Protecting the football with the body and releasing from the safe side reduces tackles, smothers and turnovers while allowing a supporting teammate to continue the possession chain.

title: Three-Player Handball Triangle
primarySkill: Maintaining accurate handball possession between three supporting players
objective: Develop continuous three-player handball possession in which players present clear targets, use the appropriate hand and move into the next support position after disposal.
groundSize: Triangles with sides five metres long, arranged within a 25-metre × 20-metre area.
equipment: One football per group of three
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players into groups of three.
Place three cones in an equilateral triangle approximately five metres apart.
One player begins at each cone.
The football starts with Player A.
The first round moves clockwise.
The second round moves anticlockwise.
Players follow their handball to the next cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player B presents a target and calls for the football.
Player A handballs accurately to Player B.
Immediately after releasing, Player A runs to Player B’s cone.
Player B receives, organises the football and handballs to Player C.
Player B follows the disposal to Player C’s cone.
Player C continues the same pattern back towards the next player.
The group completes continuous clockwise movement for one minute.
Reverse the direction so players use the opposite hand and footwork pattern.
Count consecutive clean handballs while maintaining correct movement and spacing.
coachingPoints: Present a clear two-hand target before the football arrives.
Call the handballer’s name early.
Move only after completing the disposal.
Handball in front of the receiver’s body.
Use the hand that allows the football to move naturally around the triangle.
Accelerate to the next support cone after release.
Maintain the triangle shape and avoid drifting inside.
Reset the football cleanly before each disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the next receiver communicates before the handball.
Whether handballs lead the receiver into the intended direction.
