Whether players leave only after disposal.
Whether the correct hand is used in each direction.
Whether the triangle shape remains consistent.
Whether players arrive at the next cone under control.
Whether football handling remains clean as movement increases.

commonErrors.error: Players leave the cone before completing the handball.
commonErrors.correction: Require the disposal to be finished before movement begins.

commonErrors.error: The handball arrives behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Target the front half of the receiver’s body.

commonErrors.error: Players cut through the centre of the triangle.
commonErrors.correction: Follow the outside line directly to the next cone.

commonErrors.error: Communication is late or absent.
commonErrors.correction: The receiver must call and present before the handballer may release.

commonErrors.error: The same hand is used in both directions.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate the outside striking hand for each direction.

commonErrors.error: The group loses spacing as tempo increases.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the drill and restore the triangle before restarting.

progressions: Reduce the triangle size to increase release speed.
Increase the triangle size to challenge distance control.
Add a second football once movement is stable.
Change direction on a coach call.
Require the receiver to take one step off the cone before presenting.
regressions: Keep players stationary at their cones.
Complete one full lap before introducing follow movement.
successIndicators: Deliver the football accurately around the triangle.
Use the appropriate hand in each direction.
Follow the disposal to the next support position.
Complete extended possession sequences without a fumble.
matchApplication: Australian football possession chains require the handballer to release and then move immediately into a new support position. The triangle introduces basic give-and-go movement, communication and correct hand selection without defensive pressure.

title: Four-Corner Handball Rotation
primarySkill: Handballing accurately within a four-player directional rotation
objective: Develop accurate handballing and immediate support movement within a four-corner possession structure that exposes players to changing receiving and release angles.
groundSize: Squares measuring six metres × six metres, with one square per group of four to eight players.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a six-metre × six-metre square.
Place at least one player at each corner.
Additional players form short queues behind the starting players.
One corner begins with the football.
The first round moves clockwise.
Players follow their disposal to the next corner.
The direction changes after a nominated period.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player at the next corner calls and presents a receiving target.
The ball carrier handballs accurately across the side of the square.
The handballer follows the football to the next corner.
The receiver secures the football, turns the body towards the following corner and releases.
The sequence continues around all four sides of the square.
After one minute, reverse direction.
In the next round, the coach may call “diagonal”, requiring the football to move across the square before returning to normal rotation.
Players must adjust the striking hand according to the direction and target angle.
The group counts complete circuits achieved without a dropped football, inaccurate disposal or incorrect rotation.
coachingPoints: Communicate before the football leaves the previous corner.
Present hands in front of the body.
Receive under control before turning towards the next target.
Use short foot adjustments to align hips and shoulders.
Select the hand that provides the clearest release line.
Handball to the receiver’s front side.
Follow the football after completing the disposal.
Maintain safe spacing and avoid cutting across another player’s path.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players communicate early.
Whether the football is received cleanly at each corner.
Whether players adjust their body before releasing to the next target.
Whether correct hand selection changes with direction.
Whether the handball leads the receiver appropriately.
Whether rotations remain outside the square.
Whether diagonal calls are recognised without creating confusion.

commonErrors.error: The receiver turns before securing the football.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the catch before repositioning the feet.

commonErrors.error: Players run through the middle of the square.
commonErrors.correction: Follow the outside edge to the next corner.

commonErrors.error: Handballs arrive behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Aim at the receiver’s front shoulder or presented hands.

commonErrors.error: Players use the same striking hand at every corner.
commonErrors.correction: Organise the football onto the hand that creates the direct release line.

commonErrors.error: Queues become congested at one cone.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain equal starting numbers and rotate promptly after disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players miss the diagonal instruction.
commonErrors.correction: Require the ball carrier to repeat the coach’s call before releasing.

progressions: Add a second football at the opposite corner.
Reduce the square to five metres × five metres.
Increase the square to eight metres × eight metres.
Change between clockwise, anticlockwise and diagonal movement on live calls.
Require a one-step lead before every receive.
regressions: Keep players stationary at each corner.
Allow dominant-hand disposal throughout the first round.
successIndicators: Align their body with the next target.
Rotate safely and maintain the square structure.
matchApplication: The square introduces repeated changes in receiving and release direction, similar to maintaining possession around congestion or moving the football through multiple supporting players. Players learn that handballing is connected to body alignment, communication and immediate movement.

title: Handball Fundamentals Possession Chain
primarySkill: Combining fundamental handball skills in a continuous unopposed possession chain
objective: Consolidate fundamental handball technique by requiring players to maintain an unopposed possession chain using accurate disposal, appropriate hand selection and immediate support movement.
groundSize: A rectangular area approximately 20 metres long × 15 metres wide.
equipment: Two sets of bibs if using separate groups
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a 20-metre × 15-metre rectangle.
Position players throughout the area with no defenders.
One player begins with the football.
Players may move at jogging pace to create short supporting options.
The ball carrier may take no more than three steps before handballing.
Handballs must travel at least three metres.
After disposing, the player must move to a different support position.
The group attempts to maintain possession for a nominated number of handballs.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier scans and selects a teammate presenting a clear target.
The receiver calls and moves into a visible support position.
The ball carrier handballs accurately using the hand best suited to the target’s position.
The receiver secures the football and may take up to three steps.
The previous ball carrier moves immediately to create another support option.
The group continues until it completes ten consecutive handballs.
If the football is dropped, leaves the area or is disposed of illegally, the count returns to zero.
After achieving ten consecutive handballs, increase the target to fifteen.
The coach may stop the activity to correct spacing, body alignment, hand selection or receiving technique.
Rotate the starting ball carrier after each successful chain.
coachingPoints: Spread throughout the area to create clear passing lanes.
Present a target before calling for the football.
Move towards open space rather than crowding the ball carrier.
Select the striking hand that allows the fastest direct release.
Deliver the football between waist and chest height whenever possible.
Secure possession before accelerating or changing direction.
Move immediately after disposal to provide repeat support.
Maintain legal technique as movement and tempo increase.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players create adequate spacing before possession arrives.
Whether receivers communicate and present a visible target.
Whether the ball carrier selects the appropriate hand.
Whether handballs are directed into a safe receiving area.
Whether players secure the football before moving.
Whether the previous ball carrier provides repeat support.
Whether the group maintains technique while attempting to reach the target count.
Whether players avoid gathering around the football.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Spread to the edges of the area and create different support angles.

commonErrors.error: Receivers call without presenting their hands.
commonErrors.correction: Require a visible target before the ball carrier may release.

commonErrors.error: The football is handballed to a stationary player surrounded by teammates.
commonErrors.correction: Select the player moving into clear space.

commonErrors.error: Players use only their dominant hand.
commonErrors.correction: Use the hand that provides the most direct release line to the target.

commonErrors.error: The previous ball carrier stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Move immediately to a new support position.

commonErrors.error: Players rush and fumble while chasing the target count.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce tempo and rebuild clean receiving and legal disposal.

commonErrors.error: Handballs travel below knee height or above the head.
commonErrors.correction: Target the receiver’s waist-to-chest zone.

progressions: Increase the consecutive-handball target.
Reduce the area to create tighter support spacing.
Limit ball carriers to one step.
Require alternating hands for consecutive disposals.
Add one passive interceptor who may block lanes but not tackle.
Award a bonus when the possession chain uses every player.
regressions: Permit up to five steps before disposal.
Begin with a target of five consecutive handballs.
Use dominant-hand disposal during the first round.
successIndicators: Maintain useful spacing and support angles.
Secure and release the football cleanly.
Use both hands according to the target position.
Complete extended possession chains without technical breakdown.
matchApplication: The drill connects fundamental handball technique to basic team possession. Players learn to spread, present, select the appropriate hand, release accurately and move again—the core behaviours required to maintain possession through congestion and support runners in Australian football.

title: Straight-Line Moving Handball
primarySkill: Executing an accurate handball while jogging forward
objective: Develop the ability to maintain running balance and deliver an accurate handball to a stationary target without stopping, overstriding or losing legal technique.
groundSize: Straight lanes approximately 12 metres long and four metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Establish straight lanes 12 metres long.
Place a starting cone at one end, a release marker six metres from the start and a receiver cone four metres beyond the release marker.
Organise players into groups of three to five.
One receiver stands at the far cone.
The first ball carrier begins at the starting cone.
Remaining players queue safely behind the starting point.
The receiver presents a two-hand target between waist and chest height.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first player begins jogging forward while carrying the football in front of the body.
As the player approaches the release marker, the receiver calls and presents a target.
The ball carrier maintains running rhythm and delivers an accurate handball without stopping.
The handball must be released within one metre of the designated marker.
The ball carrier continues moving after disposal and replaces the receiver.
The receiver collects the football and returns to the starting queue.
Players complete one round using their dominant fist.
Complete a second round using the non-dominant fist.
In the final round, alternate the striking hand after every repetition.
coachingPoints: Carry the football securely in front of the body while moving.
Maintain short, balanced running steps when preparing to handball.
Avoid planting both feet and stopping before release.
Position the football on the supporting hand early.
Keep the head steady and eyes directed towards the receiver.
Time the strike with a natural forward step.
Follow through towards the receiver while continuing to run.
Reduce running speed if legal technique or accuracy deteriorates.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players carry the football securely while jogging.
Whether the support platform is organised before the release marker.
Whether players continue moving during disposal.
Whether the handball reaches the receiver at a catchable height.
Whether the striking action remains legal at running speed.
Whether balance is maintained after release.
Whether both hands can be used effectively.

commonErrors.error: The player stops before handballing.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the running speed and require continuous movement through the release zone.

commonErrors.error: The football moves excessively while running.
commonErrors.correction: Carry it securely in front of the torso and organise the platform earlier.

commonErrors.error: The player overstrides at release.
commonErrors.correction: Use shorter steps approaching the marker.

commonErrors.error: The handball travels behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release slightly earlier and follow through towards the presented hands.

commonErrors.error: The player throws the football while moving.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the action and reinforce a stable supporting hand and clear fist strike.

commonErrors.error: The player loses balance after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest over the hips and continue running in a straight line.

progressions: Increase jogging speed.
Move the receiver one metre laterally before presenting.
Remove the release marker and require players to judge the appropriate release point.
Alternate hands after every repetition.
Increase the handball distance by two metres.
regressions: Allow players to take one stabilising step before release.
Position the receiver closer to the release marker.
successIndicators: Maintain forward movement through the disposal.
Organise the football before reaching the release point.
Continue immediately into the next rotation.
matchApplication: Players often need to carry the football for several steps before releasing a teammate. Maintaining movement during the handball prevents defenders from closing space and allows the possession chain to continue at speed.

title: Handball to a Leading Receiver
primarySkill: Delivering an accurate handball to a moving teammate
objective: Teach players to judge a teammate’s speed and deliver the football into the receiver’s running path rather than directly at their starting position.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 12 metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a ball-carrier cone at one end of the lane.
Position the receiver’s starting cone four metres ahead and two metres to one side.
Place a receiving gate three metres beyond the receiver’s starting cone.
A third player waits behind the receiving gate.
The receiver must move through the gate while calling for the football.
Set up mirrored lanes so players practise leading to both sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver begins beside the lane and waits for the ball carrier to establish possession.
The receiver accelerates through the receiving gate and presents both hands.
The ball carrier judges the lead and handballs into the receiver’s running path.
The receiver catches the football without stopping or reaching behind.
After receiving, the player continues forward and handballs to the waiting player.
The original ball carrier moves to the receiver’s starting cone.
The receiver joins the far queue, and the far player carries the football back to the start.
Complete several repetitions before changing the lead to the opposite side.
Encourage use of the hand that provides the clearest delivery line.
coachingPoints: The receiver should lead with purpose rather than drifting.
Call early enough for the handballer to identify the movement.
Present both hands in front of the torso.
Aim into the receiver’s path, not at the starting cone.
Judge lead speed before selecting handball force.
Release early enough for the receiver to continue running.
Use the striking hand that avoids handballing across the body.
The receiver should secure the football before preparing the next disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver accelerates and presents a clear target.
Whether the handballer looks at the receiver’s movement rather than the cone.
Whether the football is placed in front of the lead.
Whether the receiver catches without stopping.
Whether the correct striking hand is selected.
Whether the second disposal is completed under control.
Whether timing improves across repeated efforts.

commonErrors.error: The handball is directed at the receiver’s starting position.
commonErrors.correction: Aim one to two metres into the receiver’s running path.

commonErrors.error: The receiver leaves before the ball carrier is ready.
commonErrors.correction: Establish eye contact and time the lead from the ball carrier’s possession.

commonErrors.error: The football arrives behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and direct the follow-through ahead of the lead.

commonErrors.error: The receiver slows before catching.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain running speed and present the hands in front.

commonErrors.error: The handball is overhit.
commonErrors.correction: Judge the lead speed and use a controlled, catchable delivery.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier uses the wrong fist and handballs across the torso.
commonErrors.correction: Reorganise onto the hand aligned with the leading side.

progressions: Increase the receiver’s lead speed.
Delay the direction of the lead until the ball carrier is ready.
Add two possible receiving gates.
Require the receiver to handball immediately to the next player.
Increase the distance between ball carrier and receiver.
regressions: Reduce the receiver to a walking lead.
successIndicators: Time the lead and disposal effectively.
Handball into the receiver’s running path.
Allow the receiver to maintain speed.
Select an appropriate hand and force.
Complete the possession chain without a fumble.
Perform the skill to both sides.
matchApplication: A handball should release a teammate into space rather than force them to stop. Correct placement supports overlap running, transition and movement away from congestion while reducing the chance of immediate pressure on the receiver.

title: Run-Past Give-and-Go
primarySkill: Executing a give-and-go handball with a running teammate
objective: Develop coordinated give-and-go movement in which the first player handballs to a runner, accelerates past and receives the football back in space.
groundSize: Straight or slightly angled lanes 15 metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Place Player A at the starting cone with the football.
Player B begins three metres ahead and two metres to the side.
Player C waits at the far cone approximately ten metres away.
Mark a run-past channel outside Player B’s starting position.
Player A and Player B complete the give-and-go before connecting with Player C.
Set up lanes in both directions to practise right- and left-side support.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player B begins moving forward and calls for the football.
Player A handballs to Player B and immediately accelerates past on the outside.
Player B receives, turns slightly towards Player A’s run and returns the football into Player A’s path.
Player A catches while moving and continues towards Player C.
Player A then handballs to Player C.
Player B follows the movement to the far cone.
Player C carries the football back to the starting line.
Players rotate through all roles.
Reverse the run-past side after several repetitions.
The drill continues only when the outgoing lane is clear.
coachingPoints: The runner should communicate before the first disposal.
Player A must accelerate immediately after handballing.
Player B should receive with hands in front and keep the ball available for a quick return.
The return handball should be placed ahead of Player A.
Both players should avoid running on the same line.
Use the hand that releases the football into the runner’s path.
Maintain speed after the second receive.
Complete the final handball under control rather than rushing.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player A accelerates immediately after disposal.
Whether Player B times the support run correctly.
Whether the two players maintain separate running lines.
Whether the return handball leads Player A.
Whether the appropriate hand is used on each side.
Whether the final connection with Player C remains accurate.
Whether rotations occur without collisions or congestion.

commonErrors.error: Player A jogs rather than accelerating after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Make the first three steps after the handball explosive.

commonErrors.error: Player B holds the football too long.
commonErrors.correction: Receive with hands ready and return within one or two steps.

commonErrors.error: Both players run on the same line.
commonErrors.correction: Use the marked outside run-past channel.

commonErrors.error: The return handball goes behind Player A.
commonErrors.correction: Aim ahead of the runner’s chest and release earlier.

commonErrors.error: Player A looks back continuously.
commonErrors.correction: Check the receiver, then run forward and trust the call.

commonErrors.error: Players use only their dominant fist.
commonErrors.correction: Reverse the drill direction and nominate the efficient hand.

progressions: Increase the speed of the run-past.
Add a second give-and-go before the final handball.
Remove the marked channel.
Add a passive defender who tracks the original ball carrier.
Require the return handball to be completed within one step.
regressions: Complete the drill at walking pace.
Allow Player B to remain stationary.
Reduce the distance to Player C.
successIndicators: Return the football in front of the runner.
Complete the three-player possession sequence at speed.
matchApplication: Give-and-go handball allows a player to draw pressure, release a teammate and regain possession in space. It is commonly used to break a defensive line, create overlap or move through congestion without relying on a kick.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver

title: Moving Handball Through Release Gates
primarySkill: Timing a handball while moving through a defined release zone
objective: Develop consistent release timing by requiring players to deliver an accurate handball while running through a designated gate rather than before or after the optimal moment.
groundSize: Straight lanes 15 metres long and five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Mark a starting cone at one end of the lane.
Create a two-metre-long release gate using four cones positioned six metres from the start.
Place a receiver four to five metres beyond the release gate.
Additional players queue at the starting point.
The receiver presents a clear target.
Create mirrored lanes to practise release from each side of the body.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first player begins running with the football.
The receiver calls as the player approaches the release gate.
The ball carrier must complete the handball while their body is within the gate.
The player continues running after disposal and replaces the receiver.
The receiver collects the football and returns to the starting queue.
A successful repetition requires legal technique, release inside the gate and a clean catch.
Complete six repetitions using the dominant hand.
Repeat using the non-dominant hand.
In the final round, the receiver may shift one metre to either side before presenting.
coachingPoints: Organise the support hand before entering the gate.
Keep running rhythm consistent rather than slowing sharply.
Identify the receiver before the release zone.
Use short steps through the gate.
Strike the football while balanced.
Release early enough for the football to reach the receiver in front.
Continue through the gate after disposal.
Do not sacrifice legal technique to meet the timing constraint.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the platform is organised before the gate.
Whether the player releases inside the designated area.
Whether running speed remains controlled.
Whether players shorten their steps near release.
Whether the handball reaches the receiver accurately.
Whether players continue moving after disposal.
Whether both sides can be used without changing the timing.

commonErrors.error: The player organises the football too late.
commonErrors.correction: Move the ball onto the support hand before entering the gate.

commonErrors.error: The handball is released before the gate.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain possession for one additional step and trust the marked zone.

commonErrors.error: The player runs beyond the gate before releasing.
commonErrors.correction: Begin the striking action earlier.

commonErrors.error: The player slows to a stop inside the gate.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce starting speed and maintain continuous movement.

commonErrors.error: The football arrives behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and aim into the receiving path.

commonErrors.error: Technique becomes a throw under the timing demand.
commonErrors.correction: Widen the gate and reduce speed until legal contact is restored.

progressions: Narrow the release gate.
Increase starting speed.
Move the receiver laterally.
Remove the gate after players learn the timing.
Add a visual cue determining the striking hand.
regressions: Widen the release gate to four metres.
Reduce the distance beyond the gate.
successIndicators: Prepare the football before entering the gate.
Release while moving through the correct zone.
matchApplication: Effective handballing depends on releasing at the right moment. Delaying too long invites pressure, while releasing too early may fail to draw an opponent. The gate teaches players to coordinate movement, timing and disposal.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver

title: Crossing Support Handball
primarySkill: Handballing accurately between players crossing on separate running lines
objective: Teach players to exchange the football safely and accurately while crossing paths without drifting into the same running lane.
groundSize: Cross-shaped stations approximately 12 metres × 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark four outside starting cones in a cross formation around a central marker.
Place players in two opposing queues.
Player A begins at the north cone with the football.
Player B begins at the west cone without the football.
Both players run towards separate markers near the centre before continuing diagonally to opposite outside cones.
Running lines must cross visually but remain offset by at least one metre.
The coach demonstrates the safe exchange point before beginning.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A and Player B begin running simultaneously.
Player B calls and presents hands while approaching the exchange zone.
Player A handballs across the body line into Player B’s running path.
Player B receives without changing lane or slowing sharply.
Both players continue to their opposite cones.
The next pair begins once the central area is clear.
Player B carries the football into the next repetition from the new starting side.
Alternate the direction of the crossing pattern.
Players must use the hand that creates the clearest release away from the crossing point.
Stop immediately if running lanes collapse or players enter the same channel.
coachingPoints: Maintain the assigned running line.
Communicate early before entering the exchange zone.
Keep eyes up and recognise the other player’s speed.
Deliver the football in front of the receiver.
Avoid handballing across the receiver’s body.
Use the outside hand where possible.
Continue running after the exchange.
Prioritise spacing and safety over speed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players remain on separate running lines.
Whether communication occurs before the exchange.
Whether the ball carrier identifies the receiver’s speed.
Whether the football is delivered ahead of the receiver.
Whether players avoid turning towards each other.
Whether the correct hand is selected.
Whether the central area is clear before the next pair starts.

commonErrors.error: Players drift into the same running line.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce the offset central markers and require each player to stay outside their marker.

commonErrors.error: The handball arrives behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target the space ahead of the running line.

commonErrors.error: Players watch only the football and risk collision.
commonErrors.correction: Keep peripheral vision on the other runner and the central space.

commonErrors.error: The receiver slows sharply before catching.
commonErrors.correction: Present hands early and trust the handball placement.

commonErrors.error: The next pair starts too soon.
commonErrors.correction: Use a clear coach release call or wait until the middle is empty.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier uses a difficult across-body action.
commonErrors.correction: Select the outside hand and adjust the support platform earlier.

progressions: Increase running speed.
Reduce the width between crossing lanes.
Add a second handball after the players clear the middle.
Allow the receiver to choose between two crossing lines.
Introduce a passive central interceptor.
regressions: Complete the pattern at walking pace.
Increase the separation between running lines.
successIndicators: Maintain safe and separate running lines.
Communicate before entering the crossing area.
Clear the central space before the next repetition.
matchApplication: Players frequently cross, overlap and change lanes during transition. Accurate handballing between crossing runners helps maintain speed while preventing collisions, congestion and disposals that force teammates off their intended line.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver
HB-024 – Moving Handball Through Release Gates

title: Moving Triangle Support Rotation
primarySkill: Maintaining a moving three-player support triangle through repeated handballs
objective: Develop coordinated movement between three players so the ball carrier consistently has two visible handball options while the group advances.
groundSize: Corridors approximately 25 metres long and 12 metres wide.
equipment: One football per group of three
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a 25-metre-long corridor.
Three players begin in a triangle: one central ball carrier and two support players positioned three to four metres to either side and slightly ahead.
The group moves together towards the far end.
Support players must remain on opposite sides of the ball carrier.
A return lane is positioned beside the working corridor.
Groups begin at intervals to preserve space.
howTheDrillWorks:
The three players begin jogging forward while maintaining the triangle.
The ball carrier selects either support player and delivers an accurate handball.
The new ball carrier continues forward.
The player who disposed of the football moves ahead or around to rebuild a support angle.
The third player adjusts to maintain width on the opposite side.
The group continues handballing while advancing through the corridor.
A minimum of six handballs must be completed before reaching the far end.
Players jog back through the return lane.
On the next repetition, begin with a different central ball carrier.
The group restarts if the triangle collapses into a straight line.
coachingPoints: Maintain width on both sides of the ball carrier.
Support slightly ahead rather than directly beside or behind.
Communicate before presenting for the football.
Use the hand that directs the football away from the central congestion line.
The previous ball carrier must move immediately after disposal.
Avoid all three players running at the same speed and depth.
Keep handballs short, firm and catchable.
Adjust speed to preserve the support triangle.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether two clear support options remain available.
Whether players preserve width while moving.
Whether the previous ball carrier replaces into a new angle.
Whether handball selection matches the support side.
Whether players communicate before receiving.
Whether the group advances without stopping.
Whether the shape becomes a straight line under speed.

commonErrors.error: The three players form a straight line.
commonErrors.correction: Move support players wider and slightly ahead of the ball carrier.

commonErrors.error: The previous handballer stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately into the vacant support position.

commonErrors.error: Both support players move to the same side.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one player on each side of the corridor.

commonErrors.error: Handballs force receivers backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Lead the support player into forward space.

commonErrors.error: The group moves too quickly and loses shape.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed until spacing and angles are restored.

commonErrors.error: Players call without showing a target.
commonErrors.correction: Present hands and establish eye contact before release.

progressions: Increase corridor length.
Limit the ball carrier to two steps.
Require alternating left- and right-side handballs.
Add a passive central defender.
Finish with a handball through a target gate.
regressions: Complete the drill at walking pace.
Use fixed side lanes for the support players.
Allow the ball carrier up to five steps.
successIndicators: Use both sides of the corridor.
Advance through the full corridor without losing shape.
matchApplication: A moving support triangle provides the ball carrier with multiple options and reduces predictability. This structure is important when exiting congestion, advancing through the corridor or supporting a teammate during transition.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver

title: Handball-and-Follow Corridor Chain
primarySkill: Handballing and immediately following to support the next possession
objective: Develop a continuous forward handball chain in which every player follows their disposal and becomes an active support option further along the corridor.
groundSize: A corridor approximately 30 metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark two parallel lines of cones through a 30-metre corridor.
Place one player at each cone, staggered from left to right.
Additional players queue at the starting cone.
One football begins at the first cone.
A second football may be introduced only after the group establishes safe spacing.
Players follow their handball to the receiving cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first player handballs to the next player positioned diagonally ahead.
The handballer immediately follows the disposal to that cone.
The receiver secures the football, turns towards the next player and handballs forward.
The receiver then follows to the next cone.
The football continues through every station in the corridor.
The final player carries the football through a return lane to the starting queue.
Players use the hand aligned with the direction of the next target.
After several repetitions, reverse the staggered direction.
Introduce a second football when the first football is halfway through the corridor.
Stop and reset if players overtake the football or enter the wrong lane.
coachingPoints: Present a target before the previous player releases.
Receive in front of the body.
Turn the feet and hips towards the next target.
Use the hand that creates a direct forward release.
Follow immediately after disposal.
Maintain spacing between consecutive players.
Keep the football moving forward rather than across or backwards.
Preserve technique when the second football is introduced.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the next player presents early.
Whether the football is received cleanly.
Whether the receiver aligns with the following target.
Whether the disposal travels forward into the next player’s hands.
Whether the handballer follows promptly.
Whether the sequence remains spaced with two footballs.
Whether players use both hands as the stagger changes.

commonErrors.error: Players wait after handballing.
commonErrors.correction: Follow the football immediately to the receiving cone.

commonErrors.error: The receiver faces the previous player for too long.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession, then turn the feet towards the next target.

commonErrors.error: Handballs travel sideways rather than forward.
commonErrors.correction: Aim at the front half of the next player’s body.

commonErrors.error: Players arrive at the next cone before it is clear.
commonErrors.correction: Control running speed and maintain one-station spacing.

commonErrors.error: The second football catches the first sequence.
commonErrors.correction: Delay its introduction or increase corridor spacing.

commonErrors.error: Players use awkward across-body handballs.
commonErrors.correction: Select the hand aligned with the diagonal direction.

progressions: Introduce a second football.
Increase the running speed between cones.
Reduce time permitted at each station.
Remove selected cones and require players to judge support spacing.
Finish with a moving receiver beyond the final cone.
regressions: Increase the distance between starting groups.
successIndicators: Turn efficiently towards the next target.
matchApplication: Handball chains succeed when players continue to support after releasing the football. Following the disposal creates repeat options, maintains numerical advantage and keeps the ball moving forward through pressure.

title: Lateral Shuffle Handball
primarySkill: Handballing accurately while moving laterally
objective: Develop the ability to move sideways, remain balanced and handball accurately without crossing the feet or turning completely away from the target.
groundSize: Pairs operate in lanes eight metres long and five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Players form pairs facing each other four metres apart.
Mark a lateral movement line four to six metres long for each player.
Both players begin at the same end of their lines.
One player starts with the football.
Players shuffle laterally in the same direction while exchanging handballs.
The direction reverses when both players reach the far cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both players begin shuffling laterally while keeping their chest generally facing the partner.
The ball carrier delivers an accurate handball while moving.
The receiver catches and returns the football after one or two shuffle steps.
Players continue exchanging the football while travelling to the far cone.
At the cone, both players stop under control and reverse direction.
Complete one round using the hand most naturally aligned with the movement.
Complete another round using the opposite hand.
In the final round, alternate hands after every exchange.
Players restart if either crosses their feet or leaves the movement lane.
coachingPoints: Use short lateral steps and keep the feet from crossing.
Maintain a low, balanced body position.
Keep the chest sufficiently open to see the partner.
Carry the football in front of the body.
Organise the support hand early.
Handball towards the partner’s torso, not towards the direction of travel.
Continue moving after release.
Control the change of direction at each end.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players use balanced lateral footwork.
Whether the feet remain separated without crossing.
Whether players can see the partner throughout the movement.
Whether handball accuracy remains consistent.
Whether the ball is kept in front of the torso.
Whether the reversal is controlled.
Whether both hands can be used while moving each direction.

commonErrors.error: The player crosses the feet.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and use shorter shuffle steps.

commonErrors.error: The torso turns fully towards the movement direction.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest open towards the partner.

commonErrors.error: The football is carried beside the hip.
commonErrors.correction: Hold it securely in front of the body.

commonErrors.error: Handballs drift in the direction of travel.
commonErrors.correction: Follow through towards the partner’s chest.

commonErrors.error: Players stop before every disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a continuous shuffle at reduced speed.

commonErrors.error: The direction change is uncontrolled.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the centre of gravity and plant the outside foot before reversing.

progressions: Increase shuffle speed.
Reduce the distance between partners.
Add a high or low target call.
Change direction on a whistle rather than at the cone.
Introduce a second football for advanced pairs.
regressions: Allow a brief pause before release.
Increase partner distance to reduce exchange speed.
matchApplication: Players often move laterally around a stoppage, defensive exit or congestion area while looking for a release option. Balanced sideways movement allows them to preserve vision and handball accurately without exposing the football.
relatedDrills: HB-024 – Moving Handball Through Release Gates

title: Retreat-and-Release Support Handball
primarySkill: Receiving while retreating and releasing to a forward-facing teammate
objective: Teach players to receive while moving away from congestion, regain a balanced forward-facing position and release accurately to a supporting teammate.
groundSize: Stations approximately 12 metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Player A begins with the football at the starting cone.
Player B begins three metres ahead, facing Player A.
Player C stands four metres beyond Player B and slightly to one side.
A retreat line is marked behind Player B.
Player B must move backwards along the line before receiving.
The station is mirrored so the final release can be practised to both sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player B begins retreating with short, controlled backward steps.
Player A handballs to Player B’s presented hands.
Player B receives while moving backwards and secures the football.
Player B plants under control, turns the feet and hips towards Player C and regains forward balance.
Player B handballs accurately to Player C.
Player A moves into Player B’s role.
Player B follows the disposal to Player C.
Player C carries the football back to the start.
Change the final target side after several repetitions.
Players must not continue running backwards after losing sight of the space behind them.
coachingPoints: Use short backward steps and keep the body balanced.
Scan the retreat space before moving.
Present both hands early.
Secure the football before changing direction.
Plant under control rather than leaning backwards.
Turn the feet and hips towards the next receiver.
Keep the football in front of the torso.
Use the hand aligned with the final target.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player B checks the retreat space.
Whether backward movement remains controlled.
Whether the football is caught cleanly.
Whether the player establishes balance before turning.
Whether feet and hips realign with Player C.
Whether the final handball is accurate.
Whether players use both release sides competently.

commonErrors.error: The player takes long backward steps and loses balance.
commonErrors.correction: Use shorter steps with the chest over the hips.

commonErrors.error: The receiver does not check the space behind.
commonErrors.correction: Require a shoulder scan before movement begins.

commonErrors.error: The player turns before securing the football.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the catch with two hands before planting and rotating.

commonErrors.error: The player leans backwards during the handball.
commonErrors.correction: Regain a forward-balanced stance before release.

commonErrors.error: The football is moved behind the body during the turn.
commonErrors.correction: Keep it in front and turn the feet around the ball.

commonErrors.error: The final handball travels across the body.
commonErrors.correction: Select the hand that aligns directly with Player C.

progressions: Increase the retreat distance.
Move Player C after Player B receives.
Add a late left or right target call.
Require the final release within two steps.
Add passive pressure approaching from Player A after the initial handball.
regressions: Allow Player B to stop before receiving.
Reduce the distance to Player C.
successIndicators: Realign efficiently with the next target.
matchApplication: Players may need to retreat from a contest to create separation before connecting with support. Controlled backward movement and quick reorientation allow possession to be retained without blindly turning or disposing while off balance.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver

title: Moving Handball Competency Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing handball competency while moving and supporting
objective: Assess each player’s ability to handball legally and accurately while moving, deliver to a moving receiver and provide effective support after disposal.
groundSize: Four assessment stations arranged within an area approximately 35 metres × 25 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Establish four assessment stations:
Station 1: Straight-line moving handball through a release zone.
Station 2: Handball to a receiver leading to the right and left.
Station 3: Run-past give-and-go.
Station 4: Moving support triangle.
Organise players into groups and assign one coach or observer to each station where possible.
Each player receives a defined number of assessed repetitions.
Dominant- and non-dominant-hand results are recorded separately.
Explain the assessment criteria before rotations begin.
Allow one practice repetition at each station before scoring starts.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, each player completes three moving handballs with each fist while remaining inside the release zone.
At Station 2, each player completes two handballs to a receiver leading right and two leading left.
At Station 3, each player performs two give-and-go sequences on each side.
At Station 4, each player completes one full corridor as part of a moving three-player support triangle.
Observers score legal technique, accuracy, movement balance and support behaviour.
Players rotate after every member of the group has completed the station.
Technical errors are recorded without stopping the assessment unless safety or legality requires intervention.
At completion, each player receives one movement-handball strength and one priority for improvement.
Players repeat the station linked to their lowest score.
Coaches retain the results for later comparison and progression planning.
coachingPoints: Apply the same legal handball standard at every station.
Assess whether the player remains balanced before, during and after release.
Judge moving-target handballs by whether they allow the receiver to maintain speed.
Record dominant- and non-dominant-side competency separately.
Observe whether the player moves immediately after disposal.
Assess communication and target presentation, not only the handball itself.
Distinguish technical failure from poor timing or spacing.
Provide specific feedback linked to an observable action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players can organise the football while moving.
Whether the handball remains legal at increased speed.
Whether receivers are led into space.
Whether the player maintains running balance.
Whether both fists are used competently.
Whether the player accelerates or repositions after disposal.
Whether support shape remains effective.
Whether feedback is applied during the repeat station.

commonErrors.error: The player stops before every handball.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce running speed and require continuous movement through the release.

commonErrors.error: Moving-target handballs arrive behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and aim into the runner’s path.

commonErrors.error: Technique becomes a throw at speed.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and rebuild the stable platform and clear fist strike.

commonErrors.error: The player uses only the dominant fist.
commonErrors.correction: Repeat the relevant station with mandatory non-dominant disposal.

commonErrors.error: The player does not move after handballing.
commonErrors.correction: Add an assessed support action after every disposal.

commonErrors.error: The player loses balance during direction changes.
commonErrors.correction: Use shorter steps and realign the feet before release.

commonErrors.error: Support players collapse into one line.
commonErrors.correction: Restore width and depth before continuing the assessment.

progressions: Reduce the permitted release time.
Increase receiver speed.
Add a passive defender at selected stations.
Narrow the target gates.
Require the moving triangle to complete more disposals.
Compare scores across repeated assessments.
regressions: Assess stations separately across multiple sessions.
successIndicators: Deliver accurately to stationary and moving targets.
Use both hands according to the movement direction.
Apply coaching feedback during the repeat station.
matchApplication: Moving handball competency is essential for transition, overlap, stoppage exits and possession chains. The assessment identifies whether players can transfer stationary technique into realistic movement without losing accuracy, balance or support behaviour.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver
HB-024 – Moving Handball Through Release Gates

title: Receive at Speed and Release Forward
primarySkill: Receiving and handballing while maintaining forward running speed
objective: Develop the ability to receive the football at running speed, organise it efficiently and release accurately to a teammate positioned further forward.
groundSize: Straight lanes approximately 20 metres long and five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a starting cone, two receiving cones and a finishing cone in a straight line.
Position Player A with the football at the starting cone.
Player B begins five metres ahead and starts moving forward before receiving.
Player C begins a further five metres ahead.
Player D waits at the finishing cone.
Players follow their disposal to the next position.
Establish a return lane outside the working corridor.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player B begins running forward and calls for the football.
Player A handballs into Player B’s running path.
Player B receives with two hands while maintaining forward momentum.
Player B organises the football onto the supporting hand within two or three running steps.
Player C begins moving and presents a target.
Player B handballs forward to Player C without stopping.
Player C repeats the action to Player D.
Players follow their disposal to the next station.
Player D carries the football through the return lane to the starting queue.
Reverse the preferred handball side after several repetitions.
coachingPoints: Receivers should accelerate before the football arrives.
Present both hands in front of the body.
Handball into the receiver’s forward running path.
Cushion the football into the hands without trapping it against the chest.
Organise the football quickly while maintaining running rhythm.
Avoid taking excessively long steps before release.
Keep the head up to identify the next target.
Continue moving after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players begin moving before the handball is delivered.
Whether the football is placed in front of the receiver.
Whether receivers maintain speed through the catch.
Whether the football is organised without unnecessary handling.
Whether players release accurately while still moving.
Whether the next target is identified early.
Whether rotation movement remains safe and continuous.

commonErrors.error: The receiver waits stationary for the football.
commonErrors.correction: Begin the lead earlier and receive while accelerating through the cone.

commonErrors.error: The football arrives behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and aim into the player’s forward path.

commonErrors.error: The receiver traps the football against the chest.
commonErrors.correction: Present both hands and cushion the ball in front of the torso.

commonErrors.error: The player stops before the next handball.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce running speed and maintain continuous movement through release.

commonErrors.error: The football is handled several times before disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer directly from the catch onto the supporting hand.

commonErrors.error: The next receiver begins too early and becomes too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Time the lead from the previous player’s clean possession.

progressions: Increase running speed.
Limit players to two steps between receiving and releasing.
Move receiving cones laterally to create angled releases.
Add a second football once spacing is established.
Require alternating striking hands.
regressions: Complete the drill at jogging pace.
Allow receivers to slow before disposal.
Use only two moving receivers before the finish.
successIndicators: Deliver accurately to the next moving target.
Use both hands according to the release angle.
Continue into the next support position.
matchApplication: Players frequently receive a handball during transition and must move the football forward before pressure arrives. Clean receiving and rapid release at speed allow teams to preserve overlap and attack space before defenders can reset.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver

title: Change-of-Direction Handball
primarySkill: Handballing accurately after changing running direction
objective: Develop the ability to decelerate, change direction and deliver an accurate handball from a balanced body position.
groundSize: Stations approximately 12 metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Place a starting cone with the football.
Position a change-of-direction cone five metres ahead.
Place one receiver four metres to the left and another four metres to the right of the change cone.
The ball carrier begins by running towards the central cone.
The coach calls “left” or “right” as the player approaches.
Receivers remain behind their cones and present a clear target.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier runs towards the central cone.
The coach calls the release direction.
The player shortens their steps and lowers the centre of gravity.
The player plants outside the cone and redirects the feet and hips towards the nominated receiver.
The football is positioned on the appropriate supporting hand.
The player completes an accurate handball to the receiver.
The ball carrier follows the disposal to the receiver’s cone.
The receiver carries the football back to the starting queue.
Rotate the two receiver positions regularly.
Complete equal repetitions changing direction to both sides.
coachingPoints: Approach the cone under control.
Shorten the final steps before changing direction.
Plant with the outside foot and keep the knee aligned.
Turn the feet, hips and shoulders towards the target.
Keep the football secure and in front of the body.
Regain balance before striking.
Use the hand that creates the clearest release line.
Accelerate after disposal rather than remaining at the cone.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player controls speed before the direction change.
Whether the plant foot remains stable.
Whether the hips and shoulders turn towards the receiver.
Whether the football stays in front of the torso.
Whether the handball is released from balance.
Whether the correct hand is selected.
Whether the player accelerates after disposal.

commonErrors.error: The player approaches too quickly and slips past the cone.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed earlier and use shorter final steps.

commonErrors.error: The player plants with a straight, locked leg.
commonErrors.correction: Flex the knee and lower the centre of gravity.

commonErrors.error: The torso twists while the feet remain facing forward.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition the feet and hips before beginning the handball.

commonErrors.error: The player handballs while falling sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the direction change and regain balance before release.

commonErrors.error: The football is carried away from the body.
commonErrors.correction: Keep it secure in front during deceleration and turning.

commonErrors.error: The same hand is used for both directions.
commonErrors.correction: Select the hand aligned with the receiver and protected side.

progressions: Make the direction call later.
Increase approach speed.
Move receivers after the call.
Require the handball within two steps of the direction change.
Add a passive chaser behind the ball carrier.
regressions: Complete the approach at walking pace.
Allow a full stop before handballing.
Use only the player’s preferred change-of-direction side.
successIndicators: Realign the body with the target.
Perform the skill in both directions.
matchApplication: Players regularly change direction to avoid congestion, respond to support movement or escape a closing defender. Maintaining balance through the turn allows the football to be released accurately without creating an illegal or uncontrolled disposal.
relatedDrills: HB-024 – Moving Handball Through Release Gates
HB-031 – Receive at Speed and Release Forward

title: Three-Player Handball Weave
primarySkill: Handballing and crossing behind the receiver in a continuous weave
objective: Develop coordinated handball movement in which players release the football, cross behind the receiver and rebuild the next support option while advancing.
groundSize: Corridors approximately 25 metres long and 12 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a corridor 25 metres long and 12 metres wide.
Three players begin across the width of the corridor.
The central player starts with the football.
Outside players begin slightly ahead.
After each handball, the disposing player crosses behind the receiver and moves to the opposite outside lane.
Groups begin at safe intervals.
howTheDrillWorks:
The central player handballs to one outside player.
Immediately after disposal, the handballer crosses behind the receiver.
The receiver continues forward and becomes the new central ball carrier.
The third player adjusts forward and wide to provide the next option.
The new ball carrier handballs to the opposite outside player.
The disposing player again crosses behind the receiver.
The group continues weaving through the corridor.
Complete at least six handballs before reaching the far end.
Players return through an outside recovery lane.
Change the starting handball direction on each repetition.
coachingPoints: Outside players should remain slightly ahead of the ball carrier.
The receiver must call and present before the disposal.
Handball to the receiver’s inside shoulder or front hands.
Cross behind the receiver, never in front.
Maintain width after completing the crossover.
Use the hand aligned with the receiving lane.
Keep running speed controlled enough to preserve spacing.
Continue forward throughout the weave.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether support players remain slightly ahead.
Whether the handball is directed into the receiver’s path.
Whether the disposing player crosses safely behind.
Whether players maintain separate running lanes.
Whether the group preserves width and forward movement.
Whether both hands are used naturally.
Whether communication remains continuous.

commonErrors.error: The disposing player crosses in front of the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Move behind the receiver immediately after release.

commonErrors.error: Players collapse into the central lane.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish wide outside positions after each crossover.

commonErrors.error: The receiver is stationary when the football arrives.
commonErrors.correction: Begin moving and present while slightly ahead.

commonErrors.error: Handballs travel behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and aim at the front shoulder.

commonErrors.error: The group runs too quickly and loses the pattern.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed until spacing and crossing order are correct.

commonErrors.error: Players watch the football and collide.
commonErrors.correction: Keep peripheral vision on running lanes and teammates.

progressions: Increase the corridor length.
Increase running speed.
Limit ball carriers to two steps.
Add a passive chaser behind the group.
Finish with a handball through a target gate.
regressions: Complete the weave at walking pace.
Allow players to pause after each handball.
successIndicators: Present ahead of the ball carrier.
Handball accurately into the running path.
matchApplication: The weave develops the movement habits needed to maintain numerical advantage through overlap. Players learn to dispose, clear the ball carrier’s line and reappear as a new support option without creating congestion.
relatedDrills: HB-031 – Receive at Speed and Release Forward

title: Inside-Outside Support Exchange
primarySkill: Selecting and connecting between inside and outside support options
objective: Teach ball carriers to recognise whether inside or outside support provides the safer forward handball option while all players remain in motion.
groundSize: Corridors approximately 25 metres long and 15 metres wide, divided into one central lane and two outside lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark one central lane and two outside lanes through the corridor.
One ball carrier begins in the central lane.
One inside-support player runs slightly ahead in the central lane.
Two outside-support players begin wider and slightly ahead.
A finishing player waits at the far end.
The coach nominates whether the first release must go inside or outside.
Later rounds allow the ball carrier to choose.
howTheDrillWorks:
All support players begin moving forward.
The ball carrier scans the inside and outside options.
During the controlled round, the coach calls “inside” or “outside”.
The ball carrier selects the matching teammate and handballs into their path.
The new ball carrier continues forward and selects the next available support option.
Players who do not receive adjust their depth and width to remain available.
The group completes three to five handballs before connecting with the finishing player.
Players rotate positions after each repetition.
In the decision round, remove the coach call and allow the ball carrier to select.
The group must maintain lane spacing throughout the activity.
coachingPoints: Scan all available support positions before release.
Inside support should remain close enough for a quick release.
Outside support should maintain width and forward momentum.
Avoid handballing to a player occupying the same running line.
Use the hand that directs the football away from congestion.
Lead receivers into space.
Non-receivers must continue adjusting rather than becoming spectators.
Preserve forward movement without forcing the disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier scans both support sides.
Whether inside and outside players maintain distinct lanes.
Whether receivers remain slightly ahead.
Whether the appropriate striking hand is selected.
Whether the football is delivered into space.
Whether non-receivers continue to support.
Whether lane spacing survives multiple handballs.

commonErrors.error: All support players move towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one inside option and clear outside width.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier looks only to the dominant-hand side.
commonErrors.correction: Require a scan of both shoulders before disposal.

commonErrors.error: The receiver is on the same line as the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust laterally to create a visible passing lane.

commonErrors.error: Handballs force outside runners back towards congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Lead them further into the wide lane.

commonErrors.error: Non-receivers stop running.
commonErrors.correction: Continue adjusting depth and prepare for the next possession.

commonErrors.error: Players force an inside handball when the lane is closed.
commonErrors.correction: Hold possession briefly or select the safer outside option.

progressions: Remove coach calls and use live player choice.
Add a passive defender in the central lane.
Limit each ball carrier to two steps.
Award bonus points for using both inside and outside support.
Narrow the central lane to increase outside use.
regressions: Use only one inside and one outside option.
Allow up to five steps before disposal.
successIndicators: Use the hand suited to the release direction.
matchApplication: Effective transition requires players to balance direct inside support with wider outside options. The ability to recognise the safer lane helps teams avoid congestion while still moving the football forward.
relatedDrills: HB-031 – Receive at Speed and Release Forward

title: Handball Square with Moving Choice
primarySkill: Selecting between two moving handball options
objective: Develop the ability to scan, select and accurately handball to one of two moving teammates presenting from different directions.
groundSize: Squares measuring approximately 12 metres × 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a 12-metre × 12-metre square.
One player begins with the football at the centre.
One player stands at each corner.
Two opposite corner players become active receivers.
Active receivers lead along the outside edges of the square.
The central ball carrier must select one receiver.
The other two corner players act as return feeders and rotation points.
howTheDrillWorks:
Two active receivers begin moving along separate edges of the square.
Both players call and present a target.
The central ball carrier scans both options.
The ball carrier selects one receiver and handballs into their path.
The selected receiver catches and handballs to the nearest corner player.
The non-selected receiver continues to the next corner and resets.
The central ball carrier replaces the selected receiver.
The receiving player moves into the central position for the next repetition.
Rotate active receiver pairings regularly.
The coach may use coloured cues to determine which option becomes available.
coachingPoints: Scan both options before beginning the handball action.
Identify receiver speed, angle and available space.
Keep the football in front while turning between targets.
Select the hand aligned with the chosen option.
Deliver in front of the receiver.
Do not delay once the safer option is identified.
Non-selected receivers should complete their movement and reset.
Maintain clear communication without demanding the football when poorly positioned.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier scans both receivers.
Whether the selected option is moving into clear space.
Whether body alignment changes efficiently.
Whether the correct hand is used.
Whether the handball leads the receiver.
Whether non-selected players maintain movement.
Whether decisions become faster without reducing accuracy.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier locks onto the first receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Require a visible scan to both sides before release.

commonErrors.error: The player changes decisions during the striking action.
commonErrors.correction: Select the option first, then commit to the disposal.

commonErrors.error: The football arrives behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target the space ahead.

commonErrors.error: Both receivers run into the same area.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain separate outside edges and starting corners.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier uses an across-body handball.
commonErrors.correction: Reorganise the support hand and align with the selected target.

commonErrors.error: The non-selected receiver stops immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the lead and reset at the next corner.

progressions: Add a passive central defender.
Make receiver movements less predictable.
Reduce decision time.
Allow all four corner players to become possible receivers.
Award points for selecting the option with the most space.
regressions: Use one active receiver at a time.
Allow the ball carrier to turn fully before disposal.
successIndicators: Deliver into the receiver’s running path.
matchApplication: Ball carriers are frequently presented with more than one handball option. Effective players scan, compare space and pressure, then commit to the option that best maintains possession and forward movement.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver

title: Inside Support Handball Release
primarySkill: Using a short inside handball to release a close supporting teammate
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and use a close inside support option with a short, controlled handball that allows the receiver to continue forward.
groundSize: Corridors approximately 20 metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a narrow forward corridor.
Player A begins with the football.
Player B starts two metres behind and to the inside of Player A.
Player C waits further forward.
Player B runs past on the inside shoulder.
Player A must release with a short handball into Player B’s path.
Player D waits at the far end to continue the rotation.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A begins jogging forward with the football.
Player B accelerates from behind and calls on the inside.
Player A protects the football on the outside side of the body.
Player A delivers a short handball into Player B’s forward path.
Player B receives and continues running.
Player A accelerates to become a repeat support option.
Player B handballs to Player C or returns to Player A according to the coach’s nominated pattern.
The group completes the corridor and rotates.
Change the inside support side after several repetitions.
Maintain short handball distance and separate running lines.
coachingPoints: The support runner should begin from behind the ball carrier.
Call early and accelerate through the inside shoulder.
The ball carrier should protect the football away from the support line.
Use a soft but direct handball over the short distance.
Place the football in front of the receiver.
Avoid releasing so early that the support runner has not reached the ball carrier.
The original ball carrier must continue as repeat support.
Keep the two running lines separate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the support runner begins behind the ball carrier.
Whether the run reaches the inside shoulder.
Whether the ball carrier keeps the football protected.
Whether the handball force suits the short distance.
Whether the receiver maintains forward speed.
Whether the original ball carrier provides repeat support.
Whether the drill is completed on both sides.

commonErrors.error: The support runner begins ahead of the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Start behind and accelerate past the inside shoulder.

commonErrors.error: The handball is struck too hard.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the striking action and use controlled force.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier exposes the football towards the support side.
commonErrors.correction: Hold it on the outside protected side until release.

commonErrors.error: The handball arrives behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Delay slightly and place the ball in front of the lead.

commonErrors.error: Both players run on the same line.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a distinct inside support lane.

commonErrors.error: The original ball carrier stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately to provide a return option.

progressions: Allow Player B to choose between continuing forward and returning the football.
Add a passive outside defender.
Reduce the width of the corridor.
Require the first handball within a two-metre zone.
Increase running speed.
regressions: Allow Player B to begin beside the ball carrier.
Use the preferred support side only.
matchApplication: Close inside support is essential around contests and during transition. A well-timed short handball can release a teammate through the corridor while allowing the original ball carrier to continue as an overlap option.

title: Outside Release Handball
primarySkill: Releasing a wider outside runner with an accurate handball
objective: Develop the ability to identify and release a wider outside runner with a firm, accurate handball that preserves width and forward momentum.
groundSize: Corridors approximately 25 metres long and 15 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a central running lane and one wide outside lane.
Player A begins in the central lane with the football.
Player B begins five metres wider and slightly behind.
Player C begins further forward in the central lane.
Player D waits at the far end.
Player B accelerates into the outside lane.
Mirror the drill to practise release to both wings.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A carries the football forward through the central lane.
Player B accelerates outside and calls for the release.
Player A scans, turns the hips slightly and handballs into Player B’s running path.
Player B receives while maintaining width.
Player A continues forward through the centre as an inside support option.
Player B handballs inside to Player C or continues to Player D according to the set pattern.
Players follow their disposal and rotate.
Complete several repetitions on one side.
Mirror the drill to the opposite side.
Later rounds allow Player B to vary the depth of the outside run.
coachingPoints: The outside runner should hold width rather than drifting towards the ball.
Begin the run from slightly behind the ball carrier.
The ball carrier must scan wide before pressure would close the lane.
Use sufficient body contribution to reach the wider target.
Lead the receiver into the outside lane.
Avoid high, looping handballs.
The central player should continue forward after release.
Use both hands according to the release side.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the outside runner maintains width.
Whether the ball carrier recognises the option early.
Whether the handball has sufficient distance and direct flight.
Whether the receiver continues forward.
Whether the central support remains active.
Whether the correct hand is used.
Whether the drill transfers equally to both sides.

commonErrors.error: The outside runner drifts into the central lane.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the marked wide channel throughout the lead.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier sees the option too late.
commonErrors.correction: Scan outside before reaching the release marker.

commonErrors.error: The handball loops and allows pressure to close.
commonErrors.correction: Use stronger body contribution and a direct follow-through.

commonErrors.error: The football falls short of the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release with greater weight transfer and complete the strike.

commonErrors.error: The handball forces the runner back inside.
commonErrors.correction: Aim further into the outside running lane.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue forward as the next inside support option.

progressions: Increase the width of the outside lane.
Remove the fixed return pattern.
Add a passive central defender.
Require the outside receiver to make the next decision.
Increase the running speed.
regressions: Begin the outside runner beside the ball carrier.
Use the dominant release side only.
successIndicators: Complete the possession chain without slowing.
matchApplication: Outside handball releases help teams escape congestion and use width during transition. Accurate delivery allows the wide runner to maintain speed and forces defenders to spread away from the central corridor.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver

title: Three-Lane Transition Handball
primarySkill: Advancing the football through coordinated handball movement across three lanes
objective: Develop coordinated transition in which players maintain central and outside lanes while advancing the football through repeated moving handballs.
groundSize: A corridor approximately 35 metres long and 18 metres wide, divided into three lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide the corridor into a central lane and two outside lanes.
Six players begin as a transition group, with two players in each lane.
The football starts with one of the rear central players.
Front players begin slightly ahead.
Players may exchange positions within their lane but may not cross lanes during the first version.
A return lane is established outside the working area.
Start groups at safe intervals.
howTheDrillWorks:
The transition group begins moving forward together.
The ball carrier selects a teammate in the same or adjacent lane.
The football is handballed into the receiver’s forward path.
The player who disposes accelerates to provide repeat support.
Players without the football adjust their depth to remain available.
The group must use all three lanes before reaching the far end.
Complete a minimum of eight handballs during the transition.
The final handball must be received inside a marked scoring gate.
