Players return outside the corridor.
Rotate starting lane and ball carrier on each repetition.
coachingPoints: Maintain the width of all three lanes.
Support players should remain at different depths.
Scan inside and outside before disposal.
Avoid handballing to a teammate on the same line and depth.
Use the hand that directs the football into the receiving lane.
Lead receivers forward.
Move immediately after disposal.
Control team speed so the rear players remain connected.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain their lane.
Whether support options exist at different depths.
Whether the football moves across all three lanes.
Whether handballs preserve forward momentum.
Whether players reposition after disposal.
Whether the group remains connected from front to rear.
Whether both hands are used according to lane direction.

commonErrors.error: Players collapse into the central lane.
commonErrors.correction: Return to marked lanes and maintain outside width.

commonErrors.error: All players run at the same depth.
commonErrors.correction: Create one short, one level and one forward support option.

commonErrors.error: The football is handballed sideways without advancing.
commonErrors.correction: Select receivers positioned slightly forward.

commonErrors.error: Front players move too far ahead.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and remain connected to the ball carrier.

commonErrors.error: The disposing player stops.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate into the next available support position.

commonErrors.error: The same side is used repeatedly.
commonErrors.correction: Require the football to visit all three lanes.

progressions: Allow players to change lanes after disposal.
Reduce the corridor width.
Limit ball carriers to two steps.
Add one passive interceptor.
Score bonus points for a clean transition using both outside lanes.
regressions: Reduce the group to four players.
successIndicators: Reach the finishing gate without slowing or fumbling.
matchApplication: Three-lane transition reflects the need to maintain corridor access while also using outside width. Coordinated handball movement can move the football rapidly from defence into attack before the opposition establishes structure.

title: Continuous End-to-End Handball Wave
primarySkill: Maintaining repeated handball movement in continuous transition waves
objective: Develop continuous handball transition in which players advance, support, finish the possession chain and reorganise immediately for the return wave.
groundSize: A rectangular area approximately 45 metres long and 25 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a long rectangular transition area.
Divide players into two groups positioned at opposite ends.
One group begins with the football.
Four to six players enter the area as the active handball wave.
The opposite group prepares to receive the final handball and transition back.
Mark wide, central and finishing channels.
Establish external recovery lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first group enters the area with the football.
Players spread into central and outside support positions.
The group advances using a minimum of six handballs.
Every player must either receive or provide a visible support option.
The final handball is delivered to a player from the opposite group entering through the finishing gate.
That group immediately begins the return transition in the opposite direction.
The original group exits through the recovery lanes and joins the far queue.
Waves continue without a full stoppage.
The coach restarts the count after a dropped football, illegal disposal or loss of spacing.
Work periods last two to three minutes before structured recovery.
coachingPoints: Spread immediately as the wave begins.
Maintain inside and outside support options.
Handball in front of moving teammates.
Move after every disposal.
Communicate before receiving.
Avoid running behind the ball carrier at the same speed and depth.
Finish the wave with a controlled connection to the next group.
Preserve technique as fatigue increases.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the group spreads quickly.
Whether support options remain available throughout the wave.
Whether handballs lead receivers forward.
Whether players work again after disposal.
Whether the finishing connection is controlled.
Whether the next group begins at the correct time.
Whether technique deteriorates under repeated efforts.

commonErrors.error: Players begin in a tight cluster.
commonErrors.correction: Spread into central and outside lanes before the first handball.

commonErrors.error: Support players remain behind the ball.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate to level with or ahead of the ball carrier.

commonErrors.error: The final handball is rushed or inaccurate.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the final two steps and connect cleanly with the next wave.

commonErrors.error: The returning group enters too early.
commonErrors.correction: Wait until the football reaches the finishing zone.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Continue running to create a second support option.

commonErrors.error: Technique becomes a throw under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce wave duration and restore legal striking action.

progressions: Reduce the recovery between waves.
Limit each player to two steps.
Add a passive interceptor.
Require the football to use both outside lanes.
Introduce a second football once timing is stable.
regressions: Use one direction only before resetting.
Reduce the number of players in each wave.
successIndicators: Spread quickly into useful support positions.
Maintain a continuous forward handball chain.
Connect cleanly with the returning group.
Preserve legal technique across repeated waves.
matchApplication: Continuous transition requires players to attack immediately after gaining possession and then reorganise for the next phase. The drill develops sustained support running, fast handball movement and technical control under increasing physical demand.
relatedDrills: HB-031 – Receive at Speed and Release Forward

title: Handball Movement and Support Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing moving handball, support and possession-chain competency
objective: Assess each player’s ability to receive and handball while moving, select appropriate support options and contribute to a continuous possession chain.
groundSize: Four assessment stations arranged within an area approximately 45 metres × 35 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Establish four stations:
Station 1: Receive at speed and release forward.
Station 2: Change-of-direction handball.
Station 3: Moving support choice between inside and outside options.
Station 4: Three-lane transition possession chain.
Divide players evenly between stations.
Assign observers where possible.
Each player receives a defined number of assessed repetitions.
Record dominant- and non-dominant-hand outcomes separately.
Explain assessment criteria and scoring before beginning.
Allow one practice repetition at each station.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, each player completes four receive-and-release repetitions at running speed.
At Station 2, each player completes two direction changes and handballs to each side.
At Station 3, each player acts as ball carrier for four repetitions and must select inside or outside support.
At Station 4, players complete two full three-lane transition sequences.
Observers assess legal technique, balance, accuracy, target selection and movement after disposal.
Players rotate after all members complete the required work.
Errors are recorded without unnecessary interruption.
At the end of all stations, each player receives one movement strength and one priority action.
Players repeat the station associated with their lowest result.
Coaches retain assessment results for future comparison.
coachingPoints: Assess legal handball technique at realistic movement speed.
Judge whether the football allows the receiver to maintain momentum.
Observe balance before and after changes of direction.
Record whether players scan more than one support option.
Assess the appropriateness of hand selection.
Observe movement immediately after disposal.
Separate technical errors from poor spacing or decision making.
Provide feedback linked to specific observable behaviour.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players receive cleanly while moving.
Whether handballs remain accurate at speed.
Whether players change direction under control.
Whether multiple support options are scanned.
Whether inside and outside choices are appropriate.
Whether both hands are used competently.
Whether the player continues supporting after disposal.
Whether technique and decisions remain effective during the transition station.

commonErrors.error: The player stops before handballing.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and require continuous movement through the release.

commonErrors.error: The handball arrives behind the moving receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target the receiver’s forward path.

commonErrors.error: Direction changes cause loss of balance.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and realign the feet before release.

commonErrors.error: The player selects the first visible option without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Require a shoulder scan to both support sides.

commonErrors.error: The player uses only the dominant fist.
commonErrors.correction: Repeat the relevant task with mandatory opposite-hand disposal.

commonErrors.error: The player stops after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Include movement into the next support position as part of the score.

commonErrors.error: Transition spacing collapses.
commonErrors.correction: Restore lane width and staggered depth before repeating.

progressions: Add passive defensive pressure.
Reduce release time.
Narrow target gates.
Increase receiver speed.
Limit ball carriers to one or two steps.
Compare results with a later repeated assessment.
regressions: Assess dominant and non-dominant hands separately.
successIndicators: Receive and release while maintaining movement.
Deliver into the receiver’s running path.
Contribute to an organised transition chain.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can apply handball technique within realistic movement and support demands. These capabilities underpin effective overlap, transition, stoppage exits and fast possession chains in Australian football.
relatedDrills: HB-031 – Receive at Speed and Release Forward
HB-035 – Handball Square with Moving Choice

title: Stationary Release Against Shadow Pressure
primarySkill: Maintaining legal handball technique under controlled shadow pressure
objective: Develop the ability to protect the football, remain balanced and execute an accurate handball while a defender applies controlled non-contact pressure.
groundSize: Stations approximately eight metres long and five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Organise players into groups of three: ball carrier, shadow defender and receiver.
The ball carrier begins at the central cone with the football.
The shadow defender starts one metre away and slightly to one side.
The receiver stands four metres away on the opposite side.
The defender may move their feet, raise their arms and close space but may not tackle, bump or strike at the football.
The ball carrier must remain within a two-metre release zone.
Rotate roles after every repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver presents a target and calls for the football.
The shadow defender approaches under control from the nominated side.
The ball carrier identifies the pressure, positions the body between the defender and football and organises the football on the protected side.
The ball carrier delivers an accurate handball to the receiver.
The defender attempts to affect vision and timing without making contact.
The receiver secures the football and returns it to the starting position.
Players rotate from ball carrier to receiver, receiver to defender and defender to ball carrier.
Change the pressure side regularly.
A repetition is successful when the handball is legal, reaches the receiver and is released without the football being exposed.
Stop and reset if the defender exceeds the permitted pressure level.
coachingPoints: Identify the defender’s approach before organising the disposal.
Use the hips, shoulder and torso to protect the football.
Keep the football on the side furthest from pressure.
Maintain a strong, balanced stance.
Look beyond the defender to the receiver.
Use a compact striking action to reduce release time.
Follow through directly towards the receiver.
Remain composed rather than rushing into an illegal disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier recognises the pressure side.
Whether the body protects the football.
Whether the support platform remains stable.
Whether the player maintains vision on the receiver.
Whether the handball remains legal as the defender closes.
Whether the disposal reaches a safe receiving area.
Whether both sides of the body are used effectively.

commonErrors.error: The football is held on the side closest to pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer it to the protected-side supporting hand before release.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier turns their back completely.
commonErrors.correction: Remain side-on so the football is protected while vision is preserved.

commonErrors.error: The player rushes and throws the football.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the defender’s approach and rebuild the stable platform and clear fist strike.

commonErrors.error: The player watches only the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Scan beyond the pressure and maintain awareness of the receiver.

commonErrors.error: The stance becomes narrow and unstable.
commonErrors.correction: Widen the feet and lower the centre of gravity.

commonErrors.error: The defender makes excessive contact.
commonErrors.correction: Return to shadow pressure and reinforce the no-contact restriction.

progressions: Reduce the starting distance between defender and ball carrier.
Allow the defender to approach from either side without prior notice.
Reduce the release zone.
Require the handball within two seconds.
Allow controlled bump-pad pressure.
regressions: Replace the defender with a cone or stationary obstacle.
Allow the ball carrier more time.
Use the dominant protected side only.
successIndicators: Protect the football with the body.
matchApplication: Players often win possession with an opponent closing from one side. Protecting the football and releasing accurately before contact allows the team to maintain possession and use nearby support around stoppages and contests.
relatedDrills: HB-040 – Handball Movement and Support Assessment

title: Closing Defender Release Window
primarySkill: Timing a handball before a closing defender removes the release option
objective: Develop the ability to recognise a closing defender and release the football accurately within the available time and space.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 12 metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
The ball carrier begins at one end of the lane.
A receiver starts five metres ahead and slightly to one side.
A defender begins three metres behind the ball carrier.
Mark a four-metre release window with flat markers.
The defender may chase and apply shadow pressure but may not tackle.
The receiver moves forward when the ball carrier enters the release window.
Rotate roles after every repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins jogging into the lane.
The defender starts chasing on the coach’s signal.
The receiver accelerates forward and presents a target.
The ball carrier scans the receiver and the closing defender.
The player handballs within the marked release window.
The defender attempts to close the handball space without making contact.
The receiver catches while moving and carries the football through the finishing cone.
Players rotate roles.
Complete repetitions with the defender approaching from different angles.
Award one point for a legal disposal received in stride before the defender reaches handballing distance.
coachingPoints: Scan the receiver before entering the release window.
Recognise how quickly the defender is closing.
Organise the football early.
Maintain running balance.
Release before the defender reaches the striking arm.
Lead the receiver into space.
Avoid holding the football until the final possible moment.
Remain legal and accurate under time pressure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier recognises the defender’s closing speed.
Whether the football is organised before pressure arrives.
Whether disposal occurs inside the release window.
Whether the receiver is led forward.
Whether the handball remains legal.
Whether the player delays unnecessarily.
Whether both release sides are used.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier waits until the defender is too close.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier when the receiver first enters clear space.

commonErrors.error: The player looks only at the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the target before entering the pressure zone.

commonErrors.error: The handball is rushed and inaccurate.
commonErrors.correction: Organise the platform earlier and maintain a compact striking action.

commonErrors.error: The football arrives behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release sooner and aim ahead of the runner.

commonErrors.error: The defender makes contact.
commonErrors.correction: Increase the starting distance and return to shadow pressure.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier slows excessively.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain controlled forward speed through the release window.

progressions: Reduce the defender’s starting distance.
Narrow the release window.
Allow the receiver to choose either side.
Require the ball carrier to use the hand opposite the defender.
Permit the defender to attempt a controlled smother after release begins.
successIndicators: Organise the football before the defender arrives.
Use both hands according to pressure direction.
matchApplication: A player carrying the football may have only a short opportunity to release before being tackled. Recognising the closing defender and using the available handball window helps prevent holding-the-ball decisions and turnovers.
relatedDrills: HB-022 – Handball to a Leading Receiver
HB-024 – Moving Handball Through Release Gates
HB-041 – Stationary Release Against Shadow Pressure

title: Contested Receive and Protected Handball
primarySkill: Securing a receive under controlled body pressure and releasing from the protected side
objective: Develop the ability to secure the football while experiencing controlled body pressure, establish a protected position and complete an accurate handball.
groundSize: Stations approximately eight metres long and five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Organise groups of four: feeder, receiver, pressure player and release target.
The receiver begins in the central zone.
The pressure player stands beside the receiver holding a bump pad.
The feeder stands three metres away with the football.
The release target stands four metres away on the opposite side.
The pressure player applies light, controlled pad contact only after the receiver touches the football.
Rotate roles after every two repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver presents both hands and calls for the football.
The feeder handballs accurately to the receiver.
As the football arrives, the pressure player applies controlled side pressure with the bump pad.
The receiver secures the football with two hands and lowers the centre of gravity.
The player positions the body between the pressure and football.
The football is organised onto the protected-side supporting hand.
The receiver handballs accurately to the release target.
The pressure player maintains controlled contact without tackling or striking at the football.
Players reset and repeat from the opposite pressure side.
Rotate roles after both sides have been completed.
coachingPoints: Present strong hands before the football arrives.
Secure the football before responding to contact.
Absorb pressure through a balanced, flexed stance.
Keep the feet active rather than becoming upright and rigid.
Move the football to the protected side.
Maintain vision on the release target.
Use a compact handball action.
Contact must remain controlled and appropriate to the player group.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver presents early.
Whether the football is secured cleanly.
Whether body pressure causes the player to lose balance.
Whether the football is moved to the protected side.
Whether vision on the release target is maintained.
Whether the disposal remains legal.
Whether pressure is applied safely and consistently.

commonErrors.error: The receiver turns before securing the football.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the catch with two hands before repositioning.

commonErrors.error: Contact causes the player to stand upright.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and maintain a strong base.

commonErrors.error: The football remains exposed to the pressure side.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer it immediately to the protected-side platform.

commonErrors.error: The player loses sight of the release target.
commonErrors.correction: Stay side-on and keep the head up.

commonErrors.error: The handball becomes a throw under contact.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce pressure and restore a clear fist strike.

commonErrors.error: The pressure player bumps too forcefully.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce force and reinforce controlled pad contact only.

progressions: Increase the pressure slightly within safe limits.
Allow the pressure player to choose the contact side.
Move the release target after possession is secured.

Establish five assessment stations:

Record both-hand capability.
Maintain strict contact and safety controls.
Provide feedback based on specific observed actions.

Whether the body protects the football.
