matchApplication: Defenders frequently attempt to smother a handball by extending their arms into the expected release line. Players who can shift their feet and dispose through an alternative lane are less predictable and more effective in congestion.
relatedDrills: HB-035 – Handball Square with Moving Choice
HB-041 – Stationary Release Against Shadow Pressure

title: Boundary-Side Pressure Release
primarySkill: Releasing a teammate while constrained by the boundary and defensive pressure
objective: Teach players to use their body, the available inside space and an appropriate handball release when possession is restricted near the boundary.
groundSize: Boundary channels approximately 15 metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a boundary line along one side of the channel.
The ball carrier begins one metre inside the boundary.
A shadow defender begins two metres inside the ball carrier.
One support player starts four metres ahead and inside.
A second receiver waits further forward.
The defender may close the inside lane but may not tackle.
The ball carrier may not cross the boundary.
Mirror the drill for both sides of the ground.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins moving along the boundary.
The defender applies controlled inside pressure.
The support runner moves forward and presents inside the ball carrier.
The ball carrier protects the football between the body and boundary-side arm.
The player identifies the inside release window.
The handball is delivered into the support runner’s path.
The support runner receives and connects with the second receiver.
The defender attempts to close or intercept the inside lane.
Players rotate roles after each repetition.
Repeat on the opposite boundary side.
coachingPoints: Recognise that the boundary removes one escape option.
Keep the football protected away from the defender.
Maintain balance without stepping over the line.
Scan inside support early.
Use a firm, direct handball rather than a looping release.
Lead the receiver away from the boundary.
Do not force a handball if the support lane is closed.
Support runners should remain inside and slightly ahead.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier remains aware of the boundary.
Whether the football is protected from the defender.
Whether inside support is recognised.
Whether the handball leads the receiver away from the line.
Whether the disposal stays in play.
Whether the player avoids forcing a closed option.
Whether both boundary sides are practised.

commonErrors.error: The player steps over the boundary while protecting the football.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the steps and keep the feet inside the marked line.

commonErrors.error: The football is exposed to the inside defender.
commonErrors.correction: Carry it on the boundary-side protected platform.

commonErrors.error: The support runner stays level or behind.
commonErrors.correction: Move slightly ahead and inside to create an exit angle.

commonErrors.error: The handball travels towards the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Follow through towards inside space.

commonErrors.error: The player forces the release through a closed lane.
commonErrors.correction: Hold possession briefly or wait for support to reposition.

commonErrors.error: The player watches the boundary and loses awareness of the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Scan both the line and inside pressure before release.

progressions: Allow controlled tackling.
Narrow the boundary channel.
Add a second inside defender.
Require the release within three steps.
Allow the support runner to change angle late.
regressions: Allow the ball carrier to stop before release.
Practise one boundary side at a time.
successIndicators: Protect the football from inside pressure.
Release accurately away from the line.
Complete the possession chain in both directions.
matchApplication: Players near the boundary have reduced space and are easier to trap. A protected inside handball can return the football to open space and prevent the opposition from forcing a stoppage or turnover.
relatedDrills: HB-041 – Stationary Release Against Shadow Pressure

title: Front-On Pressure Side-Step Handball
primarySkill: Using a side-step to create a handball lane against front-on pressure
objective: Develop the ability to engage a front-on defender, use a controlled side-step to create separation and execute an accurate handball through the new lane.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 14 metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
The ball carrier begins at one end of the lane.
A defender begins five metres ahead.
Two receivers stand behind the defender, one left and one right.
The defender may move laterally and apply shadow pressure.
The ball carrier must engage the defender before side-stepping.
The handball is delivered to the receiver on the side created by the evasion.
Rotate roles after two repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier advances towards the defender.
Both receivers move slightly and present targets.
The defender squares up and tracks the ball carrier.
The ball carrier uses a controlled side-step left or right.
The player keeps the football on the side away from the defender.
Once a release lane opens, the ball carrier handballs to the matching receiver.
The receiver catches and runs through the finishing gate.
The defender attempts to recover and intercept without tackling.
Players rotate roles.
Complete equal repetitions stepping to both sides.
coachingPoints: Approach under control and engage the defender.
Sell the initial movement with eyes, shoulders or foot position.
Plant outside the defender’s line and move laterally with balance.
Keep the football protected during the side-step.
Organise the supporting hand immediately after the evasion.
Release before the defender recovers.
Lead the receiver into the open lane.
Avoid excessive sideways movement that stops forward momentum.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier engages the defender.
Whether the side-step creates genuine separation.
Whether balance is maintained.
Whether the football stays protected.
Whether the handball is released quickly after the step.
Whether the correct receiver and striking hand are selected.
Whether the defender applies controlled pressure.

commonErrors.error: The player side-steps too early.
commonErrors.correction: Carry closer so the defender must commit.

commonErrors.error: The movement is wide but not forward.
commonErrors.correction: Step outside the defender while continuing towards goal.

commonErrors.error: The football is exposed during the evasion.
commonErrors.correction: Keep it on the side furthest from the defender.

commonErrors.error: The player takes too many steps before releasing.
commonErrors.correction: Organise the platform immediately and dispose once the lane opens.

commonErrors.error: The handball goes behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Aim into the new running lane.

commonErrors.error: The defender tackles during the introductory version.
commonErrors.correction: Return to shadow tracking and interception only.

progressions: Allow controlled tackling after the side-step.
Reduce lane width.
Give the defender freedom to choose the starting angle.
Require release within one step of the evasion.
Add a recovering defender behind the ball carrier.
successIndicators: Create separation with a balanced side-step.
matchApplication: A side-step can create the small amount of space required to release a teammate when a defender closes front-on. Effective players evade without losing balance or carrying the football into further pressure.

title: Rear-Tackle Release Decision
primarySkill: Selecting and executing a handball release while rear pressure closes
objective: Teach players to scan for rear pressure, recognise the available release side and handball accurately before the tackler secures both arms.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 12 metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
The ball carrier begins in the centre of the lane.
A tackler begins three metres behind.
Two receivers stand four metres ahead, one to each side.
The ball carrier must scan over a shoulder before beginning.
The tackler approaches under control and completes a safe wrap without taking the player to ground.
Receivers communicate and remain separated.
Rotate roles after every repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier scans behind and identifies the tackler’s starting line.
The coach signals the repetition to begin.
The ball carrier moves forward while both receivers present.
The tackler closes from behind and attempts a controlled wrap.
The ball carrier selects the receiver on the side away from the tackler’s strongest arm position.
The player organises the football and releases before both arms are pinned.
The receiver catches and exits through the finishing gate.
The tackler completes only the safe controlled contact required.
Rotate roles.
Change the tackler’s approach angle regularly.
coachingPoints: Scan before possession movement begins.
Listen to teammate communication.
Recognise which side of the body remains free.
Keep the football away from the tackler’s reach.
Organise the support platform before full contact.
Use a short, legal striking action.
Release before the tackler controls both arms.
Maintain forward balance through the disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier scans rear pressure.
Whether the free side is recognised.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether the support platform is prepared early.
Whether the disposal remains legal.
Whether the release occurs before both arms are controlled.
Whether tackling contact remains safe.

commonErrors.error: The player does not scan behind.
commonErrors.correction: Require a visible shoulder check before the start signal.

commonErrors.error: The football is carried loosely away from the body.
commonErrors.correction: Keep it secure and protected until the release begins.

commonErrors.error: The player waits until both arms are pinned.
commonErrors.correction: Organise and release as soon as the tackler enters contact range.

commonErrors.error: The player blindly handballs to the first voice.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the visible receiver before disposal.

commonErrors.error: The player throws the football under contact.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce tackle speed and restore a clear fist strike.

commonErrors.error: The tackler drives the ball carrier forward or to ground.
commonErrors.correction: Use wrap-only contact and stop momentum safely.

progressions: Start the tackler closer.
Allow the tackler to choose the approach angle.
Move receivers after contact begins.
Require the ball carrier to take an imperfect feed first.
Progress to legal live tackling for suitable senior groups.
regressions: Allow the ball carrier to begin already side-on.
successIndicators: Prepare the handball before full contact.
matchApplication: Rear pressure is common after a player gathers a loose football or receives facing forward. Early scanning and preparation allow the ball carrier to release before the tackle becomes effective.

title: Two-versus-Two Congestion Exit
primarySkill: Creating and using a handball exit in a two-versus-two congested contest
objective: Develop the ability of two attacking players to win or receive possession, create separation and use a legal handball to escape two controlled defenders.
groundSize: Grids approximately ten metres × eight metres with a two-metre exit gate.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a ten-metre × eight-metre grid.
Place an exit gate at one end.
Two attackers and two defenders begin inside the grid.
One attacker starts with the football, or the coach may feed a loose football.
Defenders apply controlled tackling according to age and ability.
Attackers must complete at least one handball before exiting.
The possession changes immediately after a turnover.
Rotate teams after four repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins the repetition with a handball or ground-ball feed.
The attacking pair attempts to secure possession.
The player without the football creates separation and presents an exit option.
The ball carrier protects possession and scans for the support player.
Attackers must complete a legal handball before carrying through the exit gate.
Defenders attempt to tackle, intercept or force the football out.
If defenders win possession, they immediately attack the same exit gate.
The repetition ends when a team exits in possession or the football leaves the grid.
Reset with a new starting feed.
Rotate attacking and defensive roles.
coachingPoints: The support player must move away from the immediate contest.
Create a visible handball lane rather than standing behind a defender.
Ball carriers should protect the football and remain balanced.
Use a short, firm handball in congestion.
Avoid handballing to a teammate under equal or greater pressure.
Move again after disposal.
Defenders should communicate and remain connected.
Transition immediately when possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the support attacker creates separation.
Whether a clear handball lane is established.
Whether the ball carrier protects possession.
Whether the disposal improves the team’s position.
Whether players react immediately after turnover.
Whether defenders apply legal controlled contact.
Whether the exit gate is attacked with speed.

commonErrors.error: Both attackers remain in the same congestion.
commonErrors.correction: One player must separate and present outside the immediate contest.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier handballs to a teammate under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Hold possession briefly or select a safer release angle.

commonErrors.error: The support player stands behind a defender.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally into the ball carrier’s vision.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after handballing.
commonErrors.correction: Continue to support or block the defender’s recovery line legally.

commonErrors.error: Turnover reaction is slow.
commonErrors.correction: Change roles immediately when possession changes.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes uncontrolled.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce defender intensity and re-establish tackling restrictions.

progressions: Reduce the grid size.
Require two handballs before exiting.
Add a second exit gate.
Allow full legal tackling for appropriate groups.
Introduce a five-second scoring limit.
regressions: Use one active and one passive defender.
matchApplication: Two-versus-two contests occur around stoppages, boundary situations and loose footballs. The ability to separate and release one teammate can turn a neutral contest into a clean exit.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit

title: Three-versus-Three Tight-Grid Handball
primarySkill: Maintaining handball possession in a confined three-versus-three contest
objective: Develop clean receiving, rapid support and legal handball execution in a confined grid where time, space and passing lanes are constantly changing.
groundSize: Grids measuring approximately 12 metres × 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide players into teams of three.
Mark a 12-metre × 12-metre grid.
One team begins in possession.
Players may handball only.
Ball carriers may take no more than three steps.
Controlled tackling is permitted according to age and skill level.
One point is scored for five consecutive handballs.
Possession changes after a turnover, out-of-bounds disposal or illegal handball.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with a free handball from the edge of the grid.
Teammates spread to create short support angles.
The ball carrier may take up to three steps before disposing.
Defenders apply pressure, attempt interceptions and complete controlled tackles.
The attacking team scores after five consecutive legal handballs.
After scoring, the same team retains possession but the count returns to zero.
Any turnover creates an immediate change of attacking and defensive roles.
The football is restarted from the point of turnover.
Play in 60- to 90-second rounds.
Rotate team opponents and adjust the grid for ability.
coachingPoints: Move immediately after disposal.
Present at different angles and depths.
Keep handballs short, firm and catchable.
Protect the football before release.
Scan before possession arrives.
Avoid standing in the defender’s shadow.
Defenders should pressure the ball and cover nearby options.
React instantly when possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers spread despite the small area.
Whether support options appear before possession.
Whether handballs remain legal under pressure.
Whether players protect the football.
Whether defenders communicate and cover options.
Whether transition after turnover is immediate.
Whether contact remains safe and appropriate.

commonErrors.error: Attackers stand in a cluster.
commonErrors.correction: Move to separate sides and depths of the ball carrier.

commonErrors.error: Players wait until possession arrives before scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Check pressure and support before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Handballs are floated in congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use firm, direct short deliveries.

commonErrors.error: Ball carriers attempt to beat multiple defenders alone.
commonErrors.correction: Release to support before being fully closed down.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Relocate immediately into a new passing lane.

commonErrors.error: Teams argue or pause after turnovers.
commonErrors.correction: Continue play immediately with the new possession team.

progressions: Reduce the grid size.
Limit ball carriers to one step.
Increase the scoring target.
Require use of both hands before a point can be scored.
Allow match-like contact for suitable players.
matchApplication: Congested match phases demand quick, legal and accurate handballs between nearby teammates. Players must scan early, protect possession and reposition continuously to prevent the football becoming trapped.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit

title: Repeat-Effort Pressure Handball
primarySkill: Maintaining handball execution across repeated pressure and support efforts
objective: Develop the ability to preserve legal handball technique, accuracy and support behaviour during repeated high-intensity efforts with limited recovery.
groundSize: A rectangular area approximately 25 metres long and 15 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide players into two attacking groups and two rotating pressure players.
Mark a 25-metre transition corridor.
Three attackers begin with the football at one end.
One pressure player begins behind and one in front.
Attackers must move the football through the corridor using handballs.
After finishing, the same attackers immediately defend the next group returning in the opposite direction.
Work in controlled blocks with planned recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
Three attackers begin advancing with the football.
The rear pressure player chases while the front defender closes passing lanes.
Attackers use handball and support movement to reach the finishing gate.
The repetition ends with a clean possession through the gate or a turnover.
The three attackers immediately become defenders against the next group moving in the opposite direction.
The original defenders exit through the recovery lane.
Players complete repeated attack-to-defence efforts.
Work continuously for 60 to 90 seconds.
Recover for an appropriate period before the next block.
Reduce workload if legal technique or safe movement deteriorates.
coachingPoints: Organise support early before fatigue builds.
Use direct, catchable handballs.
Continue moving after disposal.
Protect the football from the rear chaser.
Scan the front defender before release.
Transition immediately from attack to defence.
Maintain legal technique under fatigue.
Quality takes priority over excessive exhaustion.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether handball accuracy changes across efforts.
Whether players continue supporting after disposal.
Whether rear pressure is recognised.
Whether transition to defence is immediate.
Whether running technique remains safe.
Whether illegal throws increase under fatigue.
Whether recovery periods remain appropriate.

commonErrors.error: Handballs become inaccurate late in the block.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce running speed and restore target focus.

commonErrors.error: Players throw the football under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the repetition and rebuild legal technique before continuing.

commonErrors.error: Support players remain behind the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate early to level or forward positions.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to transition after finishing.
commonErrors.correction: Assign immediate defensive responsibility at the gate.

commonErrors.error: Rear pressure is ignored.
commonErrors.correction: Scan over the shoulder before receiving or carrying.

commonErrors.error: Work periods exceed safe technical capacity.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the block and increase recovery.

progressions: Increase work duration gradually.
Narrow the corridor.
Add controlled tackling.
Limit ball carriers to two steps.
Require a minimum number of handballs before finishing.
regressions: Use one-way repetitions with full reset.
successIndicators: Maintain legal handball technique under fatigue.
Complete repeated efforts without unsafe deterioration.
matchApplication: Handball execution often occurs after repeated running, tackling and support efforts. Players must preserve technique and decisions when fatigued rather than allowing pressure and exhaustion to create illegal or inaccurate disposals.

title: Turnover Contest and Handball Counterattack
primarySkill: Using handball to counterattack immediately after winning a turnover
objective: Develop the ability to react to a turnover, secure possession and use fast, accurate handballs to escape the contest before the opposition reorganises.
groundSize: A rectangular area approximately 25 metres × 18 metres with scoring gates at each end.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two teams of four to six.
Mark a scoring gate at each end.
Begin with one team in handball possession.
The attacking team attempts to complete four handballs before scoring through its gate.
Defenders apply controlled pressure and attempt to win possession.
When possession changes, the new attacking team immediately counterattacks towards the opposite gate.
No stoppage occurs after a turnover unless safety requires it.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins play with a handball to one team.
The attacking team spreads and attempts to maintain possession.
Defenders pressure the ball carrier and cover nearby support.
If the defenders win possession, roles change immediately.
The new ball carrier looks for the fastest safe handball exit.
Teammates spread away from the turnover contest.
The team attempts to score through the opposite gate.
One point is awarded for exiting through the gate in controlled possession.
After a score, the coach restarts from the centre.
Play in two- to three-minute blocks.
coachingPoints: React immediately when possession changes.
The first support players should spread away from the turnover point.
The new ball carrier must protect the football before releasing.
Use short handballs to escape immediate pressure.
Avoid handballing back into the contest.
Once clear, accelerate and use wider support.
Defenders should counter-pressure immediately after losing possession.
Communicate the direction of the counterattack.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the turnover immediately.
Whether support spreads away from congestion.
Whether the first handball improves field position.
Whether the ball carrier protects possession.
Whether the new attacking team accelerates.
Whether the dispossessed team counter-pressures.
Whether handball decisions remain legal and controlled.

commonErrors.error: Players pause after a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Change roles immediately and attack the opposite gate.

commonErrors.error: Support players remain around the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Spread laterally and forward to create exit lanes.

commonErrors.error: The first handball returns into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use an outside or forward-facing release option.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier rushes an illegal disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use a compact legal handball.

commonErrors.error: Players sprint ahead without remaining connected.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain short and medium support options.

commonErrors.error: The team that loses possession stops defending.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate counter-pressure around the turnover.

progressions: Reduce the playing area.
Require the first disposal after turnover to be a handball.
Add a time limit for scoring.
Increase contact to match-like levels for suitable players.
Award bonus points for scoring within three handballs of the turnover.
regressions: Pause briefly after turnovers to organise roles.
Reduce the handball requirement before scoring.
successIndicators: Spread away from the turnover point.
Use the first handball to escape pressure.
Apply defensive pressure after losing the football.
matchApplication: Turnovers create brief periods when team structure is disorganised. A clean first handball and immediate support spread can turn a contested win into a fast counterattack before the opposition resets.

title: Complete Congestion and Pressure Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing handball competency under congestion, contact and turnover pressure
objective: Assess each player’s ability to execute legal, accurate and tactically appropriate handballs during controlled contact, confined-space contests and turnover situations.
groundSize: Five assessment stations arranged within an area approximately 50 metres × 40 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Establish five assessment stations:
Station 1: Off-balance recovery and legal release.
Station 2: Smother-line recognition and alternative handball.
Station 3: Front- or rear-pressure release decision.
Station 4: Two-versus-two congestion exit.
Station 5: Turnover contest and handball counterattack.
Divide players evenly between stations.
Assign coaches or trained observers where possible.
Explain scoring, contact restrictions and safety standards.
Each player receives one practice repetition before assessment.
Record dominant- and non-dominant-side performance where relevant.
Allow sufficient recovery between high-load stations.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, each player completes two displaced releases from each contact side.
At Station 2, each player completes four smother-evasion handballs with unpredictable lane blocks.
At Station 3, each player completes two front-pressure and two rear-pressure releases.
At Station 4, each player performs as ball carrier, support player and defender in two-versus-two contests.
At Station 5, players complete two short turnover-transition rounds.
Observers score scanning, protection, balance, legality, accuracy, decision quality and response after disposal.
Unsafe contact or an illegal action ends that repetition.
Players rotate only after all required roles are completed.
Each player receives one identified strength and one priority development action.
Players repeat the station linked to their lowest score after feedback and recovery.
coachingPoints: Assess player behaviour before possession and pressure arrive.
Record whether the football is protected on the correct side.
Distinguish technical, decision and movement errors.
Apply the same legal handball standard under every pressure level.
Observe whether the release improves the team’s position.
Include movement after disposal in the assessment.
Evaluate turnover reaction in both attack and defence.
Manage physical load and contact carefully.
Feedback must identify a specific action the player can change.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise pressure direction.
Whether body position protects the football.
Whether balance is regained after displacement.
Whether smother and tackle lines are identified.
Whether handballs remain legal and accurate.
Whether support players create usable separation.
Whether decisions improve possession position.
Whether turnover reactions are immediate.
Whether players apply feedback during reassessment.

commonErrors.error: The player disposes while off balance.
commonErrors.correction: Recover the feet and establish a stable platform before handballing.

commonErrors.error: The football is exposed to pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Move it to the protected side and use the body as a barrier.

commonErrors.error: The player releases into a smother or closed lane.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the defender’s position and select the alternative option.

commonErrors.error: The disposal becomes a throw under contact.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce pressure and restore a stable platform and clear fist strike.

commonErrors.error: The player handballs to a teammate under greater pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Select a support option that improves possession position.

commonErrors.error: Support players remain in congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Separate laterally or forward into a visible lane.

commonErrors.error: Players react slowly after turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Change roles immediately and attack or defend the next phase.

commonErrors.error: Contact or fatigue becomes unsafe.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the repetition, reduce load and return to the appropriate controlled level.

progressions: Progress selected stations to match-like contact.
Reduce decision time and space.
Narrow release and exit lanes.
Add recovering defenders.
Repeat the assessment later and compare individual results.
Include consequences for illegal or ineffective disposals.
matchApplication: Congested Australian football requires players to receive imperfect possession, withstand contact, recognise pressure and release teammates legally within very limited time and space. This assessment measures whether those behaviours remain effective under realistic contest demands.
relatedDrills: HB-059 – Turnover Contest and Handball Counterattack

title: Stoppage Outlet Handball Chain
primarySkill: Using structured inside and outside handballs to exit a stoppage
objective: Develop a coordinated stoppage exit in which the first-possession player protects the football, connects with inside support and releases an outside runner into space.
groundSize: A stoppage circle approximately eight metres in diameter with an outside release corridor extending 20 metres.
equipment: Optional ruck bag or coach feed
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark an eight-metre stoppage circle.
Position one first-possession player inside the circle.
Place one inside-support player two to three metres from the contest.
Position one outside runner five metres wider and slightly forward.
Add one controlled pressure player inside the stoppage circle.
Place a finishing receiver 15 to 20 metres beyond the outside runner.
The coach begins each repetition with a ground-ball, tap or handball feed.
Mirror the structure to practise exits on both sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach feeds the football into the stoppage circle.
The first-possession player wins or receives the football under controlled pressure.
The player protects possession and handballs to the inside-support player.
The inside-support player receives facing towards the outside runner.
The outside runner accelerates into space and presents a target.
The inside-support player handballs into the runner’s path.
The outside runner receives at speed and connects with the finishing receiver.
The pressure player attempts to close the initial release without tackling beyond the agreed contact level.
Players follow their disposal and rotate through each role.
Repeat on both exit sides and vary the starting feed.
coachingPoints: The first-possession player must protect the football before releasing.
Inside support should remain close enough for a quick, safe handball.
The outside runner should hold width until the inside possession is secured.
Use short, firm handballs around the stoppage.
The inside-support player should receive with hips open towards the outside.
Release the outside runner into space rather than at their starting position.
Players must move again after disposal.
The structure should expand from congestion rather than collapse towards it.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the first-possession player secures and protects the football.
Whether inside support is available immediately.
Whether the outside runner maintains width.
Whether the second handball leads the runner forward.
Whether players move after disposal.
Whether the structure works on both sides.
Whether contact remains controlled and safe.

commonErrors.error: The outside runner moves too close to the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the inside-support player receives possession.

commonErrors.error: The first-possession player forces a long handball from congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use the nearby inside option before releasing outside.

commonErrors.error: Inside support receives facing back towards the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips and shoulders towards the outside runner before possession arrives.

commonErrors.error: The second handball is delivered behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target the runner’s forward path.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Follow the handball and replace into the next support role.

commonErrors.error: Pressure becomes uncontrolled.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce contact and return to restricted shadow pressure.

progressions: Add a second pressure player around the stoppage.
Allow the first-possession player to choose either inside support side.
Require the outside runner to make the next decision.
Add a kick after the final handball.
Begin with a live ruck contest for suitable groups.
regressions: Begin with the first-possession player already holding the football.
successIndicators: Release the outside runner into space.
Complete the chain without a fumble.
Perform the pattern on both sides.
matchApplication: Stoppage clearances are often created through a short inside handball followed by an outside release. This structure helps teams move the football from congestion to space before the opposition can establish pressure.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit
HB-059 – Turnover Contest and Handball Counterattack
HB-060 – Complete Congestion and Pressure Assessment

title: Defensive 50 Handball Exit Triangle
primarySkill: Using a three-player handball triangle to exit defensive 50
objective: Develop a reliable defensive 50 exit in which the ball carrier uses short angled support and width to move the football away from pressure.
groundSize: A defensive 50 channel approximately 30 metres long and 20 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a starting zone representing deep defensive 50.
Position one ball carrier near the starting line.
Place one short support player inside and one wider support player outside.
Position a fourth receiver beyond the defensive 50 exit line.
Add one shadow defender who pressures the ball carrier.
Mark safe inside and outside handball lanes.
Mirror the drill on both sides of the ground.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins with the football under shadow pressure.
The short support player presents at a 45-degree angle.
The ball carrier handballs to the short support option.
The wider player accelerates beyond the first possession.
The short support player turns away from pressure and releases the wide runner.
The wide runner receives and crosses the defensive 50 exit line.
The wide runner connects with the fourth receiver.
The original ball carrier moves after disposal to provide emergency support.
Players rotate through all roles.
Repeat on both defensive sides and vary the pressure angle.
coachingPoints: Avoid handballing directly across the face of goal when pressure makes the lane unsafe.
Create angled support rather than standing directly beside the ball carrier.
The first receiver should open the body towards the exit side.
Wide support must remain outside the pressure area.
Use short, reliable handballs before accelerating out.
The original ball carrier should remain involved after release.
Receivers must present before the football is delivered.
Exit with controlled speed rather than rushed disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the first support angle is safe.
Whether the ball carrier protects possession.
Whether the first receiver opens towards the exit.
Whether wide support remains clear of congestion.
Whether the football crosses the exit line in controlled possession.
Whether the original ball carrier supports again.
Whether players recognise unsafe central releases.

commonErrors.error: The first support player stands directly behind the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally to create a visible 45-degree handball lane.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier handballs across goal into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Use the safer angled support or retain possession briefly.

commonErrors.error: The wide runner starts too close.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside width until the first handball is completed.

commonErrors.error: The first receiver turns back towards goal.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the exit side before possession arrives.

commonErrors.error: The original ball carrier stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue behind the possession as emergency support.

commonErrors.error: The final handball is rushed beyond the exit line.
commonErrors.correction: Balance before connecting with the next receiver.

progressions: Add a second defender covering the wide lane.
Allow the ball carrier to choose either exit side.
Introduce controlled tackling.
Require the final receiver to connect with a kick.
Begin from a contested defensive ground ball.
successIndicators: Create a safe first support angle.
Keep players connected behind the football.
Complete the structure on both sides.
matchApplication: Defensive exits require composure and safe support angles. Short handballs can move the football away from immediate pressure and release a wider runner without exposing the team to a turnover near goal.
relatedDrills: HB-059 – Turnover Contest and Handball Counterattack

title: Half-Back Rebound Overlap
primarySkill: Creating a handball overlap from half-back
objective: Develop coordinated half-back rebound in which defenders handball, run past and create an overlap to advance the football beyond the first defensive line.
groundSize: A half-back transition channel approximately 35 metres long and 18 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position Player A deep in the channel with the football.
Player B begins five metres ahead and inside.
Player C starts wider and slightly behind Player B.
Player D begins 15 metres further forward.
Add one shadow defender near Player B.
Mark an outside overlap lane.
Players rotate through all positions after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A carries forward and handballs to Player B.
Player A immediately accelerates past Player B through the outside overlap lane.
Player B receives and draws the shadow defender.
Player B returns the football to Player A’s forward run.
Player C maintains width and becomes the next handball option.
Player A either handballs to Player C or continues to Player D according to the coach’s call.
The possession chain finishes beyond the half-back exit line.
Players follow their disposal into the next role.
Repeat on the opposite side.
Increase tempo only when spacing and timing remain controlled.
coachingPoints: The original ball carrier must accelerate immediately after disposal.
The first receiver should engage the defender before returning the football.
The overlap runner must pass on the outside, not through the receiver’s line.
Wide support should hold position until the overlap develops.
Return handballs must be placed in front of the runner.
Use both hands according to the overlap side.
The group should continue forward after breaking the line.
Avoid overusing handball when the forward player is already clear.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player A accelerates after the first handball.
Whether Player B draws the defender.
Whether the overlap occurs outside the receiver.
Whether the return handball leads the runner.
Whether Player C maintains width.
Whether the group breaks the half-back line.
Whether players recognise when the direct forward option is preferable.

commonErrors.error: The original ball carrier jogs after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate with the first three steps through the outside lane.

commonErrors.error: Player B returns the football before drawing pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Carry for one or two steps until the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: The overlap runner cuts in front of Player B.
commonErrors.correction: Run around the outside shoulder.

commonErrors.error: Wide support moves too early into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the return handball is completed.

commonErrors.error: The return handball arrives behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and lead the outside run.

commonErrors.error: Players handball repeatedly when a direct option is open.
commonErrors.correction: Scan forward and use the simplest effective possession.

progressions: Add a second recovering defender.
Allow Player B to choose whether to return or release wide.
Introduce controlled tackling.
Finish with a kick to a leading target.
Reduce the width of the overlap lane.
regressions: Complete the drill at jogging pace.
successIndicators: Lead the runner with the return handball.
Break the first defensive line in possession.
matchApplication: Half-back rebound often begins when a defender releases a teammate and continues running to regain possession beyond pressure. Effective overlap creates numerical advantage and accelerates transition.

title: Corridor Access Handball Pattern
primarySkill: Using handball to access the corridor from a wider starting position
objective: Develop a structured handball pattern that moves the football from a wide position into the corridor through safe inside support.
groundSize: A 30-metre × 25-metre area divided into a wide lane, inside lane and corridor.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a wide starting lane along one side.
Mark an inside-support lane five metres infield.
Mark the corridor through the centre.
Player A begins wide with the football.
Player B starts inside and slightly behind.
Player C begins in the corridor and slightly ahead.
Player D waits further forward.
Add one shadow defender between the wide and inside lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A carries the football forward in the wide lane.
Player B accelerates into an inside support position.
Player A engages the shadow defender and handballs to Player B.
Player B receives with the body open towards the corridor.
Player C leads forward through the corridor.
Player B handballs into Player C’s path.
Player C receives and connects with Player D.
Player A continues forward as outside support.
Players rotate through all roles.
Mirror the drill to access the corridor from both sides.
coachingPoints: Do not leave the wide lane until inside support is available.
The first inside runner should begin slightly behind the ball carrier.
Draw pressure before using the inside handball.
The inside receiver should open towards the corridor before possession arrives.
The corridor runner must stay clear and slightly ahead.
Use direct handballs that preserve forward movement.
The original wide player should remain involved.
Avoid using the corridor if defensive pressure clearly closes the lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the wide ball carrier engages pressure.
Whether inside support arrives from behind.
Whether the inside receiver opens correctly.
Whether the corridor runner maintains separation.
Whether the handballs move the football forward.
Whether the original ball carrier continues supporting.
Whether players recognise when corridor access is unsafe.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier moves inside before support is ready.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the wide lane and wait for the inside runner.

commonErrors.error: The inside support player starts ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Begin slightly behind and accelerate into the release lane.

commonErrors.error: The inside receiver faces back towards the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the corridor before receiving.

commonErrors.error: The corridor runner moves too close to the second possession.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain forward depth and a clear passing lane.

commonErrors.error: The handball is forced through defensive pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Retain width or use a safer option when the corridor is closed.

commonErrors.error: The original ball carrier stops.
commonErrors.correction: Continue forward as outside support.

progressions: Add a corridor defender.
Allow Player B to choose corridor or return outside.
Reduce lane width.
Add a final kick after corridor access.
Begin with a contested wide possession.
successIndicators: Hold width until inside support arrives.
Open the inside receiver towards the corridor.
Access the centre without forcing possession.
matchApplication: Teams often begin possession near the boundary but seek to use the corridor when support and pressure allow. A short inside handball can change the angle of attack and open the ground.

title: Wing-to-Corridor Handball Switch
primarySkill: Switching the point of attack from the wing into central support
objective: Teach players to recognise when forward movement on the wing is blocked and use handball support to switch possession towards the corridor.
groundSize: A 35-metre × 30-metre area divided into wing, central and opposite-side lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Player A begins on the wing with the football.
One shadow defender blocks the forward wing lane.
Player B provides short support behind and inside.
Player C begins centrally.
Player D starts on the opposite side and slightly forward.
Mark a central switch gate.
Players must use handball to move possession through the centre before reaching the opposite side.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A carries forward until the defender closes the wing lane.
Player B presents behind and inside.
Player A turns away from pressure and handballs back to Player B.
Player B receives facing infield.
Player C accelerates through the central switch gate.
Player B handballs to Player C.
Player D moves forward on the opposite side.
Player C connects with Player D through a final handball.
Players follow their disposal and rotate.
Repeat in both directions and vary when the defender closes the wing.
coachingPoints: Recognise when the forward wing lane is genuinely blocked.
Support behind and inside rather than directly behind.
The ball carrier should turn away from pressure under control.
The supporting player should receive with vision towards the corridor.
Central support must time the run after the reset begins.
The opposite-side player should hold width until possession reaches the centre.
Use direct handballs to move the point of attack quickly.
Avoid switching slowly if the original wing remains open.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player A recognises the blocked lane.
Whether Player B provides a safe reset angle.
Whether the turn away from pressure is balanced.
Whether central support times the run correctly.
Whether opposite-side width is maintained.
Whether the switch moves quickly through the centre.
Whether players avoid switching unnecessarily.

commonErrors.error: The wing player forces possession forward into the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Use the supporting reset option when the lane is closed.

commonErrors.error: Reset support stands directly behind the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Move inside to create a safer angled lane.

commonErrors.error: The central runner begins too early.
commonErrors.correction: Time the run from Player B’s clean possession.

commonErrors.error: The opposite-side player drifts into the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the central handball is completed.

commonErrors.error: The switch handballs are slow and looping.
commonErrors.correction: Use firm, direct disposals to move the defence.

commonErrors.error: Players switch when the wing remains open.
commonErrors.correction: Continue forward when the original lane is still safe.

progressions: Add a central interceptor.
Allow live choice between continuing wing-side or switching.
Narrow the central gate.
Add controlled tackling.
Finish with a forward entry.
matchApplication: When the wing is closed by defensive pressure, a controlled handball reset can move the football back inside and switch the point of attack before the opposition shifts across.

title: Numbers-at-the-Football Release
primarySkill: Using additional teammates around the contest to create a clean handball exit
objective: Develop a team method for creating numbers around a contested football, securing possession and releasing one player into clear space.
groundSize: A contest zone 10 metres × 10 metres with a 20-metre exit corridor.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a central contest grid.
Place three attacking players and two defenders inside or around the grid.
Position one outside receiver at the beginning of the exit corridor.
The coach feeds a ground ball or contested handball into the grid.
Attackers aim to use their numerical advantage to secure and release.
Defenders attempt to lock the football in or win possession.
Rotate roles after three repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach feeds the football into the contest grid.
One attacker attempts to win the football.
A second attacker provides close support.
The third attacker separates towards the exit side.
The first-possession player protects and handballs to close support if required.
Close support releases the separating player.
The outside receiver accelerates through the exit corridor.
Defenders attempt to tackle, intercept or prevent separation within controlled contact rules.
If defenders win possession, they attack through the opposite side of the grid.
Reset after the football exits or possession is lost.
coachingPoints: Only one player should attack the football directly when possible.
A second player should provide close handball support.
The third player must separate and create the exit.
Communicate roles early.
Protect the first possession before attempting to release.
Use short handballs inside the contest.
Accelerate once the football reaches the outside player.
React immediately if possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attacking players assume different roles.
Whether too many players attack the football.
Whether close support remains visible.
Whether the third player creates separation.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether the exit handball improves possession.
Whether turnover reaction is immediate.

commonErrors.error: All attackers crowd the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one winner, one close support and one outside release.

commonErrors.error: The first-possession player attempts a long handball immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Use the close support player before releasing outside.

commonErrors.error: The outside player remains near the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Separate early and hold the exit lane.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand behind defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally into the ball carrier’s vision.

commonErrors.error: Attackers stop after losing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and defend the opposite exit.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes unsafe.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce intensity and re-establish controlled tackling rules.

progressions: Add a third defender.
Reduce the contest grid.
Allow the outside player to choose either exit side.
Require two handballs before exit.
Begin from a live stoppage contest.
matchApplication: Teams create effective stoppage and contest exits by having different players win, support and separate. Numerical advantage is wasted when everyone moves towards the football instead of creating an outside release.

title: Forward Entry Handball Connection
primarySkill: Using handball support to create a controlled forward entry
objective: Develop a handball chain that releases a player through the front of congestion and creates a balanced forward entry into inside 50.
groundSize: A forward transition area approximately 35 metres long and 25 metres wide, finishing at an inside 50 line.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Player A begins outside the forward 50 with the football.
Player B provides short inside support.
Player C begins wider and slightly forward.
Player D starts centrally near the inside 50 line.
Add one shadow defender near the first possession.
Position a forward target inside 50.
Mark a release gate through which the final handball must travel.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A carries towards the first pressure line.
Player B presents inside and receives a short handball.
Player C accelerates outside or through the release gate.
Player B selects and handballs to Player C.
Player D moves forward to become the final connecting option.
Player C handballs to Player D near the inside 50 line.
Player D enters inside 50 and delivers to the forward target.
The original players continue supporting behind the football.
Players rotate through all roles.
Mirror the drill and vary which support runner enters the release gate.
coachingPoints: The first support player should arrive inside and slightly behind.
Draw pressure before releasing.
The second runner should accelerate into the space created.
Handballs must lead players forward.
The final receiver should arrive at the inside 50 line in balance.
Avoid excessive handball if a direct forward entry is already available.
Maintain support behind the final possession.
Forward targets should time their movement from the final receiver’s possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player A engages pressure.
Whether Player B provides a safe inside option.
Whether Player C times the release run.
Whether Player D arrives in balance.
Whether the handballs maintain forward momentum.
Whether the forward target leads at the correct time.
Whether players avoid unnecessary extra handballs.

commonErrors.error: The first handball is released before pressure is drawn.
commonErrors.correction: Carry further until the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: Inside support runs ahead of the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Begin slightly behind and accelerate into the lane.

commonErrors.error: The second runner enters too early.
commonErrors.correction: Time the run from Player B’s possession.

commonErrors.error: The final receiver reaches inside 50 off balance.
commonErrors.correction: Control the final steps before receiving.

commonErrors.error: The group over-handballs and misses the direct entry.
commonErrors.correction: Scan forward and use the simplest effective option.

commonErrors.error: The forward target leads too early.
commonErrors.correction: Begin the lead when the final receiver secures possession.

progressions: Add two defenders.
Allow live choice between handball continuation and direct kick.
Narrow the release gate.
Introduce controlled tackling.
Add a scoring outcome from the forward entry.
regressions: Finish at the inside 50 line without a forward target.
successIndicators: Connect effectively with a forward target.
matchApplication: Handball chains can break the final defensive line and create a more balanced forward entry. The final possession should improve the quality of the inside 50 rather than simply increasing disposal count.

title: Behind-the-Football Reset Handball
primarySkill: Using support behind the football to reset possession under forward pressure
objective: Teach players to recognise when forward options are closed and use a controlled handball behind the football to reset the angle of attack.
groundSize: A 25-metre × 20-metre area with forward, reset and alternate-exit lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Player A begins with the football in the forward lane.
One defender blocks the direct forward option.
Player B provides support behind and slightly to one side.
Player C begins in the alternate-exit lane.
Player D waits further forward.
Mark the reset and alternate lanes clearly.
The defender may pressure the ball carrier but may not tackle.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A advances and identifies the blocked forward lane.
Player B communicates and presents behind the football.
Player A turns under control and handballs to Player B.
Player B receives facing across the ground.
Player C accelerates into the alternate-exit lane.
Player B handballs to Player C.
Player C receives and connects forward with Player D.
Player A moves after disposal to remain an emergency option.
Players rotate through all positions.
Later rounds allow Player A to continue forward if the defender leaves the lane open.
coachingPoints: Scan forward before deciding to reset.
Support behind should remain offset rather than directly in the pressure line.
The ball carrier must turn under control and protect the football.
The reset handball should be firm and accurate.
The receiver behind must open the body towards the alternate side.
The alternate runner should move only after the reset begins.
Resetting should create a new attacking angle, not simply move backwards.
The original ball carrier should remain involved.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player A scans the forward option.
Whether the decision to reset is appropriate.
Whether Player B creates a safe angle.
Whether Player B receives facing the alternate side.
Whether Player C times the release run.
Whether the reset leads to renewed forward movement.
Whether players avoid resetting unnecessarily.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier forces the blocked forward option.
commonErrors.correction: Use the supporting reset player when the lane is closed.

commonErrors.error: Reset support stands directly behind the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally to create a clear handball lane.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier turns blindly.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the support position before changing direction.

commonErrors.error: The reset receiver faces back towards pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the alternate side before receiving.

commonErrors.error: The team continues moving backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Use the second handball to attack the new forward angle.

commonErrors.error: Players reset even when forward space remains open.
commonErrors.correction: Continue forward when the direct option is safe.

progressions: Add an alternate-side defender.
Allow live choice between forward and reset options.
Reduce the reset space.
Introduce controlled tackling.
Add a time limit to re-establish forward movement.
successIndicators: Use safe support behind the football.
matchApplication: Teams need support behind the football when forward lanes close. A purposeful reset can retain possession, shift the defence and create a new route through the corridor or opposite side.

title: Full-Ground Handball Transition Pattern
primarySkill: Connecting structured handball support from defensive 50 to forward entry
objective: Develop a coordinated full-ground transition pattern that uses handball to exit defence, access the corridor and create a balanced forward entry.
groundSize: Half to full ground, depending on age and physical capacity.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Establish four connected zones:
Defensive 50 exit.
Half-back overlap.
Corridor access.
Forward entry.
Position players in structured roles through each zone.
Begin with the football deep in defence.
Players follow the football into the next zone after disposal.
Use external recovery lanes.
Begin with one football before introducing additional groups.
Ensure the next zone does not start until the previous receiver is ready.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defensive player begins with a short angled handball to support.
A second handball releases a wide half-back runner.
The runner uses an overlap or inside handball to access the corridor.
Central support advances the football through the middle zone.
A forward runner presents near the inside 50 line.
The football is handballed into the forward runner’s path.
The final player delivers to a forward target.
Every player follows their disposal or fills the next support role.
The football is returned through an outside recovery channel.
Add a second group only after timing and spacing are stable.
coachingPoints: Each zone should connect to the next rather than operate as an isolated drill.
Maintain width in defence and half-back.
Use inside support to change the attack angle.
Corridor runners should operate at different depths.
Handballs must lead moving teammates.
Players must continue running after disposal.
The forward entry should occur from balance.
Control group spacing so one transition does not catch another.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defensive support angles are correct.
Whether half-back overlap develops at speed.
Whether corridor access is timed effectively.
Whether players maintain different depths.
Whether handballs preserve forward momentum.
Whether the final forward entry is controlled.
Whether full-ground rotations remain organised and safe.

commonErrors.error: Players treat each zone as a separate stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Continue movement and connect immediately into the next phase.

commonErrors.error: Defensive players collapse centrally too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the exit is established.

commonErrors.error: Central runners operate at the same depth.
commonErrors.correction: Create short, level and forward options.

commonErrors.error: Handballs arrive behind moving teammates.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target forward space.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Follow the football or replace into the next support role.

commonErrors.error: Groups become congested.
commonErrors.correction: Increase starting intervals or reduce the number of active footballs.

progressions: Add passive defenders in each zone.
Allow live decisions between multiple support options.
Introduce controlled tackling in selected zones.
Require a score from the final forward entry.
Run simultaneous transitions in both directions.
regressions: Practise two connected zones at a time.
matchApplication: Successful transition depends on connected support from defence to attack. Full-ground handball chains should preserve width, use the corridor when available and deliver the final possession from a balanced position.

title: Team Handball Movement Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing structured team handball movement across multiple field zones
objective: Assess the team’s ability to use handball structure, support angles and decision making to move the football from congestion or defence into an effective forward entry.
groundSize: Half to full ground with four assessment zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Establish four assessment stations or phases:
Station 1: Stoppage outlet handball chain.
Station 2: Defensive 50 exit triangle.
Station 3: Corridor access or wing-to-corridor switch.
Station 4: Forward entry handball connection.
Divide the squad into positional or mixed groups.
Assign coaches to observe each phase.
Include controlled defenders to test decisions without creating full match pressure.
Explain assessment criteria before starting.
Allow one rehearsal before formal scoring.
Record team structure and individual execution separately.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, groups complete three stoppage exits on each side.
At Station 2, groups complete four defensive 50 exits under shadow pressure.
At Station 3, groups complete two corridor-access and two switch repetitions.
At Station 4, groups complete four forward-entry chains.
Coaches assess spacing, support timing, handball legality, ball placement and decision quality.
Players rotate through all required roles.
Each group receives one structural strength and one priority correction.
Groups repeat their lowest-scoring station.
Finish with one connected half- or full-ground transition combining all phases.
Retain results for later tactical comparison.
coachingPoints: Assess the structure before the football reaches each player.
Observe whether support exists inside, outside and behind.
Record whether ball carriers draw pressure before release.
Evaluate whether handballs improve field position.
Assess whether width and corridor access are used appropriately.
Include movement after disposal in the score.
Evaluate the balance and quality of the forward entry.
Distinguish individual technical errors from structural team errors.
Feedback should identify a specific team behaviour to improve.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether stoppage players assume distinct roles.
Whether defensive support angles are safe.
Whether outside width is maintained.
Whether corridor access is recognised and not forced.
Whether reset options exist when forward lanes close.
Whether players continue running after handballing.
Whether the forward entry improves scoring opportunity.
Whether feedback is applied during the repeated phase.

commonErrors.error: Players move towards the football instead of creating roles.
commonErrors.correction: Establish first-possession, close-support and outside-release responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Defensive exits use dangerous central handballs.
commonErrors.correction: Create angled support and use the safer outside lane.

commonErrors.error: Wide players collapse inside too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the football has exited pressure.

commonErrors.error: Corridor access is forced into defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Retain width or reset behind when the central lane is closed.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Follow the handball or replace into a new support position.

commonErrors.error: Forward entry occurs from an off-balance receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Control the final connection and arrive at inside 50 balanced.

commonErrors.error: Team errors are blamed only on the final disposer.
commonErrors.correction: Review spacing and support before possession reached the player.

commonErrors.error: Feedback is not applied during the repeat.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one observable correction before restarting.

progressions: Increase defensive pressure.
Add live turnover consequences.
Reduce preparation time between phases.
Progress to match-like contact for suitable groups.
Add scoreboard or time scenarios.
Compare results across later assessments.
regressions: Use half-ground instead of full-ground work.
successIndicators: Use short handballs to exit congestion.
Access or avoid the corridor appropriately.
matchApplication: Team handballing is effective only when individual technique is supported by coordinated positioning and decision making. This assessment measures whether the team can connect stoppage, defensive exit, transition and forward entry phases through purposeful handball movement.

title: Centre Bounce First-to-Third Possession Chain
primarySkill: Connecting first, second and third possessions from a centre bounce
objective: Develop a structured centre-bounce handball chain in which the first-possession player uses close support to release a third player into forward space.
groundSize: A centre-square area approximately 25 metres × 25 metres with a 20-metre forward exit corridor.
equipment: Optional ruck bag or nominated ruck player
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a central stoppage circle and forward exit corridor.
Assign one first-possession midfielder, one close-support midfielder and one outside runner.
Position one ruck or coach feeder at the stoppage.
Add two controlled-pressure opponents around the first and second possessions.
Place a finishing receiver at the end of the forward corridor.
Mirror the outside-release role on both sides.
Rotate all midfield and pressure roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ruck or coach directs the football into the stoppage area.
The first-possession player wins or receives the football.
The player protects possession and identifies the close-support midfielder.
The first handball is delivered to the close-support player.
The outside runner holds width before accelerating through the exit lane.
The close-support player receives with the body open towards the runner.
The second handball releases the outside runner into forward space.
The runner connects with the finishing receiver.
Pressure players attempt to close the first two handball lanes within controlled contact rules.
Players reset and repeat from the opposite exit side.
coachingPoints: First-possession players should secure and protect the football before releasing.
Close support must remain visible and within a short handball distance.
The second-possession player should receive with hips open towards the intended exit.
The outside runner must hold width until possession is secured.
Use short, firm handballs inside the stoppage.
Release the third player into space rather than at their starting position.
Midfielders should communicate their role before the football arrives.
The chain should expand progressively away from congestion.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the first-possession player protects the football.
Whether close support is available immediately.
Whether the second player receives with appropriate body orientation.
Whether the outside runner holds width.
Whether the third possession is released into forward space.
Whether pressure affects decisions without creating unsafe contact.
Whether players can execute the chain to both sides.

commonErrors.error: The first-possession player attempts a long handball from congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use the close-support player before releasing outside.

commonErrors.error: The second-possession player receives square to the stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the planned exit before possession arrives.

commonErrors.error: The outside runner enters the contest too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the second player secures possession.

commonErrors.error: Handballs are slow and looping.
commonErrors.correction: Use firm, direct disposals at short distance.

commonErrors.error: All midfielders move towards the football.

progressions: Begin from a live ruck contest.
Allow the outside runner to choose either exit side.
Add a recovering defender in the corridor.
Require a kick after the third possession.
Introduce full legal stoppage pressure for suitable groups.

Practise one exit side at a time.

Release the third player into forward movement.
Complete the chain on both sides.

title: Boundary Throw-In Fold-Out Handball
primarySkill: Using layered support to exit a boundary throw-in
objective: Develop a boundary-stoppage exit in which midfielders fold away from the contest and use handball to move the football from the boundary into open space.
groundSize: A boundary stoppage area approximately 20 metres × 18 metres with an inside exit lane.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a boundary line and stoppage zone.
Position one first-possession player near the boundary side of the contest.
Place one fold-out support player two to three metres inside.
Position one wider release runner further infield.
Add two controlled-pressure opponents.
Place a finishing receiver 15 metres infield.
The coach feeds the football from a boundary throw-in simulation.
Mirror the activity on both boundaries.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach throws or feeds the football into the stoppage.
The first-possession player secures the football near the boundary.
The fold-out support player moves laterally and slightly backwards into clear space.
The first-possession player protects the football and handballs to the fold-out player.
The wider runner accelerates infield.
The fold-out player receives facing the centre of the ground.
The second handball releases the wider runner.
The runner connects with the finishing receiver.
Pressure players attempt to close the inside exit without exceeding contact restrictions.
Rotate roles and repeat from the opposite boundary.
coachingPoints: The boundary-side player must recognise the reduced space.
Fold-out support should move away from the contest, not towards it.
The first handball should be short and protected.
The fold-out player should receive with vision towards the centre.
Wider support must remain separated from the stoppage.
Use the hand that directs the football away from boundary pressure.
The second handball should lead the runner infield.
Players must avoid forcing the exit when the lane is closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the first-possession player protects the football.
Whether fold-out support creates genuine separation.
Whether the first handball remains short and controlled.
Whether the second receiver holds infield width.
Whether body orientation supports the infield release.
Whether the football exits the stoppage in possession.
Whether the pattern works from both boundaries.

commonErrors.error: Fold-out support moves back into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally and backwards into clear infield space.

commonErrors.error: The first-possession player handballs along the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Use the infield support angle when available.

commonErrors.error: The fold-out receiver faces the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the centre before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Wider support starts too close to the stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Hold separation until the first handball is completed.

commonErrors.error: The second handball forces the receiver sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Lead the runner towards the centre.

commonErrors.error: The exit is attempted through a closed lane.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession or use an alternate support option.

progressions: Begin from a live boundary throw-in.
Add an infield defender.
Allow the first-possession player to choose between two fold-out options.
Require a forward kick after the exit.
Progress to match-like contact for suitable groups.
successIndicators: Protect and release the first possession.

matchApplication: Boundary stoppages compress available space. Folding one player away from the contest creates a short outlet and can shift the football into the centre before opposition pressure resets.
relatedDrills: HB-071 – Centre Bounce First-to-Third Possession Chain

title: Intercept-to-Overlap Handball Launch

setup:
Position one intercept player inside a marked defensive zone.
Place one immediate support player inside and one overlap runner outside.
Add one recovering attacker who applies shadow pressure after the intercept.
Position a further receiver beyond the transition line.

Mark an outside overlap channel.
Mirror the drill to both sides.

The intercept player secures the football.

The football is returned into the intercept player’s overlap run.
The overlap runner carries forward and handballs to the next receiver.
The recovering opponent attempts to close the return lane.
Players rotate through all roles.
Repeat from both defensive sides.
coachingPoints: Secure the intercept before initiating transition.
Immediate support should arrive at a safe angle.
The interceptor must accelerate after disposal.
The return handball should occur only after the recovering opponent commits.
Use the outside overlap lane to avoid central congestion.
Lead the runner forward.
Support behind the football should remain connected.
Do not force the overlap when the direct forward option is already open.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the intercept is secured cleanly.
Whether immediate support arrives quickly.
Whether the interceptor accelerates after disposal.
Whether the support player draws the recovering opponent.
Whether the return handball leads the overlap.
Whether the transition remains connected.
Whether players recognise when the overlap is unnecessary.

commonErrors.error: The interceptor runs before securing possession.
