title: Centre-Square to Wing Release
primarySkill: Moving the football from central congestion to a wing runner
objective: Develop a coordinated handball exit from central congestion that releases a wing runner into space while preserving forward momentum.
groundSize: A central grid approximately 15 metres × 15 metres with two 20-metre wing corridors.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central possession grid.
Position one ball carrier and one close-support player inside the grid.
Place one wing runner in each outside corridor.
Add two shadow defenders inside the central grid.
Position a finishing receiver at the end of each wing corridor.
The ball carrier may release to either side.
Rotate central and wing roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach feeds the football to the central ball carrier.
The ball carrier protects possession under shadow pressure.
The close-support player moves into a visible handball lane.
The first handball is delivered to close support.
Both wing runners hold width and begin accelerating.
The close-support player scans and selects the wing with the clearest lane.
The football is handballed into the selected runner’s path.
The wing runner receives and connects with the finishing receiver.
Defenders attempt to close the first and second lanes.
Reset and rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Central players should use short support to escape immediate pressure.
Wing runners must hold width until the central possession is secure.
The second-possession player should scan both wings.
Select the clearest release rather than the preferred-hand side.
Use sufficient force to reach the wider target.
Lead the wing runner forward.
The unused wing runner should remain available for the next phase.
Central players should continue supporting after release.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether central possession is protected.
Whether close support creates a visible lane.
Whether both wing runners maintain width.
Whether the second player scans both sides.
Whether the handball leads the selected runner.
Whether the unused runner remains active.
Whether central players support again.

title: Wing Fold and Inside Return
primarySkill: Using a wing fold and inside return handball to change the running lane
objective: Develop a wing possession pattern in which the outside player releases an inside runner and receives the football back beyond pressure.
groundSize: A wing corridor approximately 30 metres long and 15 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Player A begins wide with the football.
Player B begins inside and slightly behind.
Player C starts further forward in the wide lane.
Add one shadow defender between Player A and Player C.
Mark an inside support channel and outside return channel.
Player A must use Player B before regaining possession outside.
Mirror the pattern on both wings.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A carries forward in the wide lane.
Player B accelerates from inside and behind.
Player A handballs to Player B.
Player A immediately folds behind and then outside Player B.
Player B receives and engages the shadow defender.

The first handball must be short and accurate.
The original ball carrier should fold behind before moving outside.
Player B should engage the defender before returning the football.
The return handball must lead Player A into the outside lane.
Running lines should remain clearly separated.
Use the correct hand for each direction.
Continue forward after breaking the pressure line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player B times the inside support run.
Whether Player A folds behind rather than crossing in front.
Whether Player B draws the defender.
Whether the return handball leads the outside runner.
Whether players maintain separate lanes.
Whether the final connection remains accurate.
Whether both wings are used effectively.

commonErrors.error: Player B begins ahead of the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Start slightly behind and accelerate into the inside lane.

commonErrors.error: Player B returns the football immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Carry until the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: The return handball goes behind Player A.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target the outside running path.

commonErrors.error: Players collide or occupy the same line.
commonErrors.correction: Use the marked inside and outside channels.

commonErrors.error: The pattern slows after the return handball.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate beyond the defender and connect forward.

Allow Player B to choose between returning outside and continuing inside.
Reduce channel width.
Introduce controlled tackling.
Finish with a forward entry.

title: Half-Forward High-Handball Support

groundSize: A half-forward area approximately 20 metres × 18 metres.

setup:
Player A begins with the football near half-forward.
One defender stands two metres in front and may raise the arms to block a direct handball.
Player B begins behind the defender and moves laterally into a receiving lane.
Player C waits near the inside 50 line.
Player D acts as a return feeder.
The defender may not jump into the ball carrier or make contact.
Rotate all roles regularly.

Player B begins moving behind or to the side of the defender.
The defender raises the arms to remove the flat release lane.

The football travels over the defender’s hands and into Player B’s receiving area.
Player B catches in front of the body.
Player B connects with Player C near inside 50.
The defender attempts a controlled smother without leaving the marked zone.
Players rotate roles.
Repeat with the support runner moving to both sides.
coachingPoints: Use the elevated handball only when the low lane is blocked.
Maintain a legal striking action; do not scoop or throw the football.
Create enough height to clear the hands without producing an excessive loop.
The support runner should remain visible beyond the defender.
Target the receiver’s chest or front hands.
Use appropriate force for the short distance.
The receiver should continue the possession quickly.
Do not use a high handball when a direct low option is available.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier recognises the blocked lane.
Whether the disposal remains a legal handball.
Whether trajectory clears the defender without excessive height.
Whether the receiver remains visible.
Whether the football arrives in a catchable area.
Whether the next possession is completed quickly.
Whether players avoid unnecessary elevated handballs.

Move the receiver later.
Reduce the distance between defender and ball carrier.

Add a second low support option to create a live decision.

Practise trajectory into a stationary target.
successIndicators: Recognise when the high release is appropriate.
Connect quickly with the next possession.
matchApplication: Front pressure can remove a direct handball lane near half-forward. A controlled elevated handball may release a nearby teammate over the defender’s arms without requiring the ball carrier to retreat.

Maintain possession rather than forcing a low-percentage shot or boundary disposal.
Move quickly once the central angle opens.

Whether support behind is visible.
Whether the football is protected.

Whether the pattern works from both pockets.

commonErrors.error: The group slows after escaping pressure.

Allow live choice between shot, reset and inside handball.
Introduce controlled tackling.
Add a scoreboard consequence.
Require a score within three possessions.

Player A secures possession near the goal square.

Use firm, controlled handballs.
Retain possession if the safe exit lane is closed.
The final release should cross defensive 50 with support behind.

Whether players avoid backward goal-line disposals.
Whether both defensive sides are practised.

Divide the ground into four positional zones:

Midfield and centre-square line.

Position players in realistic team roles.
Begin with the football in defence.
Each zone must provide at least one short, one wide and one forward handball option.
Players follow their disposal only within their positional line during the introductory version.
Use external recovery lanes.
Begin with one active football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defensive line begins with a short angled handball exit.

A half-forward receives near the forward 50.
The half-forward releases a forward or balanced entry player.

Whether rotations preserve positional structure.

title: Positional Handball Systems Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing positional handball systems across stoppage, defence, transition and attack
objective: Assess whether players can execute their positional handball roles and connect team structure across stoppage, defensive exit, midfield transition and forward attack.
groundSize: Half to full ground with five positional assessment zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Establish five assessment phases:
Phase 1: Centre-bounce first-to-third possession chain.
Phase 2: Boundary stoppage fold-out exit.
Phase 3: Defensive intercept or goal-square escape.
Phase 4: Wing, corridor and positional transition.
Phase 5: Half-forward or forward-pocket handball connection.
Assign players to realistic positional roles.
Include controlled defenders in every phase.
Explain the technical, tactical and positional scoring criteria.
Allow one rehearsal before formal assessment.
Record individual role execution and team connection separately.
Provide planned recovery between phases.
howTheDrillWorks:
In Phase 1, midfielders complete three centre-bounce handball exits on each side.
In Phase 2, players complete three boundary-stoppage exits from each boundary.
In Phase 3, defenders complete intercept launches and pressured goal-square exits.
In Phase 4, positional lines complete wing, corridor and full-ground transition patterns.
In Phase 5, forwards and half-forwards complete pocket escapes and controlled inside 50 connections.
Coaches assess support timing, body orientation, hand selection, ball placement and movement after disposal.
Controlled defenders test each planned structure.
A turnover creates a short transition consequence before the phase resets.
Each positional group receives one strength and one priority correction.
Finish with a connected full-ground repetition incorporating all five phases.
coachingPoints: Assess role preparation before the football reaches the player.
Observe whether first, close and outside support roles are distinct.
Evaluate whether defensive disposals minimise scoreboard risk.
Record whether players hold width when required.
Assess whether corridor access is recognised rather than forced.
Include movement after disposal in every positional score.
Evaluate whether handballs lead receivers into the next phase.
Observe team reaction after turnovers.
Feedback must identify a specific positional behaviour.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether midfield roles are organised before stoppage possession.
Whether boundary exits create infield space.
Whether defenders select safe handball angles.
Whether wings and outside players maintain width.
Whether positional lines connect at useful depths.
Whether forwards create improved scoring angles.
Whether players use both hands according to field position and pressure.
Whether feedback is applied during the final connected repetition.

commonErrors.error: Players abandon positional roles and crowd possession.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce first-possession, close-support, outside and behind-ball responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Stoppage exits rely on one predictable side.
commonErrors.correction: Prepare and assess both release directions.

commonErrors.error: Defenders use dangerous central handballs near goal.
commonErrors.correction: Select angled pocket support or retain possession.

commonErrors.error: Wing players collapse inside too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the football has exited immediate pressure.

commonErrors.error: Positional lines operate as separate drills.
commonErrors.correction: Begin the next line’s movement before the previous phase finishes.

commonErrors.error: Handballs fail to lead moving receivers.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target forward space.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Move into repeat support or positional replacement.

commonErrors.error: Turnover reaction is delayed.
commonErrors.correction: Transition immediately into pressure or counterattack.

progressions: Increase defensive pressure to match-like levels.
Introduce live disposal choice between handball and kick.
Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Reduce coaching intervention between phases.
Compare positional results across later assessments.
Progress to full match simulation.
successIndicators: Protect the football and field position.
Connect stoppage, defensive, midfield and forward phases.
Use appropriate hands and release angles.
Apply positional feedback in the final repetition.
matchApplication: Effective team handballing depends on every positional line understanding how to win, support, release and connect. This assessment identifies whether individual roles combine into a complete team system under realistic field-position pressure.
relatedDrills: HB-071 – Centre Bounce First-to-Third Possession Chain

title: Disguised Handball Release
primarySkill: Disguising handball intention before releasing to an alternate target
objective: Develop the ability to use eyes, shoulders and body position to influence a defender before completing an accurate handball to a different support option.
groundSize: Stations approximately 12 metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Organise groups of four: ball carrier, defender and two receivers.
The ball carrier begins in a central three-metre release zone.
The defender starts two metres in front.
One receiver stands four metres to the left and one four metres to the right.
Receivers may move within a two-metre target area.
The defender may shuffle and attempt to intercept but may not tackle.
Rotate roles after four repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both receivers present and communicate.
The ball carrier scans both targets.
The player uses eyes, shoulder position or a partial football movement to suggest one release side.
The defender reacts towards the apparent target.
The ball carrier maintains control and reorganises towards the open receiver.
The player completes a legal handball through the newly opened lane.
The defender attempts to recover and intercept.
One point is awarded for a clean handball received beyond the defender.
The ball carrier must use both release sides during the set.
Players rotate roles after the nominated repetitions.
coachingPoints: Scan both receivers before attempting deception.
Use subtle eyes and shoulder movement rather than an exaggerated full-body fake.
Keep the football secure and close enough to reorganise.
Do not begin an illegal throwing action during the fake.
Recognise the defender’s actual movement before changing target.
Move the feet and support platform towards the final receiver.
Use a compact release before the defender recovers.
Select deception only when it creates a genuine advantage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier scans both sides.
Whether the deception influences the defender.
Whether the football remains controlled.
Whether the player reorganises the feet and platform.
Whether the final handball is legal and accurate.
Whether the defender can recover if the deception is slow.
Whether players use deception purposefully rather than automatically.

commonErrors.error: The fake is so large that the player loses balance.
commonErrors.correction: Use a smaller eye and shoulder movement while keeping the feet controlled.

commonErrors.error: The football is thrown or lifted during the deception.
commonErrors.correction: Keep it secured until the final legal handball action begins.

commonErrors.error: The player decides the final target before reading the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Watch the defender’s movement and use the option created.

commonErrors.error: The release is delayed after the defender commits.
commonErrors.correction: Reorganise immediately and use a compact strike.

commonErrors.error: The player uses only the dominant-hand side.
commonErrors.correction: Require successful deception and release to both sides.

commonErrors.error: Receivers stand still and become easy to cover.
commonErrors.correction: Move within the target area and remain visible.

progressions: Allow the defender to begin closer.
Add a third receiver behind the defender.
Reduce the release time.
Permit controlled tackling after the defender commits.
Require the ball carrier to disguise while moving.
regressions: Allow a full reset after the fake.
Practise eye and shoulder deception without defensive movement.
successIndicators: Influence the defender with controlled deception.
Complete accurate handballs to both sides.
matchApplication: Deception can shift a defender or open a narrow release lane around stoppages and congestion. Effective disguise gives the ball carrier additional time and allows support players to receive in safer space.
relatedDrills: HB-035 – Handball Square with Moving Choice

title: No-Look Support Handball Decision
primarySkill: Using pre-possession scanning to release support without prolonged visual confirmation
objective: Develop the ability to scan support before possession arrives and complete a rapid handball based on confirmed movement and communication rather than staring at the final target.
groundSize: Stations approximately 14 metres long and ten metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Organise groups of four: feeder, receiver-ball carrier and two support players.
The receiver-ball carrier begins facing the feeder.
Support players stand behind and to either side of the receiver.
Before the feed, only one support player moves into the active lane.
The receiver must scan over both shoulders before the football arrives.
One shadow defender may stand in front to restrict prolonged turning.
Rotate roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both support players begin in their starting positions.
The receiver scans over each shoulder.
One support player moves into space and calls.
The feeder delivers the football to the receiver.
The receiver secures possession while facing the feeder.
Using the earlier scan and communication, the receiver organises the football and handballs to the active support player.
The player may use a brief peripheral check but should not complete a full turn before release.
The support player catches and exits through a gate.
One point is awarded for the correct option and accurate delivery.
Rotate roles after four repetitions.
coachingPoints: Scan both shoulders before the football arrives.
Confirm the support player’s movement and voice.
Secure the football cleanly before release.
Maintain awareness of pressure in front.
Use peripheral vision rather than blindly disposing.
Select the hand aligned with the known support side.
Keep the release compact and legal.
This is an awareness drill, not permission to handball without reliable information.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver scans before the feed.
Whether the active support player communicates.
Whether the correct target is selected.
Whether the receiver uses enough visual confirmation to avoid blind disposal.
Whether the handball is accurate.
Whether front pressure remains recognised.
Whether non-dominant-side releases remain controlled.

commonErrors.error: The receiver does not scan before possession.
commonErrors.correction: The feeder must wait for two visible shoulder checks.

commonErrors.error: The player handballs blindly based only on a voice.
commonErrors.correction: Require prior visual confirmation and a brief peripheral check.

commonErrors.error: The receiver turns fully and delays release.
commonErrors.correction: Use the pre-possession scan to organise the handball sooner.

commonErrors.error: The incorrect support player is selected.
commonErrors.correction: Identify colour, position and voice before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: The handball is rushed before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Complete clean two-hand control before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players use the drill as a trick rather than an awareness task.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that reliable information must exist before release.

progressions: Add a second moving support option.
Introduce a passive interceptor.
Delay the support movement until immediately before the feed.
Require release within one second of possession.
Begin with an imperfect handball feed.
regressions: Allow the receiver to turn partially.
successIndicators: Confirm the option through communication or peripheral vision.
matchApplication: Elite players scan before receiving so they can release rapidly when pressure arrives. The skill depends on accurate prior information and communication, not on disposing without awareness.
relatedDrills: HB-035 – Handball Square with Moving Choice
HB-071 – Centre Bounce First-to-Third Possession Chain

title: Delayed Handball Draw and Release
primarySkill: Delaying a handball to fully engage a defender before releasing support
objective: Develop the ability to hold possession for the correct extra moment, draw a defender and release a supporting teammate through the space created.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 18 metres long and ten metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Two attackers begin at one end of the lane.
One attacker has the football.
A defender begins five metres ahead.
Mark an engagement line three metres before the defender.
The support runner maintains outside width.
The ball carrier may not release before crossing the engagement line.
Rotate the defender after two repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both attackers advance towards the defender.
The support runner remains level with or slightly ahead of the ball carrier.
The ball carrier crosses the engagement line while protecting the football.
The defender commits towards either attacker.
The ball carrier delays only until the defender is unable to cover both players.
The football is handballed into the support runner’s path.
The receiver accelerates through the finishing gate.
The defender attempts to recover and intercept.
Attackers score for a correctly timed release and controlled finish.
Rotate roles and repeat from both support sides.
coachingPoints: Maintain enough speed to force a defensive decision.
Keep the support runner separated and visible.
Protect the football while closing the defender.
Delay only until commitment is clear.
Avoid carrying so long that tackling pressure removes the disposal.
Release into the runner’s forward path.
Use the hand that keeps the football away from the defender.
Accelerate immediately after the handball.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier crosses the engagement line.
Whether the support runner maintains separation.
Whether the defender is genuinely drawn.
Whether the release occurs before the tackle window closes.
Whether the football leads the runner.
Whether the correct hand is selected.
Whether the ball carrier continues supporting after disposal.

commonErrors.error: The football is released before the defender commits.
commonErrors.correction: Carry across the engagement line and attack the defender’s space.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier waits too long and is closed down.
commonErrors.correction: Release as soon as the defender can no longer cover both attackers.

commonErrors.error: The support runner moves too close.
commonErrors.correction: Hold at least two metres of lateral separation.

commonErrors.error: The support player falls behind.
commonErrors.correction: Stay level with or slightly ahead of the ball carrier.

commonErrors.error: The handball goes behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target forward space.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue through as repeat support.

progressions: Permit controlled tackling.
Start the defender closer.
Add a recovering defender.
Allow the support runner to switch sides.
Require a second handball after the first defender is beaten.
regressions: Move the engagement line further from the defender.
matchApplication: A premature handball allows a defender to shift onto the receiver. Holding possession for one additional step can commit the defender and create a clean numerical advantage.

title: Four-versus-Three Handball Wave
primarySkill: Using a four-versus-three numerical advantage in transition
objective: Develop coordinated support and handball decisions that allow four attackers to use their numerical advantage against three recovering defenders.
groundSize: A transition corridor approximately 30 metres long and 18 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Four attackers begin at one end of the corridor.
Three defenders start five to seven metres ahead or in staggered recovery positions.
One attacker begins with the football.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
Attackers may use the full corridor width.
Defenders may intercept and apply shadow pressure.
A turnover creates an immediate defender counterattack towards the starting line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The four attackers begin advancing together.
Players create one inside, two outside and one behind-ball support option.
The ball carrier scans defender positions.
Attackers use handball to engage and move defenders.
The previous ball carrier repositions immediately after disposal.
Defenders communicate, close lanes and attempt interceptions.
Attackers score by carrying the football through the finishing gate.
If defenders win possession, they counterattack towards the opposite line.
The repetition ends after a score, turnover exit or football leaving the corridor.
Rotate attacking and defensive groups.
coachingPoints: Use the full width of the corridor.
Attackers should operate at different depths.
The ball carrier must engage a defender before releasing when safe.
Avoid handballing to a teammate on the same line and depth.
The player behind the football provides security and change of angle.
Move immediately after every disposal.
Accelerate when defenders become separated.
React instantly if possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers maintain width and depth.
Whether a behind-ball option remains connected.
Whether defenders are engaged before release.
Whether the handball improves the attacking position.
Whether previous ball carriers provide repeat support.
Whether attackers accelerate through defensive gaps.
Whether turnover transition is immediate.

commonErrors.error: Attackers run in a flat line.
commonErrors.correction: Create staggered short, level, forward and behind-ball options.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier releases without engaging pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Carry forward until a defender commits or a clear lane opens.

commonErrors.error: The behind-ball player becomes disconnected.
commonErrors.correction: Stay within a safe supporting handball distance.

commonErrors.error: Outside players drift centrally.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width and stretch the defensive line.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition immediately into the next support angle.

commonErrors.error: Attackers pause after turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Apply pressure or recover towards the counterattack line immediately.

progressions: Allow controlled tackling.
Narrow the corridor.
Add a fourth recovering defender after the first handball.
Limit ball carriers to two steps.
Require the attack to use both outside lanes before scoring.
regressions: Use two active defenders and one passive defender.
successIndicators: Provide support inside, outside and behind.
matchApplication: Four-versus-three situations occur during rebound and turnover transition. Effective support spacing forces defenders to make choices and allows the football to move through the resulting gap.
relatedDrills: HB-059 – Turnover Contest and Handball Counterattack
HB-083 – Delayed Handball Draw and Release

title: Corridor Risk Handball Decision
primarySkill: Evaluating risk before selecting a central handball option
objective: Develop the ability to assess whether a corridor handball provides genuine advantage or creates unacceptable turnover risk.
groundSize: A 30-metre × 25-metre area divided into outside possession lanes, a corridor and defensive turnover zone.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position the ball carrier in an outside lane.
Place one support player behind and one further along the outside lane.
Position two potential receivers in or near the corridor.
Add two defenders who may occupy or leave central lanes.
Mark a defensive scoring gate behind the ball carrier.
An intercepted corridor handball allows defenders to counterattack immediately.
Rotate all roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives in the outside lane.
Corridor receivers move to create possible handball options.
Defenders adjust their position and may bait or close the central lane.
The ball carrier scans corridor, outside and reset options.
If the central lane is genuinely open, the player handballs into the receiver’s path.
If the corridor is unsafe, the player uses outside or behind-ball support.
Attackers score by progressing through the forward gate.
Defenders score double for intercepting a corridor handball and counterattacking through the defensive gate.
Play continues for five to eight seconds after each decision.
Reset with a new ball carrier and defensive shape.
coachingPoints: Scan the defender behind and beside the corridor receiver.
Consider field position and turnover consequence.
Do not confuse a visible teammate with an open handball lane.
Use a firm corridor handball only when the receiver can continue safely.
Use outside or behind support when central risk is excessive.
The receiver must move out of the defender’s shadow.
Decisions should improve possession, not simply appear aggressive.
React immediately after interception.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier scans defender positioning.
Whether the central receiver creates a genuine lane.
Whether field position affects the decision.
Whether safer support is used when required.
Whether corridor handballs lead the receiver forward.
Whether defenders counterattack after interceptions.
Whether players learn from repeated risk outcomes.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier handballs centrally because a teammate is visible.
commonErrors.correction: Assess the defender’s interception line and the receiver’s next action.

commonErrors.error: Corridor receivers remain in defensive shadows.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally or forward to create a clear lane.

commonErrors.error: The handball floats through the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Use a firm, direct disposal or reject the option.

commonErrors.error: Players ignore support behind the football.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the reset option before forcing central possession.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier becomes excessively conservative.
commonErrors.correction: Use the corridor when the lane and receiver advantage are clear.

commonErrors.error: Attackers stop after an interception.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and defend the counterattack gate.

progressions: Reduce decision time.
Increase defensive movement.
Add a second corridor receiver.
Use field-position-specific turnover values.
Introduce controlled tackling.
regressions: Predetermine open and closed corridor scenarios.
Pause briefly to discuss the decision before restarting.
successIndicators: Use firm, accurate central handballs when appropriate.
matchApplication: Corridor handballs can open the ground but create severe turnover consequences when misjudged. Players must balance attacking opportunity with field position, pressure and interception risk.

title: Overlap or Hold Decision Game
primarySkill: Deciding whether to use an overlap handball or retain possession
objective: Develop the ability to distinguish between a productive overlap handball and a support run that should be ignored because it does not improve possession.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 20 metres long and 12 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Player A begins with the football.
Player B starts behind and prepares an overlap run.
One defender begins ahead of Player A.
A second defender starts near the overlap lane and may stay, follow or switch.
Player C waits further forward.
The ball carrier must decide whether the overlap creates advantage.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A advances towards the first defender.
Player B accelerates past through the outside lane.
The second defender reacts by following, switching or holding position.
Player A scans both defenders.
If the overlap runner is released into space, Player A handballs into the run.
If the overlap is covered, Player A retains possession, changes angle or uses Player C.
Play continues through the finishing gate.
Defenders attempt interceptions without tackling.
Attackers score for selecting the option that creates the clearest advantage.
Rotate roles and vary defensive responses.
coachingPoints: Support running does not automatically require a handball.
Read the second defender as well as the player pressuring the ball.
Use the overlap when it creates separation or breaks a line.
Retain possession when the runner is covered.
Communicate when the support player recognises the lane is closed.
Protect the football while delaying the decision.
Avoid rewarding disposal count over possession quality.
Continue forward after the selected action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether Player A scans both defenders.
Whether Player B maintains a clear overlap lane.
Whether the ball carrier uses the overlap only when advantageous.
Whether possession is retained when the lane is covered.
Whether alternate support is recognised.
Whether defenders vary their response.
Whether decisions improve across repetitions.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier handballs every time the runner passes.
commonErrors.correction: Read whether the second defender has covered the overlap.

commonErrors.error: The runner demands the football while marked.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate that the lane is closed and continue to clear space.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier focuses only on the first defender.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the defender responsible for the overlap lane.

commonErrors.error: The player holds possession after the runner becomes clearly free.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately once the overlap creates advantage.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier becomes stationary while deciding.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain balanced forward or lateral movement.

commonErrors.error: The alternate forward option is ignored.
commonErrors.correction: Scan Player C when the overlap is covered.

progressions: Allow defenders to tackle.
Add a second overlap runner.
Reduce decision time.
Introduce a kick option beyond the finishing gate.
Award defensive counterattack points after poor decisions.
regressions: Allow a coaching pause before the decision.
successIndicators: Select actions that improve field position.
matchApplication: Players must not handball simply because a teammate runs past. The disposal should be used only when the overlap creates space, draws pressure or advances possession.
relatedDrills: HB-083 – Delayed Handball Draw and Release

title: Pressure-Handball Rotation Game
primarySkill: Maintaining possession while pressure and numerical roles change continuously
objective: Develop rapid adaptation to changing attacking and defensive numbers while maintaining legal, accurate handball possession.
groundSize: A grid approximately 18 metres × 18 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into three teams of three to seven.
Two teams begin inside the grid: one attacking and one defending.
The third team waits around the boundary as neutral support.
The coach changes roles through colour or number calls.
Neutral players may receive and return one handball but may not enter initially.
Controlled tackling is permitted according to the group.
Score one point for six consecutive handballs.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins in possession.
The defending team pressures and attempts to win the football.
Boundary neutrals provide outside support.
On a coach call, one team’s role changes immediately.
A defending team may become attacking, attacking may become neutral or neutral may enter as defenders.
Players must recognise the change and reposition without stopping play.
The possession team scores after six consecutive legal handballs.
A turnover changes possession immediately.
Play continues in 60- to 90-second rounds.
Rotate the initial roles between rounds.
coachingPoints: Scan both football pressure and likely role changes.
Communicate team status immediately after the cue.
Move to new support or defensive positions without hesitation.
Keep handballs short and direct under pressure.
Protect the football before releasing.
Neutral support should create width without becoming static.
React immediately after turnovers.
Maintain legal contact and handball technique despite confusion.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise role changes.
Whether communication clarifies the new structure.
Whether attackers create immediate support.
Whether defenders apply pressure after the cue.
Whether handball technique remains legal.
Whether boundary neutrals stay available.
Whether turnover reactions are immediate.

commonErrors.error: Players stop to work out the new roles.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the call immediately and move while processing.

commonErrors.error: Former attackers continue supporting the wrong team.
commonErrors.correction: Identify team colour and new responsibility on the cue.

commonErrors.error: Neutral players remain hidden behind defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition around the boundary into clear lanes.

commonErrors.error: Handballs become speculative during role changes.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the nearest confirmed support option.

commonErrors.error: Defenders fail to pressure after entering.
commonErrors.correction: Close the ball carrier first, then cover support.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes uncontrolled during confusion.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce intensity and simplify the role-call sequence.

progressions: Increase the frequency of role changes.
Allow neutral players to enter the grid.
Reduce the grid size.
Limit ball carriers to one step.
Add scoring consequences for slow role reaction.
regressions: Use only two possible role changes.
Stop play briefly after each cue.
successIndicators: React quickly to turnovers and cues.
matchApplication: Match play changes rapidly between possession, pressure and support. Players must reorganise immediately rather than waiting for formal structure to be restored.
relatedDrills: HB-059 – Turnover Contest and Handball Counterattack

title: Fatigue Decision Handball Circuit
primarySkill: Maintaining handball decision quality under football-specific fatigue
objective: Develop the ability to preserve legal technique and select effective handball options after repeated high-intensity football efforts.
groundSize: A circuit approximately 30 metres × 20 metres with three decision stations.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Establish three connected stations:
A short acceleration and ground-ball collection.
A pressure-release decision with two support options.
A finishing transition handball to a moving target.
Players work in groups and rotate continuously.
One shadow defender operates at the decision station.
Support options vary between inside, outside and reset positions.
Work periods must be planned to protect technique.
Provide an external recovery lane.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player completes a short acceleration and collects a ground ball.
The player handballs to a feeder and immediately completes a repeat run.
The football is returned as the player enters the decision station.
Two support players move while the shadow defender closes one lane.
The player selects and completes the safest handball.
The player continues forward and receives a return handball.
A final handball is delivered to a moving target through a finishing gate.
The player exits through the recovery lane.
Complete 45- to 60-second work periods followed by planned recovery.
Stop the block if legal technique or safe movement deteriorates.
coachingPoints: Scan support before receiving at the decision station.
Maintain a stable platform despite elevated breathing and fatigue.
Do not force the first visible option.
Keep handballs firm and catchable.
Use shorter steps when balance begins to deteriorate.
Continue supporting after disposal.
Recovery between blocks must preserve skill quality.
Fatigue is a constraint, not an excuse for illegal technique.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether scanning decreases under fatigue.
Whether players default to the dominant-hand side.
Whether handball legality deteriorates.
Whether support choices remain appropriate.
Whether ball placement allows receivers to continue.
Whether running mechanics remain safe.
Whether recovery periods are sufficient.

commonErrors.error: The player chooses the first option without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Require a head movement towards both support lanes before release.

commonErrors.error: Handballs become throws late in the block.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the effort and restore technique before resuming.

commonErrors.error: The player overstrides and loses balance.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps before disposal.

commonErrors.error: The non-dominant hand is avoided.
commonErrors.correction: Position the open support option on the required side.

commonErrors.error: The player continues despite unsafe fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: End the repetition and increase recovery.

commonErrors.error: The final handball is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance and target the receiver rather than chasing speed alone.

progressions: Reduce recovery gradually.
Increase defender movement.
Add controlled contact.
Vary the final target late.
Record decision accuracy across repeated blocks.
regressions: Separate the circuit into individual stations.
matchApplication: Important handball decisions often occur after repeated running and contest efforts. Players must continue to scan, select and execute effectively when physically fatigued.

title: Scoreboard Scenario Handball Possession
primarySkill: Adapting handball risk and tempo to scoreboard and time scenarios
objective: Develop the ability to adjust handball decisions according to whether the team must retain possession, attack urgently or protect a narrow lead.
groundSize: A rectangular area approximately 35 metres × 25 metres with scoring gates at each end.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark scoring gates at each end.
Handball is the only permitted disposal.
The coach announces one of three scenarios:
Protect a one-point lead with 45 seconds remaining.
Scores level with 30 seconds remaining.
Trail by one point with 20 seconds remaining.
Controlled tackling is permitted.
The score and remaining time are displayed or called.
Restart with a different scenario after each round.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession.
Players organise support according to the announced scenario.
When protecting a lead, the possession team uses safe width, reset support and controlled tempo.
When scores are level, the team balances possession with forward opportunity.
When trailing, the team increases urgency and uses higher-value forward handball options.
The defending team attempts to force a turnover and score through the opposite gate.
The coach counts down the remaining time.
A score, turnover exit or time expiry ends the round.
Teams discuss whether their decisions matched the scenario.
Repeat with reversed possession and a new scoreboard situation.
coachingPoints: Confirm the score and time before play begins.
Communication should reflect the scenario.
Protecting possession does not mean standing still.
Use support behind and wide when protecting a lead.
Increase forward urgency when trailing without abandoning legal technique.
Understand the turnover consequence of central or speculative handballs.
Players without the football must provide scenario-appropriate support.
Review the decision process, not only the final outcome.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players understand the scenario.
Whether support shape changes appropriately.
Whether handball risk matches score and time.
Whether players communicate game-state information.
Whether technique remains legal under urgency.
Whether the team reacts appropriately after turnover.
Whether post-round reflection identifies the key decision.

commonErrors.error: Players use the same tempo in every scenario.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust possession speed and risk according to score and time.

commonErrors.error: A team protecting a lead becomes stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Keep moving to create safe short and reset options.

commonErrors.error: A trailing team panics and throws the football forward.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain legal technique and select the fastest effective option.

commonErrors.error: Players force central handballs while protecting a lead.
commonErrors.correction: Use width and support behind unless the central lane is clearly safe.

commonErrors.error: Teammates do not communicate the countdown.
commonErrors.correction: Assign players to call time and scoreboard information.

commonErrors.error: Players judge success only by whether the round was won.
commonErrors.correction: Review whether the decisions were appropriate when made.

progressions: Add kick or handball choice.
Use shorter and more complex scenarios.
Introduce boundary stoppage or defensive 50 starting positions.
Increase contact to match-like levels.
Allow the coach to change the scenario during play.
regressions: Use handball possession targets instead of scoring gates.
matchApplication: Handball decisions should change with the scoreboard, time remaining and field position. Match-aware players understand when to retain, reset, accelerate or accept greater risk.
relatedDrills: HB-059 – Turnover Contest and Handball Counterattack

title: Advanced Handball Decision Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing advanced handball deception, risk, numerical advantage and fatigue decisions
objective: Assess each player’s ability to execute technically legal handballs while making advanced decisions involving deception, defender commitment, numerical advantage, fatigue and match context.
groundSize: Five assessment stations arranged across half a ground or an area approximately 55 metres × 45 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Establish five stations:
Station 1: Disguised handball release.
Station 2: Pre-possession scan and rapid support release.
Station 3: Delayed draw-and-release against a defender.
Station 4: Four-versus-three transition wave.
Station 5: Fatigue and scoreboard decision scenario.
Assign coaches or trained observers to each station.
Record technical execution and decision quality separately.
Explain contact, scoring and workload standards.
Allow one practice repetition at each station.
Schedule recovery before the fatigue and scenario station.
Rotate players through attacking, support and defensive roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, each player completes four deceptive releases to varied targets.
At Station 2, each player completes four pre-scanned rapid releases.
At Station 3, each player performs twice as ball carrier and twice as support runner.
At Station 4, each player completes two attacking and two defensive four-versus-three waves.
At Station 5, players complete a fatigue circuit followed by one scoreboard scenario.
Observers score scanning, deception, legality, accuracy, risk selection, timing and movement after disposal.
Poor outcomes are reviewed according to the information available when the decision was made.
Unsafe contact or illegal technique ends the repetition.
Each player receives one advanced decision-making strength and one priority action.
Players repeat the station linked to their lowest decision score.
coachingPoints: Assess what the player sees before judging the disposal.
Separate successful deception from unnecessary trick play.

Whether deception creates real advantage.
Whether rapid releases are based on confirmed information.
Whether defenders are engaged before disposal.
Whether numerical support is used correctly.
Whether fatigue affects legality or accuracy.
Whether risk matches field and scoreboard context.
Whether feedback is applied during reassessment.

commonErrors.error: Deception is used when a direct handball is already open.

commonErrors.error: The player handballs without reliable visual information.

commonErrors.correction: Carry or hold possession until commitment creates advantage.

commonErrors.correction: Maintain width, staggered depth and support behind.

commonErrors.correction: Review the information and decision process at the moment of disposal.

Combine multiple decision problems within one station.
Reduce preparation and recovery time.
Add live kick-or-handball choice.
Repeat the assessment in a later training phase.
Compare decisions by field position and match scenario.

Apply feedback during the repeated station.

relatedDrills: HB-083 – Delayed Handball Draw and Release

title: Moving Disguise and Release
primarySkill: Disguising a handball while moving before releasing to an alternate support option
objective: Develop the ability to influence a defender with eyes, shoulders and running line while maintaining movement and completing an accurate handball through the space created.

setup:
Organise groups of four: ball carrier, defender and two support runners.
The ball carrier begins at one end of the lane.
The defender starts five metres ahead.
Support runners begin in separate left and right channels.
Both support runners move forward when the repetition begins.
The defender may track the ball carrier and shift towards either support option but may not tackle.
Mark a finishing gate beyond the defender.
Rotate roles after four repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier advances towards the defender with both support runners available.
The player scans both runners while maintaining forward movement.
The ball carrier uses eye direction, shoulder position or running line to suggest one handball option.
The defender reacts towards the apparent release lane.
The ball carrier adjusts the feet and supporting hand without stopping.
The player handballs into the alternate runner’s forward path.
The receiver catches and carries through the finishing gate.
The unused support runner continues moving to remain available.
The defender scores by intercepting or forcing an inaccurate disposal.
Rotate roles and require releases to both sides.
coachingPoints: Maintain running balance while applying deception.
Scan both support runners before engaging the defender.
Use subtle eyes and shoulder movement rather than an exaggerated fake.
Keep the football protected and under control.
Read the defender’s actual reaction before changing the release.
Reorganise the supporting hand early.
Use a compact legal strike before the defender recovers.
Lead the receiver forward rather than handballing at their body.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player scans both support options.
Whether the deception affects the defender.
Whether movement continues throughout the action.
Whether the football remains protected.
Whether the player changes the supporting and striking hands efficiently.
Whether the final disposal is accurate and legal.
Whether the receiver maintains forward speed.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier stops to perform the deception.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce running speed and maintain continuous forward movement.

commonErrors.error: The handball goes behind the support runner.

Start the defender closer.
Delay support-runner movement.
Add a third support option behind the football.
Require a second handball after the first defender is beaten.

title: Receiver-Protection Handball Placement

howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver presents and begins moving forward.
The pressure player establishes position on one side of the receiver.
The handballer scans the pressure relationship.
The player delivers the football towards the receiver’s protected hand and body side.

coachingPoints: Look at the receiver’s pressure, not only the receiver’s hands.
Place the football away from the opponent.
Use the striking hand that provides the clearest protected-side delivery.
Avoid forcing the receiver to reach across the body.
Lead the receiver slightly forward when space permits.
Use firm, catchable ball flight.
The receiver should present the protected hand clearly.
Judge success by the receiver’s next action, not only whether the football is caught.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the handballer recognises the pressure side.
Whether the disposal reaches the receiver’s protected side.
Whether the receiver can continue forward.
Whether the football forces the receiver to turn into pressure.
Whether the correct hand and trajectory are selected.
Whether communication clarifies the safe side.
Whether placement remains accurate at increased speed.

commonErrors.error: The handball is delivered to the pressure side.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the defender’s position and target the opposite hand.

commonErrors.correction: Place it outside the receiver’s protected shoulder.

commonErrors.error: The receiver does not show the protected hand.

Delay the pressure player’s side selection.

title: Late-Arriving Support Decision
primarySkill: Recognising and releasing a support player who arrives late into space
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession briefly, recognise a late-arriving support option and release accurately without overholding the football.
groundSize: A grid approximately 16 metres × 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Player A begins with the football in the central zone.
One defender starts two metres away and applies shadow pressure.
Player B provides an early short option.
Player C starts behind the play and becomes a late-arriving runner.
Player D waits beyond the finishing gate.

howTheDrillWorks:
Player A receives possession under shadow pressure.
Player B presents as the immediate option.
The defender positions to discourage or close Player B.

Player A protects the football and continues scanning.

The defender attempts to close the late lane without tackling.
Rotate roles and vary which support option becomes available.
coachingPoints: Scan continuously rather than locking onto the first option.
Protect the football while waiting for support to develop.
Do not reject a clearly open early option merely to complete the drill pattern.
Recognise the late runner’s speed and lane.
Release as soon as the support player becomes the best option.
Avoid holding until the defender reaches tackling distance.
Use the hand aligned with the late-arriving lane.
Support runners should communicate as they enter space.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier scans after the first option is presented.
Whether possession is protected while waiting.
Whether the player recognises the late runner.
Whether an open early option is used appropriately.
Whether the handball leads the runner.
Whether release timing avoids unnecessary pressure.
Whether support communication is effective.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier automatically uses the first option.
commonErrors.correction: Scan again and compare the early and late support lanes.

commonErrors.error: The player ignores a clearly open early option.
commonErrors.correction: Use the best available option rather than forcing the late pattern.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier waits until pressure fully closes.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately when the late runner enters the open lane.

commonErrors.error: The handball travels behind the late runner.

commonErrors.error: The football is exposed while the player waits.

progressions: Allow the defender to tackle.
Add a second late runner.

title: Defender-Switch Exploitation Handball

coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Two attackers begin at one end of the lane.
The ball carrier starts inside and the support runner outside.
Two defenders begin five metres ahead in corresponding lanes.

Defenders attempt interceptions without tackling.
Attackers score for identifying and exploiting the genuine defensive error.

The support runner must change lanes with speed and purpose.
Communicate the crossing movement early.
Release only if the switch creates separation.
Place the football into the runner’s new path.
Retain possession when the defensive switch is completed effectively.
Avoid running the support player into the ball carrier’s lane.
Continue supporting after the decision.

Whether the support runner changes lanes effectively.

Whether the ball carrier scans both opponents.
Whether the handover gap is recognised.

Add a third attacker.

Increase defender communication and recovery.
Add a turnover counterattack.

title: Trap-Side Handball Escape

Three attackers begin inside the channel.
Two defenders position to trap the ball carrier against one side.
One attacker provides close support and one provides a reset or opposite-side option.
Mark a near-side exit gate and an opposite-side escape gate.
Defenders may tackle under controlled rules.
The coach determines which side the trap begins on.

The coach feeds the football to an attacker near one side of the channel.

The third attacker moves behind or across to create the alternate escape angle.

The repetition ends after an exit, turnover or football leaving the area.
Rotate roles and begin traps from both sides.

Do not force a handball through the trap.
Protect the football and use support behind or across.
Close support should not remain in the same pressure pocket.
The alternate player must create width on the far side.
Use firm, short handballs to shift the angle.
Accelerate once possession escapes the trap.
React immediately if the football is turned over.

Whether the ball carrier recognises the trap.
Whether possession is protected.
Whether support creates different angles.
Whether attackers avoid crowding the pressure pocket.
Whether the handball chain shifts the football away from pressure.
Whether the exit player accelerates.
Whether turnover reaction is immediate.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier forces the forward lane.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession and use support behind or across.

Three attackers begin inside the grid against four defenders.
Two additional attackers wait outside separate reinforcement gates.
The possession team begins with the football.

Controlled tackling is permitted.
One exit gate is marked at the far end.

The attacking team begins in possession while outnumbered.

The possession team recognises the new numerical balance and attacks the exit.

The repetition ends after a successful exit, turnover score or football leaving the grid.
Rotate teams and reinforcement players.
Vary the reinforcement timing between repetitions.
coachingPoints: Recognise that retaining possession may be the best initial outcome.
Use width and support behind the football.
Avoid handballing to a teammate surrounded by defenders.
Protect the football and remain composed.
Continue moving to make defenders work.
Identify the moment reinforcement enters.
Change from retention to attack quickly when numbers improve.
Communicate the new support option.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers recognise the numerical deficit.
Whether support remains available behind and laterally.
Whether risky forward handballs are avoided.
Whether ball carriers protect possession.
